Okay so, first off - this game has been getting a supreme amount of hate. Yes the Uplay thing is annoying and the in game store is unnecessary, and yes, launching a DLC with the game is a weak move. Well I just finished the game and I have to call out all the haters who said they loved Stick of Truth but hated this game. TFBW is Stick of Truth + - it has everything that made that game great, and more. Yes it recycles several elements, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. I plays similarly to the first game with a couple of major improvements - the combat system is more strategic for one. Think the first game plus Final Fanatsy Tactics. There are classes to deal with and you can actually spec your character in a few different ways.   Stick of Truth was very much a game for South Park superfans and the sequel is the same exact approach. There are great call backs to the last few seasons of the show. Whereas the first game had about 15 seasons to work with, this one is more centered on the last 5 or so. The boss battles are challenging and there is a puzzle element to it that actually made me think a few times.  Last good point - it's bigger than the first. More playable characters, more special moves, and more shit to collect. If you didn't like Stick of Truth, or generally hate South Park, then obviously don't bother with this game. Otherwise, get it and love it.  $60 felt pricey, but I was too excited to wait for a sale.

A great take on the Dungeon Delving Genre, to say the very least, the game is well built, the mechanics run fluidly, and you can actually see yourself learning the enemies and getting better simply at playing it in general  Pros and Cons  Some Pros 1. Every single line of dialogue is interacting and basing themselves on what's happened previously, and every single one is 100% Voice Acted 2. It's Consistent, the game does what it says it'll do and a lot of failures when playing or seeing others play seems to stem from Panic and lack of practice 3. You can see exactly what your going to get for each room you clear, at the end of a room you choose between 1-2 doors, and they show you exactly what you'll get, once you recognize the symbols, they also warn you if the enemies within will be of a harder difficulty, from simply tougher enemies, to complete minibosses  Some Cons 1. To say the least, it is a LONG GAME, played for 21 Hours at time of writing, and i've only finished 10 Escape Attempts, it's fast paced but don't expect to be grinding multiple runs in hours 2. Builds are not consistent, you have to be good at changing your play style, you have choices of weapons before you start and each one is unique in how it fights, from the Classic Sword OR Bow, to nothing but a Shield, or possibly a spear that returns when thrown, and you can only bring one of these weapons with you for your escape attempt. Building off of this, your never going to get the same build, both the Gods and Unique Weapon upgrades have MANY options to choose from and it'll only show 3 of them for you to choose 1 of.  Some Tips  1. Keep an eye on what upgrades you have, you can look over them at any time you want, You want to do this so that you don't get confused and start mixing up your current build, with previous builds you remember, again, YOU WILL NEVER HAVE THE SAME BUILD  2. Remember to use your Cast: at the start, it's weak and does little else, but extra damage is extra damage and later Perm. Upgrades will allow you to deal extra damage or slow down enemies that have your cast within them at that time which makes them even easier to slaughter, [i]though some upgrades will prevent your cast from possessing enemies at all, but those are usually the stronger casts anyways, looking at you Ares[/i]  3. A VERY Important thing personally, Do NOT Spam your Dashes, they recharge in less than a second but you need to pay attention where AND when your dashing, mid dash, you'll avoid any attacks well enough, but there is a subtle, barely a second, where your a bit slower and can't dash again which can cause a bit of trouble if your getting swarmed, beyond that, some upgrades focus on Dashing specifically when your about to be hit, so you have to pay attention  4. Gods Upgrades will each have a Unique Effect and are found only with that god, Artemis Grants Crit. Hit Chances, Athena can allow you to deflect attacks and projectiles, Zeus helps summon lighting, so on so forth, and each of these can be upgraded, BUT, when upgrading, you only get to choose 1 of 3 Random Boons from whatever you have, so if you want to specifically upgrade something, you have better odds if you have a small selection of powerful upgrades rather than a wide boasting range of abilities  5. You do have a degree of control over your playstyle, Permanent Upgrades after you die will slightly help you upgrade yourself, increasing damage, allowing you to survive death once with half health per Run, and letting you damage enemies who you've Cast at, and later, you get the choice of fluidly changing each possibility to a similar but wholely different alternative, which is upgraded seperatly, Ex. Ugrade to Increase Max Casts, Changes to allowing 1 Cast only, but it's on a cooldown instead of needing to be collected.  Finally Summarizing  It's a Hard Game, it's a Long game, but it's very fun, VERY well built, and it's extremely consistent with keeping everything knitted together, keeping a level head will suffice, and while it will throw challenges after you to shake up what you thought was consistent on occasion . . . well, it's not like you can die FOREVER in Hell, Right?

My name is Commander Shepard and this is my favourite game on the Citadel. My love for this game cannot be described. Starting off on X-Box 360 I fell in love, playing the 3rd game first lmao.  Choosing your background actually comes into play for the story as people will view Shep differently based on if you're a war hero or ruthless, spacer or colonist, if you're adept or a solider, etc. In ME1 you also get background specific quests as well. I like for a spacer mumma Shep in ME1 is a well known Executive Officer (Admiral ME2 / Rear Admiral ME3) in the Alliance and makes a few appearances through email or interviews. So I would recommend trying out a few different paths in different playthroughs.  Also want to add that renegade Shep is such a d*ck lol, so if you want to play as a ren Shep I'd say be a ruthless war hero. The Legendary Edition is such an improvement from the original games, ME1 is more enjoyable with the change in UI and the HUD. As well as having all the DLCs (apart from Pinnical Station for ME1 thanks to the DLC file being corrupted so the devs couldn't add it), the graphics getting some love and for $100 NZD (when not on sale) is just amazing, I can't explain how much money I spent originally on PS3 for all of them. It is extremely worth the price. Trust me when I say you will enjoy the Citadel DLC in ME3. It grabs you away from the war and puts you in an amazing side story filled with a decent plot twist ending, inside ME jokes, jokes in general, heartwarming moments, extra scenes for romanced characters, closer for a character (not going to spoil it), one night stand with the amazing James Vega ;) and guns, many guns. OH and having to press the mouse button 183 fricken times taking around 15 minutes to beat Vega's pull up record, no it doesn't actually affect your rep even though it gives prompts. You can tell the team put a lot of work into this DLC, there is so much love in this DLC. Yes it is short if you race through, but it's one where once you finish the story line it doesn't kick you out. You can go back to Anderson's I mean your apartment at any point, expect from when you go to Cerberus HQ (which is basically no return). Down side is that for ME3 they got rid of the Multiplayer aspect to it, I enjoyed it on PS3 but I'm glad they got rid of it based on the amount of people that hated that it was a compulsory thing if you wanted the best war score and HAD to play it so the score wouldn't go down. But otherwise no other complaints. If you love Sci-Fi RPGs where putting in effort with side content actually matters, then you'll love this game. 100% the game takes about 120ish hours to complete so you won't be short on content. Kafasını çevirdiğinde yüzü kanlar içinde olan adama tarikat şövalyeleri saldırmaya başlar ancak adam hepsinin sanki kağıt kesiyormuş gibi keser. Nero da bu adama saldırmaya başlar. Ardından Nero bu adamı yakalamak ve yaptıklarının bedelini ödetmek için adanın derinliklerine doğru yolculuğa çıkar.  !!!BURADA SPOİLER VERECEĞİM NE KADAR TAKARSINIZ BİLMEM AMA BEN UYARIMI YAPIYORUM!!! Esse jogo me surpreendeu desde seu anúncio de lançamento, uma vez que eu nunca havia visto uma tentativa de refazer um soulslike de uma maneira tão cômica, não joguei por muito tempo, todavia posso dizer que o jogo está maravilhoso para quem é fã da série Souls, tendo seus prós e seus contras.   PRÓS  - O jogo está muito divertido com o  mecanismo de desvio e combate literalmente igual ao de jogos da séries souls, sendo assim se tornando bem tranquilo pra quem é veterano, além de ser bem amigável a novos jogadores - O modo coop está bem diferente do que eu estava esperando, já que é possível jogar com um amigo compartilhando os pixels (tem a mesma utilidade que as almas do dark souls), além de permitir que o convidado também resgate itens para seu próprio personagem levando a uma progressão conjunta dos personagens e da história - Tem uma boa quantidade de armamentos e armaduras para se utilizar - Mapa grande com desing muito bem feito, possuindo atalhos que podem ser utilizados para encurtar o tamanho do mesmo  - O level desing é muito bom, te fazendo observar a beleza dos locais em certos momentos - Customização inovadora do personagem, diga-se de passagem :D  CONTRAS  - Infelizmente nem tudo são flores, esse primeiro ponto se leva a uma questão do próprio combate, já que sem pré que você leva dano seu personagem fica parado por alguns segundos não te possibilitando esquivar, e isso é um pouco chato, já que se vc estiver lutando contra um grupo de inimigos a sua vida vai ser reduzida em um nível significativo  - Por mais que exista uma boa variedade de armas as únicas diferenças que existem entre elas é a velocidade e o dano que cada uma da, umas batendo bem mais rápido que outras, todavia dando menos dano - O cooperativo também apresenta alguns problemas que vão desde a conexão entre os playes até umas situações um pouco chatas, já que o jogo cooperativo te permite jogar o game inteiro com um amigo, ou seja se vc derrotou um boss junto com seu ambos permaneceram na mesma sala, não tendo a desconexão forçada que existe, por exemplo em dark souls, todavia para chamar um amigo é necessário utilizar um item e colocar um código com quatro números, só que sempre que você ou seu amigo morrerem a desconexão forçada acontece, sendo necessário repetir todo o processo de novo (e leva um tempo desde caçar o item no inventário, pegar o código e invoca-lo), não é um ponto contra que afeta o jogo negativamente, todavia é um processo chato que poderia ter sido evitado apenas colocando uma opção após a tela de morte perguntando se ambos os jogadores querem continuar juntos no mesmo mundo. - A variedade de inimigos também se apresenta como uma questão meio chata, uma vez que muitos inimigos só possuem um desing diferente, porém os golpes são iguais.  Considerações Finais The Last Hero é um jogo muito bom, claro que ele peca em certos aspectos assim como todo jogo em época de lançamento, e tem seus pequenos defeitos que podem ser facilmente concertado e retrabalhados, contudo o jogo é uma carta para os fans de soulslike e de jogos em geral brincando com o mundo dos jogos enquanto você explora um mundo destruído, podendo ser com um amigo ou não, vale muito apena joga lo para experimentar um estilo de jogo com um aspecto mais diferenciado, que n se prende muito a seriedade e conseguindo fazer com que o jogador seja desafiado em cada local que se encontra. After about 3 weeks I've been using this along with a wired logitech pro device that I've had since...oh the ps2 days. I got it because I didn't want to mice and keyboard my way through Hitman. Anyway, to best describe the controller is that it's not weird, but different. Yes, this controller is different and for some that could either be a good thing, or a bad thing.   I have small hands, but generally a lot of people still say the controller is big. Yes, that is true, but I thought it was comfortable. It's thick and it does have some weight on it. The biggest complaint is finding the buttons. When I first purchased it, the store guy said that he confuses the X and A buttons with the Y and B buttons. It does happen, but that has to do with 2 reasons: 1.The size of the controller and 2. just getting used to the control scheme. It's funny, because that was the biggest complaint from the store guy the control scheme. Not the weight, or what I think is the biggest issue (I'll get to that in a moment). The more I used it, I got more comfortable with the buttons. I actually like the toggles underneath because I don't feel that they are gimmicky and in fact,  I actually see those being used in console devices. What does feel weird is the right touchpad. Taking the place of a traditional right stick, the right pad is clickable on the edges and you can add haptic feedback so it gives you a sense a touch when touching the edges. The left pad is similar so if you want to touch the controls as opposed to pressing them you can.   But, my huge issue with this pad is the fact that it's a controller with a very high learning curve. Good luck finding ways to program this thing. It's been over 6 months since it's release and I still can't find a way to properly program this thing. It's flexible, and that is a good thing, but no instructions mean that programming it to find a sweet spot is hit or miss. The community does offer settings you can download and use to serve as default controls, for most games, but it's hit or miss. And that's a shame because unless a developer submits a default control scheme you're not sure what to really expect. Sometimes the community gives you something that gives you a better, while other times you have to jump back and forth in your game trying to get comfortable finding just the feel. Most of the issues stem from the amount of feedback you want from the mouse pad regions of both the left and right pads. For some it's a matter of getting used to it, for others that need buttons or a stick, you're not going to enjoy the experience as much.   Now saying all that...I love this controller! I have yet to test this out on fighting games, but for adventure, platform, third person and fps games, this controller is great. The ability to program keyboard inputs into your controller without the use of mods or patches is a godsend. The weight of the device doesn't hamper me at all. The ability to adjust the speed of the right pad gives me the ability to line up shots easier if I want to go slow, or if I want to make it faster I can (I realize I just complained about the right pad, but the issue was the learning curve). The bumpers underneath are not gimmicky as much as they are useful. Perhaps the most exciting thing I like about it is that I'm no longer stuck using keyboard and mouse controls. I can now purchase older games that were built for kb+m controls and map them directly to a controller. It's not perfect because I can't find a control scheme that I like, but I no longer have to find alternatives.   Overall, I would recommend this controller for those that don't want to use a kb+m and don't have or want an xbox 360 or One controller. If you got one of those keep them and use them. Most games read those inputs anyway. But, if you don't want one of those controllers, and don't mind tinkering with the controls for the first 30 minutes of your game, than I think you would like this controller.

It's okay. If you're kind of expecting technomancy fallout, this isn't it.   Pros: It looks good It plays good - it's a very smooth isometric feel. The mapping isn't the best though, and more than once I've wondered why I was in combat when all I neede to do was move to the next area. Its stable - no crashes, no bugs that I noticed.   Cons Its short. 5.8 hrs and I've already beaten main antagonist number 1. And now there's a mystery second antagonist because oh no, we've only got 6 hours of content.  It's linear - Wow. No side quests, no interesting lore, no interesting characters just to talk to. It's the opposite of Skyrim. It's very cliched (it's like your otaku friend vomited all the cool japanese words he knew into this game somewhere). The RPG elements aren't quite there It's not really an RPG - The item/armour choices are ridiculous. I bought armour in the first 20 minutes of the game, and haven't changed it since, as I was never offered better options. Same with guns. The spells aren't that interesting, they seem to be heavily geared towards support magic (reducing enemy armour, etc) so any mages I have are usually spamming one or two spells all the time. They're pretty though. It's not written very well - It's okay, but again, it's cliched. You're gonna roll your eyes a bit, and you never really do get too invested in the characters. You get maybe one or two side missions with each character, maybe, and then not even so much as an option to converse in hub worlds.  It's repetitive - I'm probably not going to play the main campaign again, ever.  Most of the enjoyable content of this game will be made by players, not devs. I feel like the devs gave us an amazing tool to craft isometric stories, but that it's not really their job to build a sprawling fallout-esque world. Maybe it isn't. But I'm glad I didn't pay full price for it, then.   In short, it looks nice but there's no life to this world. Skip it, or pick it up at bargain bin prices, and get some of the player made content. Or buy Fallout 1 or 2.

I do love this game. It has a good interesting idea. The aliens all play and feel different, Marine's guns and exos are fun as hell. The problems with this game are not in the game itself, but with the fanbase. This game suffers from tryhard like players. Often times you wont even notice a problem, but because the enemy is holding that one little point, or you lost one of your 3 bases, they are ready to just give up. Not all servers are like this, but they rarely name or say at any point if that server is gonna be tryhardish. I would give this game a 8-9/10. The fanbase I would give it a 5/10. It brings the whole game down when players are more willing to give up and start over rather than coming up with plans to win. Often times games go back and forth when people dont give up instantly something goes wrong. The commander may have a overview of the situation but they almost never put faith in their teamates to push back.  I am recommending this game to players who like FPSes with fun twists or people who liked AVP2. but you should really be careful about the servers you play on.

Wow this latest update rocks, the physics is almost perfect now, i do the same errors i usually do on the real table. i had purchased paddle up and ping pong vr too and before this update paddle up had the best physics. In paddle up on its side it's easier to do curved shots, but i've just seen in the options they have added a couple of fader to tune the paddle speed and spin, nice. Multiplayer is ok and it looks it handle latency a bit better than paddle up, i have played with a 100ms ping opponent and it was somewhat playable, obviously not perfect but there's not much they can do with that latency, anything above 40 ms produces visible latency and probably going over 100ms gives unexpected behaviours, the key is how they handle it.  EDIT: Played again with a 95 ms opponent in california (i'm in italy) the match was very smooth to be honest, i didn't expected so much quality with a so far connection. i've lost a couple of points where i was sure i did it right, but we played several matches and the overall experience was great.  So for the guys that have problems with multiplayer they have probably packet loss due to other factors, like other people using the connection, other programs inside the computer using bandwidth, a low or disturbed wifi signal in case of wifi, or some nodes over the net that have problems (saturated dslam or node for example), if connections are smooth, game is smooth.  Remember to serve FAR from the table, if you serve over the table you will lose the point ( i think it's a real table tennis rule)

Short version: 10/10 recommend  A classic finally available on Steam! OpenTTD is easy to learn and rewarding to master: there's plenty of tutorials both written and recorded online to teach you the basics of railways layouts and signals, and from there it's up to you to embark upon the addictive journey of blessing a sleepy, stagnant province with your transportation empire! The basic premise (move resource from A to B, profit, repeat) conceals significant depth: resource transfers, stations serving multiple modes of transport, complex railway networks allowing dozens if not hundreds of different trains to run on the same tracks without interruption etc. If games like Factorio give you the itch for optimising and automating resource flows, OpenTTD is definitely the experience for you. Don't let my steam hours fool you: I've played this game for hundreds of hours prior to its arrival at this platform!  Don't be put off by the basic graphics! Not only does OpenTTD bless you with fun gameplay for a tiny download, it can also be expanded and enhanced through the use of NewGRFs. These downloadable packages - essentially mini-mods - add new vehicles, buildings, resources, graphics and more, allowing you to broaden the default 1950-2050 setting into anything from horse-and-buggy networks, enhanced modern transportation or even a colony on Mars, all with a few clicks.  But you don't have to go it alone! There's internet servers for a global multiplayer experience, plus LAN options for playing with your friends. Co-operate to build a single massive empire or compete for the greatest profits - the choice is yours.  And the best bit? It's all FREE. Why are you even reading this? I don't have to convince you to risk money on it, go try it yourself! It costs you NOTHING, and it might just be the most addictive, charismatic game you've played in a while. Full respect to all of the developers, bug-fixers and modders for maintaining and enhancing this project, creating a complete, timeless experience that just works.  So if you're open to an eye-opening open-sandbox experience, open OpenTTD and open up a world of possibilities today!

Steam is full of hidden object adventure games - this one is competing right at the top.  Reason for that is because pacing is just right in this game. As soon as the map becomes available early on the game moves on like it's on rails. Sometimes you have a large list of objectives to fulfill and sometimes it slows down and forces you to calm down and catch up on your bearings/read some journal entries - but you are never completely stuck.   Handy map shows where there are actions to do - a very essential tool since the map is also a time machine and you are constantly jumping from one time point to another while still staying in the same areas.  Without it the game would be quite frustrating as 'green cloud' object puzzles appear in different time points and places most of the time without any logical reason so locating them on the map is essential.   I did not complete the most demanding achievements but i must say i was tempted to really play the game cleanly and not use any hints or random clicks as the puzzles were very challenging.   All in all money and time well spent with this title. Perfect for quick 15min+ game sessions where you must also stress your brain a bit. Some puzzles are plain devilish in the way it hides item in the picture.

So I see a lot of criticism that in my opinion is very weak, here's my take on the game:  ObsCure 2 is a solid PS2 title. The combat is smooth, you can change weapons on input, manage your inventory, etc. The graphics are great for the time, and some areas of the game still look good today. The story, albeit lackluster and campy, is cohesive enough to follow. The level design, linear or not, keeps you on edge and guessing what's going to happen next. The scares had me terrified as a kid and still sometimes get the jump on me today. The gameplay rewards you for exploration, and is difficult enough for you to have to scrounge as much ammo as you can because you keep running out of it.  Of course, the game is not perfect if you compare it to the first game. But on its own retrospect it's a solid horror title and offers a lot of replayability through gameplay alone.   Is it worth the buy? If you enjoy older games and can stomach old game design, definitely.  7.5/10

I have an undying love for horrors of all formats. My current passion is audio creepypastas [i](Mr. Creeps, CreepsMcPasta, The Dark Somnium, RomNex; you know, the good stuff)[/i] and occasionally video ones [i](Strawberry Nightmare is particularly good)[/i]. So, when I saw a copy of Scarlet Hollow on my curator group, I immediately dug my nails into it. That is my cup of tea here, baby!  https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2523510760  [h1]Ready For An Adventure?[/h1]  There are a lot of things that I can (and will) praise the game for. Let me explain them step by step.  First comes the most important part – [b][u]the writing[/u][/b]. If the story is poorly presented, hardly anything can save it. Audio tales prove it really well and visual ones are not far behind. Currently, Scarlet Hollow offers only two episodes out of seven (which explains the Early Access status), but it is already oblivious how good everything is written. Descriptions are vivid, story flow is smooth and has a good build-up before any scary events while also not dragging out for too long, and characters have interesting personalities.   Another interesting point is the [b][u]good variety of choices[/u][/b]. Not only ones that just add some flavor to the text, but also really major options that lead to different outcomes and occasional…victims. Also, at the beginning of the game you must choose two personality traits that will add special phrases to almost each situation. Some of them can help you uncover extra information, others are more for roleplaying, but it is still interesting to see how your character can change in many scenes. My personal recommendation is the Talk To Animals trait – trust me, it will bring a lot of extra funny moments.   And for all of you, paranormal aficionados, I bring good news: Scarlet Hollow also explores various [b][u]Appalachian myths and cryptids[/u][/b] – ever heard of a skunk ape? Or a cursed cat-like creature that might or might not have been a beautiful woman before? Or maybe tommyknockers tickle your fancy? There are a lot of unique animals and humanoids that you might have never heard before but will die to find out more about now.   https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2523521462  [b][u]The setting and atmosphere[/u][/b]. Ooooh, the aesthetics of this game! Hit me right in the kokoro [i](I should really stop hanging around manga and manhwa websites so much…)[/i]. This visual novel has some curious tricks up its sleeve. [b][u]The art style[/u][/b] is quite unusual – you might need some time to get used to it [i](just…when you see the cousin’s “smile”…you will understand; it is a horror of its own)[/i]. But it works really well with scary scenes. Creates a very unsettling pressure that follows you through the whole game. Locations feel authentic and have lots of neat details, specifically horror ones. And the overall range of colors – dark, murky whites, blacks, greys and yellows – bring this heavy feeling of wrongness, foreboding disaster.  The atmosphere is oppressing and creepy, but also devilishly alluring. After all, who does not like investigating a mystery of a scary little town in the middle of nowhere?  [b][u]The music[/u][/b]. Comes last on this list but is definitely one of the most important features in the whole game. It. Is. Gorgeous. In absolutely all aspects – from just normal sounds of the forest to truly creepy tunes during dynamic confrontations. To be honest, half of events in the game would not have nearly the same impact without these incredible tracks.    [h1]Something Bad, Maybe?[/h1]  Hmmmm…To be honest, this visual novel is one of the rare cases when I have literally nothing to complain about – except for the fact that it is in Early Access and I all have to wait for who-knows-how-long to finally find out how the story ends. Oh, and I caught a coding issue at one point of the second chapter. But really, that is all.   https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2524211923  [h1]The Hunt Has Started[/h1]  Scarlet Hollow has one very important feature that not all horror games boast – replayability. From the great selection of choices and personality traits’ combos to various outcomes – some of which will haunt you for a long time. Will you try to save everyone or just look out for yourself? Can you actually change the fate of this small mining town? Or are you doomed to go down with it and die at the hand of yet another supernatural creature? Oh, and by the way, do you think you can trust anybody here? Well, we will see…  If you have not understood yet, I cannot recommend this game enough. It is a bit short right now and yes, Early Access status can scare people away. Some of us also just really hate waiting. I get it, really. But trust me, Scarlet Hollow is definitely a game to look out for. Or even better – to buy and enjoy. I am extremely curious about where the story will go next and how the authors will be able to connect all events together. All I can say for now is that there is already basis for a great horror title. 优秀的竞技FPS。拟真？什么拟真？你见哪个拟真游戏连标尺都不能调？ 总的来说像地图大点的红管，步兵体验有时还不如红管，但优点还是很多的、  ·真实的倒地机制，一旦被爆头或炸碎那就一命呜呼了。[spoiler] 不像某个酒精绷带妙手回春的现代战争游戏 [/spoiler]  ·单兵智能弹药管理系统。类COD的弹药机制让你放心换弹而绝不会浪费一发子弹。时时刻刻都可以掏出压满的弹夹和对面激情火并。  ·40亿支产量的STG44，你可以在这游戏里到处看到这把二战名枪。但显然第三帝国为了产量而放弃了质量，现在它的后坐力和绍莎一样大了。  ·二战暖暖，琳琅满目的头盔和衣服任你选择。穿上夏季迷彩和布罩M42胖揍穿制式军服的萌新。当然这也意味着你可以在6月的法国北岸看到穿冬季大衣的德美士兵。 [spoiler] 但有一说一，自定义服装确实是我喜欢玩这游戏的主要原因 [/spoiler]  ·优秀的团队配合。你的队员或队长总有100种不开麦的理由。  ·真实的驾驶机制。你在驾驶坦克时甚至要挂挡！[spoiler] 老是在这些莫名其妙的地方做的过分拟真 [/spoiler] 虽然凝聚德意志科技结晶的欧宝是自动档[spoiler] 自动换档，不用你手动切 [/spoiler]，但你还是要等那个小儿麻痹把方向盘打死了才能转过向。  ·振金打造的负重轮，或许V2的直接命中也不能将其摧毁。等东线出了也不用担心时速200迈的BT，战车的履带会忠实的履行它的职责直到最后一刻。当然，如果你是队伍中的反坦克手就要小心了，优秀的坦克驾驶员会用负重轮和履带抵挡来袭的火箭弹。  ·44年的雅利安低能儿和美利坚乡巴佬。即使你可以按住shift无限奔跑，但你冲刺起来的速度仍像郊游一样。而这群废物们甚至没办法跨过一面比他们头还低一点的矮墙。  ·莫名其妙的空气墙。在400高地挑战你的血压极限。  ·令人发指的服务器质量。大部分CN服务器在使用加速器的情况下都有100+的pings。   如果你能忍受以上要素，那这游戏绝对适合你。如果你还有三两成群的沙雕网友，那这游戏一定会成为你的快乐源泉。

Игра неплохая, геймплея маловато, чувствуется сырой, как и большинство игр которые издает PlayWay. Конечно дает простор для различных триксов, перелетание за заборы, например. Однако на деле, не все так гладко и игра ощущается слегка топорно и дёргано.    Минусы:  -За всю игру не нашел возможности сменить кредитопомойку на которой катается главный герой. Нет возможности положить плазму на плазму. В багажнике куча места, но увозить ты будешь только один принтер. Хотелось бы видеть фургон, пикап. Что-то, куда влезает больше крупногабаритного хлама.  -Крупногабаритный хлам в поздней стадии игры не нужен. Прохожие постоянно снуют вперёд-назад вокруг дома который ты грабишь, никуда не уходя, будто это агенты тайной военной полиции. Зачем нужна картина за 2к$, если самые дорогие плюшки, например большинство антиквариата, смартфоны, спокойно можно раскидать по карманам и пойти домой пешком.  -Залезаю на глазах полицейских в урну, они некоторое время даже стоят около неё. Но достать не могут, брезгуют.  -Никакой реиграбельности. После тринадцати часов игры просто нечего делать, вынес все что можно.   -Вор ходит без маски, нет возможности ее надеть перед ограблением. Представьте, к вам в дом заходит лысый мужик, разбивает любимый сервиз и окно на втором этаже, после чего забирает картину и галопом убегает за город, злобно посмотрев перед этим вам в лицо. И все нормально. Никто его не найдет, потому что он лысый и был в чёрном. Никаких зацепок.  -Низкоуровневые отмычки не нужны. После получения автоматической, нужно сделать возможность не париться с тупыми замками, принцип действия которых ничем не отличается.   -CMS 2018 внутри игры про вора, еще и кривой. Разбор автомобилей явно лишняя часть в этой игре, судя по тому, что в ломбарде детали стоят 0$ и кроме как на BlackBay их продать негде, еще и недопилено.   -Пешеход с улицы может увидеть через окно, под диким углом, сквозь шторы, как кто-то взламывает сейф внутри дома и вызвать полицию.  -С такой физикой движения, не хватает прыжков.  -Нет серьёзных ограблений, ты только домушник и всё.  -Человеческий трафик ночью ничуть не уменьшается.   Плюсы:  +Игра весёлая.   +Главный герой - лысый Ваня.  +Постоянные обновления ( непонятно, допиливают игру и добавляют геймплей, или просто фиксят баги )  +Есть где размахнуться, в пределах обычного домушника.  +Есть концовка, что для песочницы не всегда характерно.  +Мир населён додиками.  +Чувствуется развитие, хоть и короткое. Фармить на очередную примочку хочется.  +Не сможет быстро надоесть, слишком короткая для этого.  +Проходится за 1-2 дня на одном дыхании.  +Наличие сюжета скорее в качестве обучения, чем в качестве передачи истории.  +Интересная концепция.   P.S.  Жду DLC  P.P.S  Короткая история. Представьте, как вы угоняете машину из особняка. Дали по газам и сильно разогнались. Выехали за его пределы и тут, на всю карту слышится FREEZE! от охранника особняка. Конечно, вы ничего не можете с собой поделать и жмёте на тормоз, вместо того, чтобы просто уехать. 关于Hermit Games工作室，其实应该写一部小说叫《关于一个神级美工和一个大佬企划被一帮猪队友干碎的日常》，刚玩我还觉得这没有无敌帧的翻滚，这超高的上手难度怎么这么熟悉，然后一看关联，原来是《神明在上》和《猎源》的开发商啊，那没事了。 （以下以有过场动画的关卡为界限而称的一关）  先说为啥打差评： 1.非常高的上手难度（没有瑟西的影子技能你打boss能打俩钟头），非常多的易损血点（怪物近乎疯狂的好战性、第一关的多数机关房、第三关必须先杀稻草人的机制、还有各个精英怪、大小boss的疯狂弹幕等） 2车轮战下，自身的脆弱且低伤害,回复道具回复量少而且数量少（没错你不仅是个玻璃，还是个面，还没有多少药能扶起来来，当然也可以选每次用回复之心满回复的祝福，但重点是前边） 3技能品质的随机（没错，满级蓝品的蛋黄酱的约定和橙品的约定根本就是天壤之别，有满级橙品蛋黄酱约定配合瑟西的影子盾站撸一切！） 4.翻滚不是躲避技，是位移技能（没有无敌帧，容易被卡地形，更容易掉进特殊地形受伤，也没法穿越怪物，当然你如果选瑟西的闪避无敌也行，就是我认为没有闪避伤害技能打起架来回很痛苦） 5.魔物娘好看的一匹，为啥我带出去就变成原形了？快给我变回来！（没错，哪个LSP能对着章鱼冲出来，那操作系统也太牛逼了，但是我TM冲爆蛋黄酱） 玩了这个公司的几个游戏，除了《神明在上》的联机很简单外（单人模式难度高的吓人），其他的我都认为这个公司可能是SM运动的倡导者——给你非常好看的外表和非常难受的内容，但是只是抢先测试，先打个差评，如果能在游戏性上有更多的进步，游戏内容进一步充实，我会回来改评论，建议是趁打折入或者观望。  如果你入了，但是你手又残怎么办（不针对各位大神，只是想给一直不能通关的朋友的建议）：前期隐忍攒够锤子喷子连弩，一定要做找瑟西的任务。锅子多点科技和探索，主要点出爆率和祝福品质、等级提升。然后带上喷子，碎片技能选喷子连发和对同一目标逐渐加伤和连弩射速加快（忘了叫啥） 祝福方面：1.瑟西的远程攻击出影子和影子盾必备（影子盾建议紫品以上）影子辅助可选（进一步增加连弩的伤害，这东西伤害非常可观，没有品质限制），剩下的瑟西的技能也都可以选，瑟西技能是真的万金油。2.蛋黄酱的濒死冻结自身，约定都是必备（手残就要增加自己的容错率，建议紫品以上）3.罗斯柴尔德的翻滚技能，建议选（就是金钱猫的翻滚出飞机，也忘了叫啥了，不需要品质，有就行，躲闪时候能配合影子打输出，冰火也都行）。4.阿罗那的火焰环绕，看情况（一是为了增加输出，二是如果拿的都不错，可以直接找瑟西合成影子爆炸，进一步增加伤害），剩下角色技能都选被动系（自动触发的，比如亚撒的扫描弓，也能和瑟西的影子合成影子箭，进一步增加输出，对方死的快，我们才死的慢嘛），大招建议选阿罗那得爆炸——配合塔罗牌的大招后召唤20S的强力影子。塔罗牌选治疗之心满血回复、大招后召唤影子、多两条命（人菜命就要多——鲁迅玩魂斗罗后如是说）        你问锤子？锤子就是个锤子！要不是因为它带50护盾谁带他。

Follow The Cpt Froggy Club Curator Page for plenty more![/b][/url][/quote]  Indivisible: ~~~~~~~~   In the beautiful village of Ashwat, a sixteen-year old girl known as Ajna, daughter of the village leader, lives a happy and cheerful life within the community. Her father, who was an excellent soldier in his youth, wants to make sure his young daughter becomes the best fighter in the land, and therefore enforces a strict regime every single day. Every morning, Ajna must attend a martial arts training session with her father. But one day she arrived late, which displeased her father, Indr.  Well, we all know how a sixteen year-old teenager can react, and yes, an argument took place, and Indr made his way swiftly back to the village. Feeling sad and annoyed with herself, Ajna ran after her Dad to apologise. But when she arrived at the outskirts of Ashwat, the village was on fire, and all the villagers, including her beloved father, were dead, having been killed by the army of Lord Ravannavar! Furious, she promises herself to find Lord Ravannavar and take revenge for the death of her father.   Indivisible is an action/RPG platformer game developed by Lab Zero Games and published by 505 Games on Steam on the 9 of October 2019.  This game is also available on PS4, as well as on Xbox One. The Switch version has not been released at the time of writing this review, but should be available later on this month (October 2019).  After fighting your father’s killer, Ajna decides not to return him the favour by killing him, but instead forces him to lead her to Lord Ravannavar, his boss. Right there comes the first funny thing in this game; Ajna can absorb people into her head. Not everybody, only people who join her in this adventure. In total, she’ll absorbed 22 characters along her journey. Can you imagine having 22 voices popping out of your head during a conversation? You’d be a bit edgy, wouldn’t you? But Ajna is a natural, and can even travel into her own head (her Inner Realm) to talk to each of these individuals and upgrade her offensive and defence fighting techniques. But to improve her fighting skill, she must find Ringsels, which are red stones laid out in the levels and usually not easy to reach.  As Ajna welcomes new guests inside her head, you will be given a short description of the guest’s attacks. You can select right there to use this new character in your party (4 in total) or at any given time.  The levels are very well-structured, and Ajna will find herself going up, down, left and right non-stop! Be careful to avoid spikes on walls, ceilings and on the floor as it will dramatically decrease Ajna’s health each time she touches them. She’ll be talking to new people, of whom some will find a new home in her brain, along with others who will give her information as part of the story. Within each level, there are small structures with a bells hanging in the middle, similar to the ones you find in some monasteries. When she reaches one of them, she can meditate and save her journey. As she progresses through her quest, she’ll acquire new items, such as an axe, a bow with an explosive arrow and a spear. With the axe, she will be able to smash wooden obstacles to access new rooms, or use the explosive arrows to break rocks into pieces that block entrances to other rooms or areas. The spear she’ll be able to use as a pole vault to reach higher grounds. All these items will help her to fight enemies within each level (if she doesn’t touch them; if she does, it will activate the combat phase) to inflict as much damage as possible before entering the combat phase.  She’ll find enemies in each stage, and they will be tougher ones each time she reaches a new location.  Before entering the combat phase, she will be able to use her bow and arrow to damage some enemies as they come towards her.  Later in the game, she will also have access to a spear. Bear in mind that some enemies will not receive any damage if she only uses the bow and arrow.  In these cases, she’ll need to get close to the opponent before the opponent gets up, and hit it hard to activate the combat phase.  I really like the real-time combat phase. Here, Ajna and three other characters will engage with one or more enemies. The exciting thing is that as a player, you never know how many opponents you will face before you’re actually in the combat phase.  Each of your characters will have three small spheres underneath them, which represent their attacks. Each time you use one or all of them rapidly, it will take a few seconds to regenerate each of the spheres before you can re-attack the foe(s). Each successful attack will increase a power bar located on the top left of your screen, and when it is full, you can use it to activate a special move with one of your four characters. However, the opponent(s) will fight back. Some will attack the entire party and other’s will attack specific characters. At the moment, you need to block their strikes. If you don’t, not only will your character’s health decrease, but the power bar will reduce.  The trick is to manage to keep having your characters’ spheres full and continue striking your enemies all the time to inflict more and more damage. At the end of the combat, you’ll receive experience points, and your characters might level up.    What a game, let me tell you! I found myself absolutely absorbed right from the start. I have been playing Indivisible for the past 14 hours and successfully completed 7 levels so far. I’ve really enjoyed the story so far, along with each of the characters that I have found during my gameplay.   The hand-drawn artwork and animations are top-notch, and the game runs smoothly — splendid narrative, both voice and written, with lots of humour.  There are plenty of settings available for this game, and it has been translated into 10 languages so far. You can use your keyboard or gamepad to play Indivisible (for me, gamepad is the way to go for PC player). Very hard to find a negative for this game.  Positives: ~~~~~~~   +	Splendid artwork +	Over 20 characters to play with +	Fun Story with fabulous narrative, both voice and written, and good humour +	Great combat phases +	Extremely addictive +	Full controller support +	Achievements  Negatives: ~~~~~~~~   -	No trading cards as yet (Steam)  Join Ajna and her friends in a fabulous journey through a stunning Fantasy world! An absolutely delightful and addictive game!  9/10   Key provided by developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own! If you don't like Telltale Games, this is not for you. If you don't like visual novels, choice, or episodic games a la Life is Strange or Always Sometimes Monsters, you won't like this. There's a lot of reasons not to like this, including the somewhat hamfisted cameos from the original HBO cast and the fact that there are a lot of choices that don't make a bit of difference in the overall outcome. There are some that do, but you'll have to find those out.   Personally? I love this. I would throw my entire wallet at Telltale Games if I could, simply because I'm the kind of person who enjoys visual novels and latches onto characters like a fangirlish leech. Rodrik and Asher are some of the best characters I have seen from a game in a very long time. There are, in fact, several choices you can make, especially in the later episodes, that have a huge impact on the fate of House Forrester -- but, unfortunately, there are others which don't make a damn bit of difference. Another struggle for me was getting the stupid mouse to not lag, which involved getting into the guts of my AMD card and turning VSync off (which still didn't work), so that's a thing.   However, overall, I love this series. I love Telltale Games. I don't know GoT outside the first season of the show and the first few chapters of the first book, but I was still able to understand most of what was going on (partly because the internet is a wonderful den of spoilers just waiting to pop out at you). But that's my personal opinion, and if anything above turns you off from this, then I wouldn't recommend buying it. If you like Telltale Games and GoT, absolutely go for it.

Крайне необычная игра, которую я бы мог рекомендовать не всем, но только любителям много читать. Очень много читать. Зато, если вам задавали в школе список литературы на лето, то вы хотя бы прочтете эту игру, если уж решили игнорировать школьную программу. Временами текст будет достаточно сложно понять неискушенному игроку, учитывая непростой язык и тематику бесед, но здесь хватает интересных диалогов и историй, так что скучно быть не должно. Из плюсов я бы также отметил симпатичную графику и оригинальный юмор. Если вы сторонник получить максимальную продолжительность игры за свои деньги, то здесь вас также ожидают плюсы, ибо проходить эту игру придется очень долго. Лично мне больше всего запала в душу идея с системой диалогов со своими внутренними качествами. Прям вот очень хорошо показано, что мы все не единый цельный организм, а на самом деле нас раздирают противоречия и внутренние конфликты. Вот именно из-за этого мне эта игра запомнилась больше всего. Из минусов я бы мог отметить темп игры и то, что из-за специфики эта игра может зайти не всем. В остальном же это интересный инди-проект, в который стоит поиграть, чтоб поддержать разработчика в его нелегком деле и познакомиться с хорошей и необычной игрой. Всем удачи, конечно же.

[h1]Pour résumer, Heavy Fire: Afghanistanest un rail shooter[/h1]  J’ai, comme tout le monde, pris goût aux FPS où je peux faire évoluer mon personnage à sa guise et à son rythme sur le terrain. Heavy Fire: Afghanistan est un « rail shooter ». On en trouve très peu, tout au moins dans les jeux récents. Un « rail shooter » est comme un FPS dans le sens où vous tirez quasiment sur tout ce qui bouge mais à la différence, c’est que vous ne contrôlez pas votre déplacement. En effet, c’est l’ordinateur qui gère votre déplacement en fonction de certains critères bien spécifiques (temps, nombre de tirs, nombre de morts, etc).  Heavy Fire: Afghanistan est un jeu autour de la guerre d’Afghanistan menée par les américains. Ce qui est surprenant, c’est que le studio derrière le jeu est lui polonais.  Graphiquement, musicalement, au niveau du rythme du jeu, il n’y a rien à redire, c’est du très bon travail. Ce qui me dérange plus, c’est le sujet. On n’a pas assez de recul pour le juger. Qui sait, peut être que dans 50 ans, on parlera de cette guerre en Afghanistan comme on parle de la 2de Guerre Mondiale ! This game is not perfect, but I still find it fun.   I enjoyed the battle pace and seeing my horde of axe men break through enemy shield walls was satisfying to me. The last total war game i really played was shogun 2, so the diplomacy was very refreshing to me since i wasn't locked in war with the entire map for no reason. i was, however, locked in war with the entire map because i like to party. Also, it was nice that small factions with a single province weren't able to send a full stack of high quality units at me ever few turns like they would in shogun 2.  The food mechanic was a nice challenge at the beginning of the game, but by the end of it I would have needed to amass an army large enough to rival the current U.S. national debt just to bring the food count back to the double digits.  I found that I could get away with auto resolving most of the fights. If you won an auto resolve, 9 times out of 10 the enemy army was completely destroyed. when i fought an army manually, it first retreated, then i beat it in the first battle so it was forced to retreat. i followed it and beat the army again in the same turn and it still was not dead. the next turn it ran around me and took an undefended building which brings me to my next point.  back in shogun 2, you could raise small armies, without a general, to help garrison your provinces, among other things. in this game, you cant just recruit a unit, they need a leader. since they added in ungarrisoned buildings and property, it is annoyingly easy for single units of half dead generals to take land and immediatley raise a nearly full stack of similarly half dead units who will all be slowly replensihed the longer it takes you to catch up and axe them a question (sorry).  Also, i found it hard to see my unit banners through trees during battles. it made things a bit chaotic when i couldn't tell what was going on in there.  Ironically, the hardest point in the campaign for me was towards the end  when i owned 3/4 of the map. I might just not understand what buildings to use to make money, but it seemed like my only real source of income was trade. At this point, i was making about 14,000 moneys per turn and i declared war on West Seaxe. all the other remaining factions were vassals of West Seaxe, so i had no one left to trade with. In one turn i went from making 14,000 per turn, to -9,000, which made things... interesting. im pretty sure I had beaten the campaign at that point, but if you don't play total war for absolute domination, you're doing it wrong.   to sum things up, from my perspective, this is a decent game, but not perfect. the diplomacy has some nice improvements and some mechanics that could use some tweaking. the battles are fun and they seem balanced to me. I would recommend this game unless you absolutley hated the past few entries in the series.

I'm going to preface that this game was gifted to me by my partner so that we could play together, but I'm immensely glad they did. Core Keeper is super fun, and the time we've spent playing went by without even blinking! Let's dive into why, as well as some small issues we encountered along the way.  FUN STUFF:  - Controls are easy to understand and controller compatible! Partner played on controller while I played on keyboard/mouse and we noticed no issues regarding controls.   - There is so much to do! The game starts off a bit slow because you have to build yourself and your little base up from the ground but when you get into it, it really goes off!   - Multiple play styles are complimentary with this game. I enjoy decorating and shaping the house and gardening to my heart's content; my partner treats the game similarly to Terraria, in which they explore, spelunk, fight monsters, and gather resources to further our journey. It's amazing that multiple styles of play can mesh together without having problems.   - Unique story and starting point in-game: I really like that you're forced to kind of dig your way around the beginning area.   - Three bosses (so far? early access!) that are all super cool looking and frankly, a little scary! Combat is fun but linear.   THE YUCKY STUFF:  - Sometimes game would lag a little, especially when too many torches were placed in one area. Trying to light up the house properly without putting too many fire effects in one room was a little bit of a struggle.    OVERALL:   The game is wonderful, especially for Early Access!! There's a lot to do and it's definitely worth playing with friends if you can and is a worthwhile venture for solo-players as well. I'm super excited to see when the full game releases and will definitely keep playing in the mean time! Solid 15/10 pumpkins.

One of best CRPGs ever made.   The story is dark and wonderful. It explores themes like ethics in science, self-determination and religious fanaticism that have been left out of mainstream video games for a long time and asks you to make some very difficult decisions that have a real impact on the world.  The combat is a throwback to the old Infinity Engine games made by the developers who actually worked on those games at Interplay and Black Isle Studios.  They have however modernized or trimmed numerous tedious aspects of those games (I'm looking at you THAC0) and made the end-result feel a lot tighter. Also this game is seriously challenging, if you're completely unfamiliar with isometric CRPGs or if you're in it for the story start playing on easy, there's certainly no shame in it and you'll save yourself a lot of frustration while you're learning the ropes.  The White March expansion (both parts) is absolutely worth the money. You should definitely get it if you find yourself enjoying the game. However, since the expansion's story takes places during the main campaign (between Act 2 and Act 3 IIRC) you shouldn't wait too long after starting.  In conclusion, whether you've been jonesing for that sweet isometric fix for the last fifteen years or you've never even thought about touching the stuff, you should give Pillars of Eternity a shot!

There is no wealth in this game. Meaning no poor or rich. Only density and size. The only finance you have to worry about is your cities. Land value is only a measure of activeness.  2. Traffic isn't perfect. Although traffic can be a struggle things like cars or people clipping happens often and driver AI can be dumb. Most of this can be fixed with mods however.  3. Map is kind of small. I know, I know it's bigger then SimCity, but is that really that hard?. Compared to older games like simcity 4, the map is kind of small.  4. No trading with other city's. This is something I loved about simcity 4 and one of the few strong points of the modern simcity game. All your external connections are random, generated names of cities.   5. Small zoning. This is my biggest issue with this game   Overall however worth every penny.

now it says 0 hours for this game but i played it on console while i had PC repairs done and the only reason i have this game in my library is that it came in a humble bundle and all the other titles were decent but getting to the point ....just ...wow... to date this has to be not the worst game i have ever played but definitely the worst sequel. i mean it was never going to be an easy task living up to the standards set by the games predecessor Red Faction: Guerrilla but whoever was leading the Dev team for this game had clearly either never played the first game or was doing so blindfolded and with noise cancelling earphones on. the list of issues i have with this game makes it difficult to know where to begin.  okay so Armageddon is a linear third person shooter set in the Red Faction universe. the game follows the great grandson of Alex Mason (the Hero of the first game) named Darius Mason. Darius is a soldier in the Red Faction army who now rule mars after the events of the first game but after a monumental screw up on his part humanity is left living underground unable to survive on the surface of mars. the story to this game is many things and none of them good, its generic, poorly paced, poorly written and has a penchant for making scenes appear dramatic when you can blatantly see them coming. it even has a love interest side story to it (totally not trying to copy and paste from the first game) which gets a fittingly poor ending to it. its not the worst writing i have ever laid eyes on but its damn close to it. they say if you gave a thousand monkeys type writers and left them alone they would eventually type out the complete works of Shakespeare.. this game is what the monkeys typed out.  down to the core of this game, the mechanics .. now despite my disliking for this game the mechanics are one of the few things that this game actually got correct. gun mechanics work perfectly as expected, movement is smooth with no issues and in general the games mechanics are as solid as Armageddons (there is a god after all). this is a rare redeeming feature in a sea of disaster. the only real issues you could have with the mechanics would be during the flight mission when the ship does control a bit like you are having a seizure at the wheel but  other than this instance they are fine. the best part of this game which i very much believe they just copied over from the first game is the destruction engine (i shudder to imagine if they had redone this aspect as well) the engine is great providing seamless destruction of cover and environments. this is the best part of this game just being able to blow up or disintegrate the cover preventing you from slaying the enemy (be warned this works both ways) and i did quite enjoy this diamond among the rough feature after the hours of endless fun you get from it in the first game.  back to whats wrong with this game then. its a LINEAR sequel to a SANDBOX game ... how hard did the games developers hit each other over the head with a hammer to think this would work. look at any successful sandbox game such as Grand Theft Auto or Saints row ... imagine they had a linear sequel ... it just doesn't work .. this kind of game is meant to be played as a sandbox. this very story driven linear progression also hampers the range of missions the player has access to. in the first game the player conducted a wide range of mission in order to advance, now though the levels can be summarized by starting each mission and being told .. follow this line and kill everything in your path. there is no diversity it is just a repeated slog of go here run this way and kill this thing. there is also NOTHING but story in this game, no side missions except for collecting a few audio logs left in blatantly obvious places throughout the game. the first game had a wide variety missions and activities set aside from the main campaign. why would you develop a game and then remove all the content for the sequel? its just stupid really. the linear environments also have a negative affect on combat. no more flanking the enemy or sniping from afar no for this game you just have to slug it out in toe to toe combat 90% of the time unless that specific part of the game requires the use of a sniper or other specialist weapon. because we totally hated having the diverse arsenal of weapons available at any point in the previous game .. thanks THQ you are a real star .. NOT  and now we have the multiplayer.. what can i say for this other than DON'T!!.. the multiplayer for this game is almost as terrible as the single player with majority of the issues from the core game crossing over into the multiplayer. to simplify it you have two modes a mode for destruction where player stake it in turn to see who can cause the most destruction in a map and a kind of horde mode where the player stares down waves of aliens hoping not to become E.Ts Dinner. the destruction mode is pretty fun to begin with but there is again not much diversity to it and it gets pretty boring pretty quickly. the horde mode lasts a bit longer with more maps and a better experience if your playing with other players but again its just the same thing over and over and over .. the maps are okay but the AI for the aliens is shoddy at best. sometimes they wont even notice you when you stand in front of them or on the flip side they will spot you from a mile away and bring all their little buddies to tear your martian nads right off (funny when watching it happen.... not so funny when it happened to me :( ). its a great laugh if you are playing it every now and again or in split screen but it doesn't last. the hype for this game actually quite excited me at the time and i (regrettably) pre-ordered this game thinking it would be as awesome as the first game ... i was wrong. in short this game is a less than enjoyable experience. the linear, poorly written generic story and tedious gameplay coupled with the poor multiplayer experience and community make this a game i wouldn't be in a hurry to play again. despite the redeeming features of the amazing destruction engine and all around good mechanics for this game they are twinkling plus points in the sea of disaster that is this game. in short .. if you buy this game after reading this you probably have a power drill or some other sharp object jammed in the side of your head O_o in which case you probably loved the ending to RAGE and live on the moon..

Gone Home is a first person interactive story, developed by The Full Bright Company. Being released on PC in August 2013, before a planned release on PS4 and Xbox One in early 2016.   I wouldn’t say Gone Home is a game, because there is the only thing you do in this game is walk from room to room interacting with notes and books, that’s it. This game has often been marked as being a walking simulator, and to be honest, people aren’t far wrong with that notion. From start to finish there the only sort of action or puzzle, or anything really worthy of being called gameplay, would be a short puzzle involving finding hidden cupboards.  I was quite honestly bored after five minutes of starting the game.   Graphically, the game is quite nice though. There are some really nicely done lighting mechanics in the game, and textures are all really high quality as well. Even items that you pick up have really nicely made graphics and textures on, such as bottles in the kitchen or bathroom. There isn’t any animation to be found in the game though; you come into contact with no moveable objects throughout the game. Gone Home is narrated well too, the voice acting is done really well, and there is from memory no sound effects that standout, just a lot of ambiance sounds of the storm going on outside.   The only really shining light to come out of Gone Home is that it has a fairly compelling story. As a mid-twenties male though, I couldn’t relate to anything that was happening. You are basically reading a ton of notes, letters, diaries and posters. I was quite interested to follow the story until completion but I can’t say that I really enjoyed it all that much. It’s a very slow paced story which only really gathers paced towards the end of the game. You can get even more lore and plot from the game by searching high and low for more notes and letters if you want to.   A complete run through Gone Home will take you less than an hour to finish. This is with finding most of the extra notes for more stories as well. There is no replay ability, because to be quite honest, it’s a stretch to even get one run through out of it.   Technically I didn’t run into any problems. The game runs smooth and there are no glitches or bugs. Although there isn’t really anything that complicated going off on screen anyway…  To sum up, I am not going to recommend Gone Home. How this “game” is priced at £14, 99 are is astounding. I picked this up when it was on sale for £1, 79 a while ago, and even now I think I have been ripped off. There is a string of pretentious reviews on this “game” that quite honestly make me cringe whilst reading.  Gone Home is quite literally one of the most boring and unexciting “games” I have played this year and cannot recommend it to anyone. Even for the 15 quid I wouldn't recommend this game. I bought it and decided to play it on merit. I really wanted to like this game.  The game mechanics are dreadful and more rage inducing than fun. Jumping and and climbing is all pre-determined in repetitive ways. Jumping distance is determined by the situation, never making it clear if you need to swing with an axe. Several times I've jumped and tried to grapple a wall that won't allow me to as it's not next in the climbing progress, yet I can clearly get to it. Even at the end level the game is still prompting you for to climb, almost like they know it's unclear what they want you to do. So many times you just need to jump straight up but it just doesn't and you fall slightly to the side, glide down the climbable wall and die.  Combat is equally poor. You'd just have to play it to see why. Bad mechanics and a poor combat system do not make combat hard but do make it a chore rather than fun. There is little reason to use any weapon but the machine gun. Stealth is okay and a good way to avoid having to fight. That said, you can just run past all the enemies to the next section to skip almost any fight.  The story... well it starts off okay and I was getting into it. Then it gets a bit old. A bit predictable. At 60% completion I just wanted to finish the game. Overall the story is another huge disappointment. Not just as a story but how it all ends as well. It really does feel rushed at times. All that build up to disappointment and then rushed ending.   Tombs and side missions. There is no point to side missions. Time fillers, that's all they are. Tombs can be fun, they are repetitive but different enough to not be too annoying. I still didn't see the point in doing most of them though. You will never suffer for resources or money in the game and upgrades are easily obtained.  Visually its a nice game. The detail of the environments is amazing. If they had put as much time and effort into the gameplay then this would have been amazing. Ray tracing is very good and does add a lot to the experience. It's a shame I had to turn it off as not even a 20170 Super can do it without dropping below 60fps. Playing at 1080p max settings (no RT) stays nicely above 75fps in the most graphically intense areas of the game, normally higher.  Overall this was not the worst game I have even played but puts forward a strong argument and justification for those that don't pay for their games...

Fury Unleashed é um jogo em desenvolvimento que tem recebido frequentes atualizações, o que é um sinal promissor para os jogadores. A análise positiva do jogo até o momento é baseada em seus pontos fortes e nas melhorias que têm sido implementadas durante seu desenvolvimento.  Uma das características notáveis de Fury Unleashed é a jogabilidade frenética e cheia de ação. Os jogadores são colocados em um mundo repleto de inimigos desafiadores e devem usar suas habilidades e armas para enfrentar hordas de adversários. A combinação de tiroteio intenso, movimentos ágeis e mecânicas de plataforma fluídas cria uma experiência emocionante e empolgante.  Além disso, o jogo apresenta um sistema de progressão interessante. À medida que os jogadores avançam nas fases, eles podem desbloquear novas armas, habilidades e melhorias para o personagem. Isso proporciona uma sensação de crescimento e evolução, incentivando os jogadores a continuarem explorando o jogo.  A estética visual de Fury Unleashed também merece destaque. O jogo apresenta um estilo de arte em quadrinhos, com cores vibrantes e detalhes impressionantes. Essa abordagem visual única contribui para a imersão dos jogadores no mundo do jogo e adiciona um toque distintivo à experiência.  A equipe de desenvolvimento tem sido ativa na implementação de atualizações regulares, o que é um bom sinal para os jogadores. Essas atualizações podem incluir correções de bugs, melhorias de desempenho, adição de conteúdo novo e ajustes com base no feedback da comunidade. O comprometimento da equipe em aprimorar e expandir o jogo demonstra sua dedicação em fornecer uma experiência de qualidade aos jogadores.  No entanto, é importante observar que, como o jogo ainda está em desenvolvimento, algumas áreas podem precisar de mais atenção e refinamento. Bugs e problemas técnicos podem ocorrer, mas a equipe de desenvolvimento está trabalhando para corrigi-los e aprimorar a experiência do jogo ao longo do tempo.  Em resumo, Fury Unleashed é um jogo em desenvolvimento com grande potencial. Sua jogabilidade cheia de ação, sistema de progressão e estética visual única o tornam uma experiência empolgante. Com atualizações frequentes, a equipe de desenvolvimento demonstra seu compromisso em fornecer um jogo cada vez melhor. É um título que vale a pena acompanhar e explorar à medida que continua a evoluir.

Today's the 45th Anniversary of the Apollo 11 Moon Landing so I figured a review of my favorite Space Legos game is in order! There's the standard creative mode which is pretty self explanatory then there's the survival mode which adds the challenge and realism we all love.   The hardest part I've found players having when adjusting to the game is the initial loss of direction after getting thrown into space. Gravity Generators are your best friend when starting off, especially when mining with the hand drill and exploring your first asteroid. After that, it's all fun and building. Right now there isn't much in the way of enemy NPCs (besides the occasional cargo ships you can enable) but I'm sure that'll be impoved upon in the future.   If you're a fan of MineCraft that would like some more sci-fi complexity in their life, do give SE a whirl.

What can I say? It's a really solid FPS that hasn't aged too well, which i'll get into, but still gets a good enough mix of horror and action FPS elements right enough for it to be worth playing if you wish to continue the story where FEAR left off.  So, why it hasn't aged well - Despite being a console designed game the 16:9 resolution feels like a stretched out 4:3 rather than true 16:9 with a super narrow FOV to boot. Even GeForce experience records this in 4:3 which I found odd being that I played in 4K. Unlike FEAR and it's expansions the game didn't crash anywhere near as much, but still did crash maybe every hour or 2. The removal of quick save really pushed it into being a game that was clearly designed for console, but then also lacked XInput support, so no Xbox controller support and the M&K controls felt very strange to use. The gameplay was also far too easy on medium as you just killed most people before they became a threat at all with it being clearly balanced exclusively for controller so I genuinely didn't die once, save for a suicide cased by falling off I don't even know what due to another bug. The textures sometimes don't load for a checkpoint unless you reload the checkpoint so you just get black areas with a few assets loaded in and some of them were at the end of checkpoints so I would have to blindly walk through blackness until I saw I hit a checkpoint to reload the textures in manually. The textures were also fairly aged despite being technically better and so it wasn't as clean as the first game visually.  Now having said all that... Why would I recommend it? I felt the atmosphere and story were really solid as well as the general feel being good enough provided you get past the lack of a real true port and imbalanced gun-play seemingly designed for 30FPS (I played at over 144). It kept me solidly entertained as these are all minor issues to me personally when it comes to older PC ports. I think the story was very well written, not exceptional and certainly not better than the first when you account for the hidden intel lore files which i'm a sucker for when they are as intriguing as FEAR's, but solid nonetheless and the atmosphere really kept me engaged with it from start to finish. Alma is just not always on your mind here due to it's push towards a more CoD style game which doesn't lend itself well to this franchise. I much prefer the paranormal aspects to the cookie cutter grunts known as the Replicas, or ATC. I get the lore and take no issue with it, only dislike the push towards CoD imitation with horror elements. Alma felt almost secondary, but was just kept in mind enough to keep me interested.

See this old scroll in my hand . . .  can someone tell me why sailor Sean is looking at my hook? Oh, shiver me timbers - this scroll is the map of the archipelago right in front of us! One hundred islands in total and all have a cross on them! That’s right me hearties, each hold exceptional booty for the taking. Arrgh, now seriously . . . does anyone on board have half a brain? “Yo Ho Ho” the entire crew screamed! “Oh boy, it’s going to be a long treasure hunt”, thought Captain Backwater.   Captain Backwater is a casual puzzle game where you have to loot one hundred Islands - what a pirate’s dream!  Well, this is a very interesting puzzle game, to say the least. The game set out as a square with ten by ten tiles. Your goal is to match two, three or even four items on the square by colliding them into each other to clear the level with a minimum of moves.  You have one hundred stages to clear and there are plenty of variations. First, in each level some of the tiles will be occupied by a rock, which in most levels is pretty handy but in others can be a pain, especially if the rocks divide two areas in that level. The rapier icon will help you to destroy one of these rocks. The trick is to know which rock to destroy so you can clear the level. Other levels don’t have items of the same colour and you‘ll probably ask yourself, how am I going to do this? The answer is easy, look for which tile has a splash on it and make sure to send your object to it; it will then change colour to match the other item. The other way is to paint them using a paint brush, if it is available to you. On some occasions, neither of them will be available. However, bombs and dynamite will probably be placed in some tiles, which can be very helpful in those instances. Some other variants, like the spikes, can make a level tricky and as soon as one of your objects hovers over the tile where the spikes are located, that specific tile will be blocked. If you see a parrot on the sign where your score is displayed, well you’re going to have fun . . . each time one object touches another (not the one it should collide with), its colour will change.  As for goblets, make them collide and a monkey will appear, indicating time for you to catch bananas, giving you additional points at the end of the stage.  There are plenty of other variations which I’ll let you discover for yourself.   You can also collect coins. These are hidden on squares and can be collected if one item hovers over it, but be quick to use your mouse to pick them up, just like the bananas.  In regards to the gameplay, it is very simple. Select an item and with your mouse select the direction you want it to go.  Graphically, Captain Backwater is colourful and the soundtrack is cool!  As I mentioned above, I really like the variations. It’s a great game to introduce to children who have never played puzzle games. The game runs well but currently crashes when you switch it to full screen.  Positives: ~~~~~~~   -	Colourful graphics -	100 levels to clear -	Plenty of variations  -	Easy to play and great to introduce to children  Negatives: ~~~~~~~~   -	Game crashes when switching to full screen -	No achievements or trading cards  Captain Backwater is an easy, fun and well-designed puzzle game with plenty of variations. A great game to introduce to children.    7/10  Key provided by developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own! 在考试周购买这个游戏是我这学期犯下的最大的错误，三天之内给全成就了。 说几点  1.音乐。引起思考，论游戏BGM对玩家进入心流状态的促进作用。 如果说我给这个游戏打90分，有60分是给这些BGM的。 这个游戏的音乐有多出色，我语言描述不来，就列简单的数据 游戏本体98元，大小1.19G；原声带128元，大小1.50G  2.剧情。叙事方面缺少沉浸感和连续性，不过相同的叙事方式对比一下空洞骑士我觉得很友好了。随着剧情或等级的推进，主角的形象会有变化，有助于剧情理解 另，过场动画疑似有卡顿bug  3.技能。总共26个技能，大多数是玩具性质，我常用的只有9个，看个人吧。地图全收集之后技能不可能全部升到满级，但是成就系统里并未对此做出要求，无须担心。反观2077地图全收集之后的获得的钱不能买下所有的车，然后你成就系统还有这项要求，索性我直接不做了，剩下的钱你让我打混混凑？还是卖饮料凑？无趣。 无须担心为什么要说？主要还是想骂2077。  4.地图。乍一看很正常，本应该很正常，后期做全收集就离谱起来了，感觉像换了个游戏。 查了攻略我恍悟，我是在玩蔚蓝，B面水准的。  5.主观感受。[spoiler]这是2021年给我总体感受最好的游戏，有始有终有不舍，全成就之后总想再在这个世界做点什么，打打怪却发现无事可做。让我回想起了童年时，没那么多游戏可玩，电脑上的疯狂水族馆、PSP上的死神嘉年华，PS3上的瑞奇与叮当……反复玩，通关，重开，通关，重开，从来不会厌倦。看看现在，游戏多了，但我也失去了最开始玩游戏的快乐，变得浮躁，像交差一样赶紧把游戏通了然后卸载，也有很多没通就卸了的。我需要回想的，就是童年时那种重复的欲望，而这个游戏让我回想起了那种欲望，我将来会反复通关。 客观来讲，就算这个游戏BGM很优秀，但动作和战斗都有缺陷，不至于我给出这么高的评价。但我可能感性高于理性，音乐、美术、剧情、和我自己的游戏时间，谜一样作用在一起，给了我一种高于语言描述的美的享受，我喜欢上了这个游戏塑造的世界、角色和故事，我会常回来看看。对于我，获得的快乐和感受不能用98元来衡量。[/spoiler]   [spoiler]2021年那个夏天，我成为了白毛萝莉[/spoiler]

For Honor es un juego de lucha ambientado en la época medieval, en el que disfrutamos del mejor y mas realista sistema de combate jamás creado para juegos de éste tipo. Un poco complicado al principio, pero totalmente revolucionario y que una vez se aprende, hace la dinámica y la experiencia del juego super inmersiva y te da la posibilidad de enfrentarte casi de igual a igual contra cualquier adversario por experimentado que sea, si conoces los movimientos y eres capaz de mantener la sangre fría. De hecho, no se entiende que no se haya convertido en algo a tener en cuenta por otros desarroyadores. Ya quisiéramos ver éste sistema de combate implementado en otros juegos tipo Skyrim o Conan Exiles. Puedes elegir entre 3 facciones distintas, enfrentadas entre sí, hacia quienes en teoría irán dirigidos los beneficios de tus hazañas en combate o los perjuicios de tus derrotas: Caballeros, Vikingos y Samuráis. Aunque, sin importar a qué facción apoyes, podrás manejar guerreros de cualquier otra durante las batallas y combates. Hay un buen número de diferentes guerreros entre los que podrás elegir, principalmente 4 tipos en cada facción, Guardián, Híbrido, asesino y Pesado, cada uno con su propio estilo, ventajas y desventajas. Tiene una campaña de duración y dificultad bastante aceptables, muy útil para dar a conocer al jugador las posibilidades y utilidades de cada tipo de guerrero y facción, que hará que estés preparado para enfrentarte a cualquier clase de adversario. En cuanto al desarrollo de los personajes, el juego incentiva su versión online obligando al jugador a enfrentarse a otros jugadores, llegando a premiarle hasta con el triple de puntos de experiencia y ganancias que cuando juegas contra la I A. Se supone que existe un mapa en el que las diferentes facciones van ganando o perdiendo terreno a medida que los jugadores participan en sus batallas, pero no está bien implementado,,, para empezar puedes estar luchando con guerreros de otras facciones de tu lado y/o contra compañeros de facción en una misma batalla, de manera que a veces no queda muy claro si ganando la batalla favoreces a tu facción a la hora de ganar terreno en dicho mapa. Luego la gente usa demasiado a menudo guerreros de otras facciones, lo que al final le quita un poco el royo de rivalidad entre facciones y hace que parezca un todos contra todos sin mucho sentido. Recientemente han añadido una nueva facción, los chinos, que tienen guerreros realmente geniales, pero no se han molestado en darles una porción del mapa, de manera que han quedado como mercenarios para las otras, mas que como una facción en sí mismos. Por otro lado, aunque no faltará quien lo vea bien, muchos de los personajes tienen predefinido el sexo y no se puede cambiar, lo cual hace que se vean mujeres en combate constantemente, que dada la época en que se desarrolla el juego, queda totalmente anacrónico, en fin... Para gustos colores, pero a mí particularmente me disgusta bastante ir destripando y decapitando mujeres por mucho que se defienda hoy día la igualdad y que la situación se dé en campos de batalla.
