，极地战嚎5或者更通俗易懂的远哭5。这个系列从2004年至今已经跨过14年整，游戏内容也几经变革，到了正统续作的第五代育碧把我们带到了民风淳朴的美国蒙大拿州，在主角约瑟夫·席德的带领下体验一个关于对抗邪教的故事。本作为生化奇兵无限的编剧Drew Holmes，也就是被人习惯称为游戏第九艺术代表作的生化奇兵无限的编剧，我为什么要如此强调这个问题呢？因为下文将涉及到部分剧透，与这位编剧密不可分。由于牵扯到剧透，故将剧情放到最后分析，如有不足会及时更新补充，未购买游戏的玩家请看前两条即可我们所熟知的育碧除了一贯被人玩烂的土豆、bug梗以外，见多识广的玩家们总能从育碧的开放世界中体会到似曾相识的既视感，这种既视感通常来自育碧旗下其他游戏，我们将其俗称为借鉴。举几个例子，育碧传统的标记系统、警戒条系统你都能在育碧的很多游戏里见到，我不是说这种设定不好，而是按照育碧一年四五个开放世界游戏的发售速度，难免会让人产生疲劳。  远哭5基本上还是采用了3代的框架，取消了小地图、爬塔开图要素，对游戏系统稍加改动便呈现在我们面前。你要问我满不满意，我的回答一定是肯定的。远哭可以说算得上是保守的一派，本身就足够优秀成熟的游戏系统配上风格多变的游戏玩法，才造就了远哭系列的成功，但也是这种守旧的成功也难免会召来一些老玩家的抱怨，很难说如果下一代还是3、4、5代的威力加强版会不会还有那么多人买账了。远哭在经历了这么多年的的发展，似乎也到了游戏创新的瓶颈期，不过现在还刚刚好。  游戏在原本的基础上对部分内容进行了改革，刷皮刷到吐的制作系统终于砍掉了，技能解锁改为随着游戏进程、挑战特长和捡垃圾逐步解锁技能，不得不说这让游戏节奏变的紧凑而充实，游戏体验极佳。在这我要使劲夸夸育碧同志做的寻宝任务不仅没有一个重复，而且每一个寻宝地点都趣味十足，需要你动脑认真寻找线索揭开迷题发现真相。由于游戏背景变成更为文明的现代背景，打猎系统重心偏移，剥皮动画也随之取消，其实这样也不错，没有了太多的硬直更加方便简洁。  任务系统更有RPG味道，支线任务不再像之前任务设计为从A到B、杀个人、跑断腿、给点好处就张嘴，5代的任务设计为历代最佳，游戏演出效果更是让人热血沸腾，除了时不时剧情杀不讨喜以外整体问题不大除了结局。载具系统更加丰富立体，海陆空全机种制霸，载具的丰富也增强了游戏的玩法，只要你敢卖，那我全都要。游戏射击手感还不错，比4代要强，尤其是复合弓射击声音改变让我欲罢不能，biubiubiubiu的爽死了~大胆的采用真实弹道也让游戏体验有了更大变化，这些改变都是正确的方向希望育碧继续保持。  新增的游乐场模式必须要拿出来表扬一番，育碧终于开了窍，维持一个游戏生命力的最好办法就是要放得开，游戏不满意？设计师就是个垃圾？育碧你给我滚开老子教你做游戏！！鉴于育碧打算长久维持编辑器的更新我就有理由相信游戏不至于凉的飞快做完主线就吃灰，希望更多的大神能够为我们奉献出更多更优秀的地图，CC在这里先谢谢各位了。  育碧还是那个育碧，你大爷永远是你大爷  既然都说了这是育碧味开放世界，那总得有点闲话得拿出来唠唠嗑吧？哪怕是育碧粉也得认同游戏上的不足吧？每次谈到这个话题总是有种惋惜感，总有种看着自己的孩子考试总考七八十分、别人家的孩子一考试九十多分的感慨，你怎么就这么不争气呢？远哭5虽然整体问题不大算得上佳作，但距离精品还是有一定的差距，这份差距主要体现在游戏的深度上。  玩了这么多年的育碧游戏我总结出一个道理，育碧做游戏总是创意频出，总能找到意想不到的鬼点子，但这种鬼点子只停留在有想法的基础上，缺乏进一步的深度挖掘。就拿其他游戏举个例子，例如玩巫师3的时候玩家一上去并不能完全了解这个游戏，随着游戏的进行玩家逐步学会炼金打装备附魔猎魔人强化打昆特牌等内容，在你感到无聊的时候就会有新的内容注入刺激你的神经。反观远哭5，我们敲定角色进入游戏经历一场激动人心的追逐戏码之后，从道齐的地堡出来就把游戏解放内容直接丢在你脸上，做吧，这就是你的游戏内容，爱玩玩不玩滚。这盆凉水真的是透心凉心飞扬，我差点就骂出口了，要不是这四个解放项目在游戏中存在感不是很强还会让人产生育碧公式化开放世界恶习难改的错觉，育碧这步棋走的实在看不懂。  这还不是重点，我要谈的是游戏其他问题，钓鱼和打猎系统。我们都知道打猎自从三代开始就一直发挥着重要的作用那就是使人物能够装下更多更大更粗的东西，像一个移动军火库一样行走在世界各地，到了远哭5育碧一刀把这个系统废了，取而代之的是更为紧缩的经济系统，你要通过打猎钓鱼来赚取金钱，这样才能买得起更强大的装备更多的载具。我不反对经济系统的改革，因为之前的系统太过于臃肿不堪，手里揣着个几万买不起任何东西钱包还装不下，但本作问题就出在经济系统上，玩家忙着解放突突突杀杀杀，没有一个足够充裕的时间去静下心来钓钓鱼打打猎，钓鱼打猎与整体游戏流程节奏氛围不符，没等你钓完鱼敌人的剧情杀就先把你节奏打乱，解放完一个区域又得马不停蹄地前往下一个区域跟邪教组织英勇作战，除去部分支线和一两个主线需要你打猎钓鱼以外，哪怕你全程不碰钓鱼打猎也没有多大关系，有你钓鱼打猎的功夫多找几个解密地点多做几个只支线任务就有了，钓鱼打猎太过于鸡肋而且没有深度挖掘游戏乐趣，不禁让人叹息

I love this game.  It gave me that Baldur's Gate nostalgia with the cleanliness and good controls of a current game.  Simplified where it needed to be, complex everywhere else.  Loot and stats.  Excellent storytelling (and voice acting).  Characters you generally just love.  A great, twisted plot that gives you a ton of choice and control.  It played out like.....Dragon's Age did for me.  It pulled me into the world, and I played it to completion without stopping to play anything else in the meantime.  If you loved the original Dragon's Age and Baldur's Gate and wanted a great story to go through, I whole-heartedly recommend this game.  A villian as awesome as Kefka!  Awesome! ;)    Not everything in the game is strong.  It feels super fleshed out at first, but at some point it feels like it comes to a little bit of a standstill for a while, and everything just kinda slows way down.  But most RPGs have that sort of lull somewhere in the middle, and this is the same.  Sidequests are fun, but sometimes feel pretty pointless.  Then again, content is content, and if you cut all the pointless extra stories out, you don't have a very long game.  Also, you don't feel the need to use half the characters you get in your party.  I honestly never even used three of them, which was sad, because I liked their personalities but just felt like my chosen party functioned better mechanically.  Oh, the auto-pausing drove me a little crazy too, but if you turn it off, things have a tendancy to move too quickly for you to control, heh.  Anyways, I'm nitpicking.  This game rocks.  Not too long, but this is a quality over quantity sort of game.

The Witness sets out to be a modern day Myst. In that regards it had succeeded. Set on a mysterious island, you wander around completing puzzles. Rather impressively, these puzzles are all variants on the same mechanic, drawing lines on a grid. Don't let that simplicity fool you, these are hard puzzles that will leave you cursing the name of Johnathon Blow, the creator of The Witness.  Like a teacher, Johnathon Blow will gently lead you through the mechanics so that you learn not just to solve the puzzles, but to understand them. A key difference in that brute forcing through them or randomly guessing will be punished. With many areas to explore, each with its own unique take on the line drawing mechanics, it always felt like that even if I was stuck somewhere, I could go somewhere else and bang my head against a different wall. All I can say is, change your perspective and be observant of the environment.  One could even suggest that the island is like a metroidvania game, where the “item” is the knowledge you learn from each of the regions.   This game is a chain of moments where you go “Aha!” and suddenly understand the key. While you might not be physically lifting that item above your head to the world like in Zelda, you are essentially doing that mentally. I am often reminded of Fez when playing this game. Although Fez has that one moment where suddenly you see the code of the matrix, this game has a lot more (although slightly lesser) moments. Then again, it can still surprise you and make you open your eyes to wonder just what were you missing this whole time and what else might be hiding in plain sight.  Despite really enjoying this game, I did find a few pieces to dislike. While I can understand the choice in there being no music in this game, I disagree with it completely. But this is something that can be easily fixed by throwing some relaxing music on the music player. There are also certain classes of puzzles which some people might have a really hard time with. The “story” of The Witness is also very subtle and out of the way. Indeed the ending you get is rather disappointing. But it is a testament to the quality of the game that I didn't mind this all that much, helped very much by some of puzzles in the final area. Indeed the journey is much better than the destination.   Even if all you get is the first ending after 25 hours, it is still a brilliant game that is well worth the asking price. But if you wish to delve deep into the depths of the mystery of The Witness, it can still be worth your while.

I am not a Metal Gear Veteran. I have played one before but that was ages ago (Gamecube I think).   This isn't one game. This is multiple games, roled into one.  The first game you will play is about a badly hurt soldier who encounters supernatural enemies, where you can never be sure what is real and what is PTSD. That was fun. Your protagonist then recovers by the time honered method of getting shot at, mauled and generally getting abused and goes on to play the next game.  Game two is an openworld, sandbox stealth affair that takes you into afghanistan und afrika. That part almost takes itself serious if it wasn't for the serious breaks in immersion. The same soldier that just smartly called in another soldier to check the location where I just messed up my approach is completely unfazed when I use a box to hide. I whipped the box from my magic pockets and am running quite invisibly past him, because hey - whats strange in a camoflage box in the middle of the desert that wasn't there before.  Once you settled in there (and wonder idly if the PTSD soldier from game one was the same game) you get game three: half-arsed base building and online grindfest. Oh the joy! It even has microtransaction that allow you spend real money to speed up the wait for 'send X soldiers to do Y and get Z results without further interaction'! How very Farmville!  After that, the games start to mesh somewhat but it never feels like one game with different aspects but at least two horribly grafted story shooters and one farmville (you even get to collect sheep)  Everything is designed as a time-waster. Even by helicopter (which you are only a passenger in) it takes multiple minutes to get from one end of your base to the other, during which you can do little but look out the window. Missions have side objectives which are only revealed after finishing the mission so you either guess, check online or play every mission twice (or you don't give a rats ass about ratings).   Best point of the game: There is a valid reason why the fanservice waifu 'Quiet' insists on running around in pantyhose and bra in a warzone - She is powered by photosythesis and clothes would kill her

[code]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家【[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10566883]中国玩家鉴赏组[/url]】  加入我们的小组吧【[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/875486]点这里[/url]】[/code]  在《IXION》中玩家扮演一名“太坤”空间站管理员，肩负着要将整个空间站跃迁到另外星系的使命，空间站隶属于地球上的中立公司DOLOS，而这次的行动也是DOLOS对自己的宣传方式之一，结果空间站跃迁失败将月球击碎，破坏了地球上的生态环境导致地球上的人类几乎无一幸存。玩家需要做的就是管理好空间站这座“诺亚方舟”，小到建造建筑、收集材料、研发科技、供给食物等，大到建造采矿、科研、货运等飞船进行不同的工作，再扩展到探索未知宇宙坐标和星体，在太空这一主题的演出效果上，游戏确实做的十分出色。  玩家在游戏中需要派遣探测器去探索一块区域，来获得其原材料储备情况，再派遣采矿船挖掘材料并送回空间站，如果遇到了原材料堆积行星也可以直接派货运船直接搬回空间站，甚至可以在其他废弃的人造空间站里搬回冷冻仓休眠人类来补充人口。科技方面则是用科研船去探索行星采集科技点，在空间站的科研所内开发新建筑或者新科技。  游戏的建造方面目前是一个槽点颇多的部分，大多数自动化、流水线式的模拟游戏玩家都会在游戏进程逐步稳定之后来规划自己的空间，希望建筑能够既美观又高效，而在《IXION》中，玩家一不能提前预览建筑尺寸，如果想要搭建的漂亮，只能自己记录每一种建筑的尺寸，二不能在拆建筑时返还资源，这就让玩家很难在短时间内搭建出自己想要的空间站布局。  当然还有每个模拟器都绕不过的刁民问题。玩家总是在疑惑为什么都到末日了一加班还会翻脸，为什么一不满足需求就要闹事，当然从游戏设计角度来讲也是用这些“不合理”的事件来增加游戏的随机性和难度，但是给玩家的负面反馈是拉满的。更不要提《IXION》中还不是所有人都能参与工作，新人口的获取完全依赖冷冻仓，而冷冻仓只有随着故事线的解锁才能获取定量人口。即便解冻了冷冻仓，所获得的也不全是工人人口，同样还有很多的非人工人口在消耗物资，而这些人非但不能够提供任何帮助，每天不工作等吃等喝，一不高兴了还会到处搞爆炸，属于是刁民中的刁民了。  我们能从《IXION》上看到很多游戏的影子，但《IXION》确实也做出了自己的味道。玩家所经营的区域不在局限于一块土地或者一个星球，而是在整个星系中流浪，不停寻找生存空间，这种漂泊、探索的未知旅程和太空这一浩瀚神秘的主题都深深的吸引着玩家，游戏的美术、音乐所带来的那种宇宙恢弘大气和自身孤独无依的矛盾感也很难让玩家讨厌。但在游戏目前的玩法和剧情上，都有些流于表面，甚至可以说是辜负了视听上营造出的氛围，我觉得制作组完全可以再深挖这个主题的更多内容，那时才能称得上一款经典的城建模拟游戏。

This is my first Monster Hunter game and I was one of the few who had zero performance issues on launch (i7 8700 and GTX 1070 Ti with HD textures) but due to the Keyboard changes I tried to refund. Luckily Steam denied my refund and gave it another try after Capcom addressed performance issues for others. That patch lowered my CPU by a bit as well and lowered my CPU temp. And since then I've been playing it almost non stop.  Yes there's disconnects in multiplayer sometimes but most of them are due to Steam servers dying, not the game itself. This started recently only. Before it was fine.  The game as a whole is extremely polished with nearly no bugs, acceptable balance and a very well made progression system.  I rushed through the base game with defender gear, was easy, learned the basics then when I got bit into Iceborne I realized that I need Mantles, better gear, more consumables and generally be a better player and play smarter. I really loved this change and slowly everything went into a normal and rewarding progression loop.  Luckily the recent Flora Event quest got me basic Decorations too and soon got my mid MR Nargacuga set (https://i.imgur.com/X15V37d.png). Now stuff dies faster, I play way better than at the start, got more into multiplayer too since the stuff I'm doing now is popular and can't wait to hit endgame.  TLDR: If you can run the game at stable 60 fps with HD pack then you'll love this game.

Tuto hru jsem koupil ve slevě za pět euro a popravdě jsem od ní moc nečekal. Po prvních pěti minutách jsem věděl, že jsem udělal velice dobře.  Příběh hry se odehrává na asteroidu, kde lidé společně s mimozemskou rasou Vorus těží látku zvanou Promethium. Poté, co se mimozemská rasa proti lidem otočí a všechny je z dolu vyžene, přicházíte vy, nemilosrdný Jack, aby jste jim vysvětlili, že to nebyl dobrý nápad.  Hra je lineární akcí, kde máte k dispozici deset různých zbraní. Projdete celkem čtrnácti misemi, kde kosíte jednoho emzáka za druhým a jednou za čas svou misi zakončíte zabitím bosse, který vám chce váš postup rozmluvit svou velkou zbraní. Vše je posazeno sice do stereotipního, ale za to velice příjemného grafického prostředí.  Hra mě překvapila svou obtížností, se kterou se člověk dneska už moc často nesetká. Pokud máte rádi výzvy, můžete zkusit překonat sami sebe ve hře na skóre, které během každé mise získáváte. Větší počty bodů se připočítávají za zvolenou obtížnost, za střelbu do hlavy, za využívání výbušných zásobníků, které potkáváte všude kolem a za rychlou likvidaci nepřátel, kteří se na vás budou hnát.  Dále máte možnost získat zkušenostní body, díky kterým budete moci například zdvojnásobit počet nábojů ve vašem zásobníku, či počet nábojů, které unesete. Ve hře také můžete nalézt skryté bonusy nebo audiology, které mají jednoduchý příběh obohatit.  Ve hře je k dispozici i multiplayer, který obsahuje dva klasické módy deathmatch a team deathmatch. Bohužel, v současné době není snad nikdo, kdo by ho hrál, ovšem mě osobně to jakožto sólo hráči nevadí.  Pokud máte rádi odreagování s trochou té výzvy, je tahle hra to pravé. Za mě 7/10.

ALIEN ISOLATION  Most of the game isn't too hard, as it plays on my honed skills of social avoidance. Imagine that you are Ripley, a 20 yo college student who shares a house with some people. You are an introvert and like to avoid conversations every time you want food. So you start listening to the old house you share, learning the patterns of your roommates and where to hide to avoid contact. That is this game. Honestly, the alien is quite pleasant to live with in comparison. There's only one, and it'll stomp around and make itself known like an angry upstairs neighbor. This thought also makes the games more humorous than scary, as you play hide and seek, or use noisemakers to direct the alien to the human hunting parties. Fetch boy.  Weird spikes in difficulty annoyed me early on, as you lack most devices for distraction, offense, or even knowing where to go next. Even when you get the motion tracker that points you in the correct direction, the game drags on longer than it should. You keep having to do nested sidequests to move on. You want to leave the station, but your friend is hurt so you need a med pack, so you need to go to the hospital, but you need to find a keycard and password  to open the door, so you must restore the power, but the facility catches fire and you need to escape. The game is about the journey more than the destination, and I enjoyed the details to the sound (7.1 headphones helped track), and the retrofuture design of the technology. It captures the thrill of the original Alien, the stalking and evasion.  Now some hate. Worthless fucking character development and npcs. Half attack on site, the other half fail the game if you do the same to them. Why would I want to read another person's emails while an alien is stalking me? Reading my own is tedious enough.  Most of the game time is searching for the one thing in the environment that advances the plot. Can't find the plasma torch on the dead guy in the corner after 5 rounds on the area? Fuck you. Trouble finding the 3 small green lights that lock the area down for an alien trap. Do it anyways, Marco or whoever mucks it up anyway. All this backtracking and walking mocks my precious free time.  I started sprinting around and then giving the Alien a flame bath whenever he wanted a hug. Then I'd go to use a terminal and helplessly mash B to abort the uninterruptible 10 second log on time, while Alien had the chances to drop from the vent, scan the area, kill me, have tea, file his taxes, and kill me again.  The enjoyable bits of terror you get from hiding in the cupboards is quickly diluted by repetition, since the game dynamics remain the same for the nearly 25 hour journey. The save system magnifies these issues when they can literally be 20 min apart in an area where death is common.   Kevin Vanord's review on Gamespot mirrors my sentiments.

Thomas Was Alone is a puzzle platformer that shows off how good platforming games can be in the present day. You start out the game playing Thomas, a red rectangle, and as you progress through the stages you will meet many different characters, which you can also play. These different characters all have names and their own special ability that makes them all an integral part of the game.   The story of Thomas Was Alone is told by a narrator, his voice soothes you and this gives the game a lot of feelings. You wouldn't think you would grow any kind of attachment to simple shapes, but you do. The narration can be quite funny at times, and the fourth wall is often broken on several occasions.   I really like the art style in TOA, it's simple, yet it has that really polished feel to it. Like with most platformers, it's not exactly graphically intensive, but it still represents a pretty looking game.   Each level consist of a number of puzzles and jumping challenges to make, you have to make use of all the characters in each stage in order to progress, and often in some levels, there are more than one way to complete them, leaving you room to experiment with different methods. The difficulty of Thomas Was Alone is quite high once you reach the half way point, often at times I had to revert to a FAQ in order to figure out how to progress.   I finished Thomas Was Alone in seven hours, which is quite long for a platformer; there are also additional challenges, which involve getting to difficult to reach places that will let you squeeze a little bit out of replay-ability the game. Unfortunately though, once you've had one play through, there's not much else to see and you won't need to boot it up again.   My conclusion is that Thomas Was Alone must be in your library as it's one of, if not the best platforming experience you will have   If you found this review helpful, please consider giving it a thumbs up. This game is Fantastic. However be warned! This game is hard, with a steep learning curve and you'll die a lot. If you enjoy a challenge, enjoy survival, teamwork, and are willing to do some very light RP, then this game is an absolute gem.   With that said, here's a few tips for you if you do purchase the game.  1. Pay attention in the Tutorial! Actually try and learn the stuff the tutorial teaches you. I went through the tutorial, doing the things asked of me once, then dived into the game and was overwhelmed, and the things I'd just done in the tutorial  fled from my mind.  So take some extra time to really figure things out and do them a few times.   2. When starting out don't be an Eve. If you spawn alone in the wilderness as a woman, just die. It's a lot easier when just learning the game to play with other people than it is to try and build your own civilization from the get go.   3. As a baby type 'F' when you drop down to 2 boxes of hunger remaining.  When your mom breast feeds you it takes some of her nourishment to do it, so the F method not only saves her time and ensures you live, but it also lets your mom do stuff nearby while you're a baby, rather than just standing beside you all the time.  3b. Temperature matters. If you're very hot or cold, you get hungry faster, so especially as a baby try to stand somewhere with a balanced temperature so your mom doesn't have to work as hard!  4. Focus on one task at first. Starting out you'll probably be relegated as a newbie to gathering soil, putting the soil on the farm plants, and fetching water for the plants. It sounds boring, but do it! While you're still relatively useless you'll at least be earning your keep and not just being a drain on resources. If you go out for soil and water, that's also an opportunity for you to learn to navigate the map, and learn to manage your hunger.  Don't get upset if you starve a lot at first, that's pretty normal when you're still learning, especially if you forget to watch your temperature.   5. If you want to learn something else, ask someone! Want to learn new crops? Ask! Want to learn smithing? Ask! Cooking? Ask! Hunting...ask! Seriously, while this game has a recipe feature built in, you'll learn much more effectively by just talking and watching and learning from people.   6. Don't be afraid to get invested. Call your mom, 'mom'. If you have kids treat them as if they're actually your kids when you talk to them. It seems silly, but each of your lives feel a lot more rewarding and meaningful when you're actually connecting with the other people in your community.   7. Be careful with bows and knives. It's very easy to kill someone with a bow or knife, so don't just walk around with them in your hand! Also if you see someone with a bow or knife, and they're killing people, don't stand still. If you're constantly moving, they're going to find it almost impossible to stab or shoot you, so you'll remain safe from their griefing.   8. If you don't know what needs doing, ask! Ask someone what needs to be done, ask if they need help, or just ask for someone to teach you their job. Everyone lives only an hour at most, so usually people are pretty happy to train someone to eventually take their place.  9. Consider getting the mod 'One Life+'. The mod is pretty useful since it not only lets you see your age, and some basic info about your family's fertility, but it also has a feature to let you zoom out the map. Some people dislike that and consider it cheating, but I think zooming out is a great help to new players, and once you get used to the game, even if you never use the zoom, knowing your age and about your family fertility can be pretty useful.

Sam & Max Season 1, aka Save the World for the console players, is a classic Telltale episodic adventure from the golden age of Telltale, back when they were just starting out. It follows Sam, the straight man 6 ft talking dog, and Max, the hyper-kinetic rabbit-thing, members of the morally ambiguous, yet still somewhat heroic, Freelance Police, who end up wrapped in 6 interconnected case involving hypnosis that leads them to have to save the world. Now, it's been lovely remastered by Skunkape games, made up of ex-Telltale employees following the company's bankruptcy, and has bundled all 6 episodes into one game with updated graphics, textures, character models, & audio, including new character models, new music, and new camera positions. In short, it's a label of love, and if you had the chance to play the original season 1, you'll love the remaster. (side note, on their website, Skunkape games also have grayed out titles for Sam & Max Beyond Time and Space and The Devil's Playhouse, seasons 2 & 3 respectively, and their name, Skunkape, is a major character in the third season, so don't let this single remaster fool you, chances are more Sam & Max is on its way!)

[h1] 新手建议 [/h1] 摸索了一段时间，基本玩法算是有所了解。本游戏上手过程可能比长，引导教程也存在bug，导致人摸不着头脑。不过学会以下几点就基本可以深入探索下去了： 1. 开船基本操作（飞行、战斗），具体参见教程 2. 船的4种模式：  2.1. 巡航：这个教程说的比较清楚  2.2. 扫描：开启后   2.2.1. 可显示附近小行星中矿产情况   2.2.2. 任意空间站近距离移动可解锁空间站扫描进度   2.2.3. 接收空间站数据泄漏点发出的广播噪音，船头近距离指向这些数据泄漏点可以出现一些任务  2.3. 长距扫描，开启后对准一个方向按住r键，并在一定时间放开飞船将发出一道可见波，扫到的物体屏幕会有所提示并在地图显示扫到的未知空间站和未知物体  2.4. seta，开启后会加速游戏（教程说的比较清楚），脸黑的我刷了几天才凑齐所有制作材料 3. 手动降落，上下左右前后调整，标示全绿才能降落成功，有钱买一个辅助降落mk2就不用手动操作了 4. 和空间站交易，各个工厂是不出售原材料的，通过扫描模式扫描可以弄清工厂的生产链 5. 物品制作，有些物品是需要制作的，工作台在每个空间站的交易大厅 6. 飞船改装，飞船经销商处有工作台允许进行飞船改装 7. HQ任务，可自行百度 8. 空间站建设（具体可参考教程）  8.1. 空间站建材仓和贸易仓是有区别的，材料放到建材仓才行  8.2. 模块允许重叠  8.3. 模块放出来后点击选择，使用左键可进行拖拽，使用右键可进行旋转（只能左右旋转，无法上下旋转） 9. m键调出地图，右边有地图过滤器，可分别显示地图不同信息 10. 没摸清楚不同类型任务具体是什么流程前做任务时一定多保存，不然会后悔的 11. 买船（参考教程） 12. 自己其他飞船的控制（尤其是行为设置）  [h1] 个人心得 [/h1] 1. 做任务攒钱，攒够了就购买矿船，并指派矿船挖矿继续攒钱。感觉差不多就买商船并指派贸易 2. 刷ARG声望到20，解锁主力战舰。记得加入argon vs 圣教团的势力任务，其中有一类集结舰队的任务，要求提供一艘XL、一艘L、3艘M，一般需要花费2千万左右，任务奖励基本在5千万左右。可以靠这个任务攒钱。 3. 攒够钱就开船厂，我选择大批量生产日蚀 先锋型（最高配置），一艘利润大概在70万左右（这里认为飞船生产材料均为采购所得，如果自行生产利润更高） 4. 本作产品线比较单一，产品消费的核心是围绕生产飞船展开的（说一句题外话，我接触的游戏中生产线最复杂的是异星工厂，那真是令人头秃）。我建厂方案有三个阶段：1）基础原料处理工厂；2）配件工厂；3）船厂  4.1. 最基础的能量电池，每个工厂只要安装其生产线就完全足够  4.2. 基础原料处理工厂。本游戏基础原料只有五种：甲烷 --> 石墨、氦 --> 超流体冷却剂、氢 --> 反物质单元、金属矿石 --> 精炼金属、硅 --> 硅晶片  4.3. 配件工厂。基础核心配件有三种：微芯片、量子管、等离子导体，这三种生产模块投产后可在此基础上加入进一步加工生产的配件生产线，这些配件有：纳米计算机（只用于空间站建设）、船体部件（消耗量最大）、引擎部件、反物质转换器、先进电子设备、武器部件、炮塔部件、励磁线圈、护盾部件、扫描部件  4.4. 和无人机相关的有两条：无人机部件、智能芯片  4.5. 从材料到飞船到装备满足s船生产的全套蓝图估计在3到4亿，不过船厂建好后基本可以躺着赚钱了 5. 后续的大舰队战斗什么的我也还在摸索，以上流程估计跑个几天就能实现躺着赚钱。

Voici comment faire;  -Ouvrez vos documents --Dossier - Mount and Blade II Bannerlord --- Dossier- Configs ---- Engine_config (ouvrir avec bloc note par exemple) Cherchez le - cheat_mode = 0 dans la liste et ne changez que la valeur de = 0 pour 1.  Sauvegarder et fermé - Voilà les cheats dans le jeu sont activé. Il y a des listes de façons pour les utilisés sur le web, a noté que ce sont les mêmes que dans Warband.  Les - (J'ai retiré les bugs qui ont été corrigé par les patch et les hotfix) L'Optimisation est un peu désastreuse par moment... Certaines villes vont mettre votre CPU et votre GPU en sang et vos images par seconde vont tomber entre 0 et 5 et dans certaines villes plus grosses et plus détaillée vous aurez 60 Fps. A vast improvement over Assassin's Creed 3 in every term imaginable, Black Flag is at least my second favorite Assassin's Creed game, my favorite ocean game, and might even be up there among my favorite games. If you take the time to complete all the side missions and collectibles this game will last you well over 50 hours, but it has at least a 12 hour campaign if you want to rush straight through the story. You can also skip the credits! FINALLY.  The missions tend to get a little repetitive, and so does doing everything else that is so much fun in Black Flag from whaling to boarding ships, but by the time it really starts to grind on you is when the last upgrade is gained or the final collectible collected. This game goes a little overboard with the tailing missions, something I wish games on a whole would do completely away with, but they're manageable even if they artifiically increase the length of the game by making you follow some stupid Templar for what feels like 10 minutes.  The story is a lot easier to follow than Assasin's Creed 3, and doesn't have nearly as much of a dual-story as the previous Creed games did since you spend well over 90% of your time playing as a pirate instead of bounding around in the real world. Unfortunately this also means the real-world story hardly advances, and the characters we knew from the previous games get so little game time it makes you wonder why they were in it to begin with.  Black Flag is also the only Assassin's Creed game I could recommend playing entirely on its own with no interest in the rest of the series. It does a great job being a pirate game where you get to pirate other pirates, but still feels like Assassin's Creed.

Life is strange is an interesting take on what some would call a walking simulator.    Arsty, almost hipsterish, the game certainly has its own personal feel  If the above makes you gag, let me allievate that for you. Life is Strange is partially gameified narrative. There is a story, and there are 'choices' but overall the narrative remains what it is.  You control minor aspects, but are mostly a free camera to walk about environments and sets are the narrative plays.  If this doesnt sound like your cup of tea, it wont be.  The narrative is mostly good, save for certain points that cannot be discussed without spoiling.  The atmosphere and environments are well crafted, vibrant, and full.  The soundtrack is incredible.  There is a lot to love about this episodic game.  Speaking of episodes, I played through Life is Strange as it came out, episode by episode, having to wait between installments.  There are narrative break points, and the waiting and wondering made these powerful and exciting.  I feel that part of my enjoyment of the game, as it's so reliant on character arcs and narrative, came from the building energy and release between these waits.  Those who play the full game straight through WILL feel differently, and conceits in the story will be more obvious.  That being said, this game should be experienced.  Its somewhat quiet, mostly contemplative, and has faults, but the overall product is worthwhile and interesting.  Buy it and play it.

[h1] A charming dungeon crawler where nobody can become anybody[/h1]  Nobody saves the world is a pretty darn great Action RPG by the guys who brought you Guacamelee, Drinkbox. The hand-drawn art style oozes charm, very reminescent of games like Rogue Legacy 2 and of course their own previous games, Guacamelee 1&2.  NSTW doesn't reinvent the wheel or anything but what it executes it does pretty well for the most part.   The form switching mechanic at first seems a bit gimmicky but it does result in some pretty in depth customization where you can take skills from one class and apply them on another. This allows you to create a lot of bizarre and funny combos, like a horse using a bow or an egg leaving a trail of slime.  The writing has the right amount of funny without trying too hard which helps prop up the simple premise of the game, a calamity has befallen the world yada yada, you know the deal. The characters you'll meet are colorful individuals who have some really comical things to say. The dungeons you'll enter are procedurally generated, and for the most part seem simple enough in design, but feel very balanced. Some contain special parameters like everything can one-shot or everyone heals at the same time, which adds a nice bit of spice to the dungeon crawling. Usually it's all the standard procedure, you'll be fighting through hordes of enemies until you reach the boss room. The randomly generated nature of the dungeons almost gives the game a roguelite feel.  [b] NSTW is undoubtedly a great game, but it does have some flaws that prevents it from truly becoming an amazing game. [/b]  [*] The game is pretty grindy, as you need to fill out mini quests to level up your forms, so they get new abilities and also unlock the next forms. This makes the game feel more repetitive than it needs to be.  [*] I wished they implemented some puzzles that took advantage of the form swapping. Just something to give the dungeons a bit more identity and the forms more nuance.   [*] The bosses are just big versions of normal mobs you encounter, that's very disappointing.  [*] The controls takes some getting used too, the character only moves in a 4 direction axis, which can make it feel a bit clunky at times.  [*] The game is missing some QOL features like being able to customize the form wheel swapping, so it's not placed randomly and removing tips everytime you enter a dungeon with a class that has no quests available.  All in all, I'll still recommend the game. 2022 is off to a good start.  7.5/10

50 (!) hours later we managed to perfectly clear every stage (perfect = no damage).  This is a very simple/casual tower defense game, but as you progress through the levels, they become more challenging and by unlocking a variety of new tools to repel the hordes of (cute) enemies the game suddenly becomes an min-maxing challenge. The levels feel well thought-out although sometimes the balance leans towards specific strategies.  We played the whole game in couch-coop and it was a blast! (With some arguments here and there to spice things up!)  It is definitely worth its money, and with its deep and frequent discounts it's a no-brainer for TD fans. The couch-coop makes it even more fun!  It is far from perfect though, with some game design decisions that are clearly wrong and counter-intuitive, especially in coop mode. For example, money (coins) are not shared across the team, leading to each player having to save for a specific tool. Although this adds to the strategy, it often feels like an unneeded complication. Another weird decision was the ability to play the challenges (and thus unlock most of the achievements) only in solo mode. If the challenges could be played in coop mode, we would have easily sunk another 20 hours into the game!  Overall a fun but flawed experience but a must play for TD fans!  6/10  Recommended, grab it on one of its frequent sales!

Raft был просто создан для того, чтобы проводить за ним приятные вечера, играя в компании с другом. Вы вместе плаваете на плоту, исследуете большие водные просторы, строите, готовите, рыбачите, сражаетесь, открываете новый контент и т.д. На игру приятно взглянуть с графической стороны, геймплейно она достаточно проста в освоении, не нужно тратить десятки часов, чтобы понять принципы игры и наслаждаться ей. Да, Raft всё ещё в раннем доступе, а главы выходят раз в столетие. Тем не менее приятно видеть, что разработчики всё же уделяют ей внимание (хоть и не так часто, как хотелось бы), фиксят баги, добавляют сюжетный контент. На данный момент в игре достаточно всего, чтобы хватило провести в ней 30 часов минимум, поэтому если вы ищете что-то лёгкое и ненапряжное, где можно отдохнуть в компании после тяжёлого дня, то Raft как нельзя лучше подойдёт для этого.  P.S. Финальная обнова принесла своей душноты: нормально выбраться с Темперанс не помогут даже четыре мотора и груда вёсел, а после прыжков и препятствий на Утопии, возможно, захочется удалить игру. Но! Играть и исследовать в коопе всё ещё интересно, и игра такая же расслабляющая и чилловая, её покупка полностью себя оправдывает.  P.S.S. Также стоит отметить сломавшуюся акулу, которая теперь выгрызает части плота, следующие за его укреплённой линией, и изменившиеся вероятности дропа кладов и островов, что делает получение некоторых достижений (да отдайте вы уже этот последний фрагмент Тики, ну) просто невыполнимой задачей. Не то чтобы самый критичный аспект игры, но и не очень хорошая новость для любителей выбивать все ачивки.

Vom Aufbau des Bauernhofs, Beziehungen zwischen den Dorfbewohnern knüpfen (und sogar heiraten) bis hin zu Kämpfen gegen Monstern in einer Höhle, gibt es so viel zu entdecken. (Keep in mind, this is a buggy port. To get it working properly you will need mods.) Max Payne is such a good game with some crippling problems that really date it. The voice acting is top tier, and James McCaffrey is the biggest reason for this success and is one of the best voice actors ever. The gameplay is unqiue and so satisfying, diving through the air as the world explodes around you and bullets whiz past you. The depiction of New York as this grim, snowy, crime-ridden land fits so well with the place and the cheesiness makes this so good. But I played this on the PC port, and the game's crippling issues with the difficulty slider got annoying really quick. Walking through a door and getting insta-headshot three times and then the fourth time doing the same thing and not having it happen got annoying, and supposedly there is a major bug that makes it so the difficulty slider, which is tied to the only difficulty you can play at the start, is broken and doesn't properly balance the game. As well, some aspects feel a little too gamey in this serious tale, with a few levels sticking out like a sore thumb (the underground level). I feel enemy variety wasn't really a thing, just the same enemy that got stronger and stronger. But overall, this is a very good game with aspects that haven't ever really been replicated as well, which is a shame. We need more top-tier, slow-mo shooters.

"The Evil Within tries very hard to be Silent Hill, but plays like a Resident Evil. I know I only have six hours of play time, but hear me out. I couldn't bring myself to finish it, it was so frustrating.  Pros: -Looks great. Awesome visuals, monsters and level themes. -Sounds pretty good. Really gritty, crunchy, gut-wrenching sounds and visceral combat effects. -Story is interesting, but doesn't really hook you with anything that you want to figure out. It's more a collectible hunt than a narrative mystery. -Melee combat is hectic and satisfying, and ranged combat is kept as a last resort with limited ammo.  Cons: -The writing is medicore at best. None of the characters are interesting, the dialogue is questionable and the in-game journals look like they were written by a high-schooler. -The crossbow has an effective range of three feet. When the primary ammunition is explosive, you're usually better off firing it ahead of you and using it like a land mine. -Stealth is broken, in the sense that it only works half the time. There are several scripted encounters where the enemies will react to your presence whether or not you are sneaking, and they are surrounded by other enemies that you can sneak around. In fact, [spoiler] one enemy is laying on the ground, dead, and when you get near it, it gets up and pulls a lever, filling the hallway with spikes. It doesn't care if you're sneaking or not, it just magically knows you're there. [/spoiler] it's completely impossible to tell who will immediately attack you and who can be avoided. -Enemies are inconsisent. When you first encounter an enemy, he's invincible and it's clear you're not supposed to fight him. The next time you find him, you're supposed to fight him. Or you'll find a special monster surrounded by ammo, and it will stagger and collapse when you attack it, but it's actually invincible and you're supposed to run away. -Navigation and camera work are abysmal. I've spent more than one fight with the camera literally INSIDE my butt, and I've had to shuffle along fences trying to find a break in the invisible wall to hop over a two foot obstacle. -The ""puzzles"" are an insult to your intelligence. Skyrim had more challenging puzzles.  TL:DR -Looks good -Sounds good -Plays okay -Don't bother with the story -Worth it on sale"

I bought this game on a whim, I was looking for another age of sail game that would scratch the itch Sid Meier's Pirates left.  Now this is nothing like Sid Meier's Pirates, in fact, there's very little actual story outside of the lore of each faction.  It drops you into the random world you crate, gives you a basic tutorial on how things work, and then lets you go.    The art style is simple and beautiful, it's top down.  The controls take a bit of time to get used to, I ended up using both my mouse/keyboard and controller but it was completely playable with either.  I love the music, it's calm and relaxing but ramps up for combat.  The combat is where I feel the game falls a little flat.  It's simple, your cannons auto-fire a broadside when the enemy ships are close and you press two buttons for your special abilities.  Most of my combat ended up either sitting in one spot turning my ship to make sure I could always fire or going in a circle to keep them in line of fire.  The trading is simple as well, each town produces certain goods, and if they have an abundance, you can buy it and sell it for a profit at another town.   The quests are also very simple, they range from hunting down pirates, to building towers, settling a new town, defending a city, or bringing people or cargo to another city.  Completing quests levels up the towns which gives you access to better ships and items.    The worlds are randomly generated from a map you can design yourself if you choose, the map is broken down into sections, each section is it's own little map to be explored.  At the beginning of the game, most of these sections are controlled by pirates and you conquer them for your faction.  There are also instances that you can create.  These are simple maps where you can choose it to be all out combat or a trading/quest hub.  You can use these to get loot, money, and experience  and once they are complete, you are put back in to the regular world.  There are 4 factions you can play as, each with their own preferred ship type and bonuses.  When you create a map you can have all 4 on it, or just one, or any number in between.  Overall, I enjoy this game, it does have issues that I have listed above and the developer is active on the forums.

I've got a lot of good to say for this game! I've only played personally for a few hours but watching streamers play on Twitch and Youtube inspired me to buy it.  Basic Premise: Similar to Dead Cells in a lot of ways, except top down level design rather than a 2D platformer. It's a Rogue-lite, so expect to die a lot and be a little frustrated when you lose a really good run. Permanent upgrades between runs make the game easier over time, giving a more relaxed feel especially early during new runs.   Art: the visual art style in this game is absolutely beautiful. The vibrant colors and character design is perfect and greatly adds to the gameplay. The soundtrack is super immersive and really elevates the game to the next level.   Gameplay: Perfectly in line with the beautiful art, the gameplay is fluid and relatively intuitive. I use a controller and it feels very natural. I've been a fan of games like Dead Cells, Moonlighter, and rogue-likes such as Enter the Gungeon and Binding of Isaac in the past; all great games with plenty of replay potential. This game fits right in with those.

奶牛关原文链接：[url=https://cowlevel.net/game/zhan_shu_kuang_xiang_1_Chimera_of_Tactics_1/review/3031590]https://cowlevel.net/game/zhan_shu_kuang_xiang_1_Chimera_of_Tactics_1/review/3031590 [/url]  《战术狂想1》是一款灵魂画师开发的战棋策略游戏，开发者用简直犯规的美术、配以黄色暴力的脚本折服玩家的心灵的努力，[spoiler]令我感到异常兴奋[/spoiler]，这种自动选择玩家的开发理念可以说是非常先进。战棋策略游戏对机制、数值非常敏感，想做好需大量调教与反复考量，虽然我很喜欢《战术狂想1》兵棋推演风格[spoiler]（才不是对纸片人产生欲望了呢）[/spoiler]但仍然无法在现阶段给过高评价。  [h1]玩法介绍[/h1] [list][b]六种普通舰船[/b] [*]三种射导弹（攻击延迟、伤害高、可惜打不过海礁）、三种打炮弹（瞬发攻击、伤害较低）。 [*]两类由突击舰（一回合内可完成移动与射击两个行动，射程短，在前提供视野）、支援舰（一回合内只能移动、射击二选一，射程超远，在后打输出）、迎击舰（只能移动无法主动输出，被动迎击舰船飞弹，我不是很会用）。 [*]至于船只的输出、血量都有随机性。血量上，大体是“突击≥迎击>支援”。 [/list] [list][b]三种特殊舰船[/b] [*]“粉毛”本体是炮击支援舰，特殊能力为，在消灭一艘敌舰后可以再做一次输出或移动，担当输出carry； [*]“赤毛”本体是炮击突击舰，特殊技能是躲避一次敌方单支迎击舰的输出，血量最高（30是“粉毛”的十倍），是探路神船； [*]“黄毛”可以使攻击范围内的敌方飞弹变为我方，进行反杀，过于被动，用好不易，血量有特殊加厚也是探路党。 [/list] [list][b]接舷抢船[/b] [*]相邻敌我舰船进入接舷战，无法进行攻击，且接舷船只受到伤害减3、最低为1，接舷船只受到两次炮击仍存留，则残血跳反。接舷战是《战术狂想1》的精髓，有非常精彩的策略游戏体验，值得期待。 [/list] [list][b]打屁股[/b] [*]从舰船后方攻击将多造成三点伤害，“粉毛”更是无视节操直接击毁敌舰。不过，绕后敌人真的很难，所以还是请多注意自己的菊花吧。 [/list] [h1]缺点[/h1] [olist] [*][b]优化上存在问题，bug还是比较多，影响游戏体验[/b]。我发现并记住的有， [list][*]炮击支援舰会出现射程内无法射击 [*]上下左右浏览地图，会发生不规则的卡顿、锁死，流畅感糟糕 [*]会出现地图bug导致战舰无法正常移动 [*]经常有无法使敌舰跳反的bug [*]开始画面卡顿（很“正常”地卡三下） [*]一次，我的导弹支援舰一发干掉自己的炮击突击舰[strike]，希望有“海盗法庭系统”[/strike][/list]  [*]游戏难度较大，虽然开发者总多送我“几条船”，但仍是[b]用手走在悬崖边上的感觉[/b]。 [list][*]首先，各种舰船的初始数量分配就是随机的。而在我卡住的第五关，非常需要远程炮舰来去清理礁石林中的敌舰，但是除去“粉毛”，游戏随机给0~2艘，且0艘居多，这样我就[b]会一直roll[/b]。实际上，我更想有些自己选择战舰种类的余地。（比如先随机20艘，再叫玩家自己排除3艘就会有改善） [*]游戏平衡性值得怀疑。尽管我拥有了3艘远程炮舰（就一次）虽然非常接近但仍然无法通关。其中固然有我的“蠢”，但十几二十次的重复努力，后面基本都在[b]背板修正，这损害了策略的初衷[/b]。 （如果实际上是我有策略问题，还请多多指教。[b]最好是开发者能提供一份攻略，告诉每一关背后的战术选择[/b]，就比如第四关直冲敌营中心就算是战术有效）[/list]  [*]整体质量简陋，不仅仅是画风。明显感到开发者做这款游戏，最多是练练手，基本是个人爱好，定价也是steam的最低有价定价，有些地方太过“人不可貌相、海水不可斗量”，当然这个问题并不是首先要在意。 [list] [*][b]没有总菜单[/b]，进去就是上次的游戏进度，Esc才有教程、重来、退出、音量、取消、语言选择。“麻雀虽小五脏俱全”，但[b]关卡选择也还是省略掉了[/b]。这或许可以作为设计本身，但总体感受就是开发者不太会做这些。 [*]灵魂画师我并不很反感，风格化的东西总是因人而异，音乐、音效我也很认可，别管是不是免费音源，效果还是和整体风格很搭的。[b]比较注重精致感官体验的玩家，被封面筛选的会很干净[/b]，不成为实际玩家的扣分项，但这种质量影响游戏走向更多人。[/list] [/olist] [h1]游戏的优点[/h1] [list]我只说一条，那就是[b]实际玩家的惊喜感[/b]。  [*]在挑选评测游戏的时候，这么魔性的封面导致游戏自然是那种“从垃圾桶里找出来的方案”，看到好评还挺多的，加之介绍动画音乐带感，缘分就来了。 [*]进入游戏，徒穷四壁、筚路蓝缕，我也很懵逼该怎么玩，结果发现竟然有教学，并且清晰可懂、简单明了，很开心。 [*]游戏过程，不仅有[url=https://tieba.baidu.com/p/2088254465?red_tag=0470854151]羊刁习[/url]式画风，还有很骚气的剧情，兵棋推演风格的棋盘与战舰数值界面很干净，不错，我喜欢。 [*]对“接舷抢船”的玩法，非常钦佩，尤其是第四关的通关体验将这种情绪带到高潮，但第五关的无限背板，又把我从狂想拉回现实。 [*][b]简陋外观与丰富内涵的冲突，带给玩家很大的惊喜，虽然开发者很有天赋，但经验不足与能力有限，导致这款游戏有潜力但还不够好，很期待开发者未来的努力。[/b] [/list] [h1]总结[/h1] 很高兴能玩到这么具有个性、想法的策略游戏，毕竟，一位P社劝退的玩家又能玩战棋策略了，非常开心呢~作为个人是非常想安利这款有味道的游戏，但如果是更客观的评价则没有那么好看。希望开发者能有更好的机会，来推出新作。画风、菜单倒不是最首要的，[b]优化、平衡性多加打磨，游戏策略性想办法用地图、数值来突出一下[/b]，祝愿SLG的明天会有“战术狂想”的一个位置~

父亲在很久以前就去世了，到如今我已很难回忆起他的面容。  记得在我刚上大学不久的时候，某天下午我在寢室里睡得很沉。   梦中，我和父亲像从前那样并排走在街上，深夜的街道除了我们以外空无一人。   我们边走边聊，莫名的开心。   走到一半的时候，我正在说笑，抬起头却忽然发现他已经不见踪影，瞬间心里涌起一阵阵难过，但并没有回身去找。 不知为什么，就是潜意识里觉得他不会回来了。   于是我沿着街继续走，不久遇见了表姐，她很开心，说晚上要带我开车去喝酒。   我的心情顿时好转了，上车后和她听着音乐聊了很多事。我一路哼着歌，哼着那首从童年的磁带里听到的《yesterday once more》。但那是在很多年以后，我才知道这首歌的名字。也是在更多年以后，我才体会到歌中的伤感。  车终于开到了酒吧门口，我很开心的下车。但下车后才发现，那家酒吧竟然已经歇业了。   于是心又沉到了谷底。   不是因为故去的人，也不是因为没喝到的酒，就是单纯地觉得许多种爱与失望的故事都再也无法挽回了。   我已经记不清父亲的脸，也许以后也将记不起他的名字（如果我能老成那副样子的话）。  逐渐消失的记忆带走了所有的生机，我两手空空地站在时光的对面，只剩下一具躯壳。  很多年以后的今天，我偶然看见了这款游戏。  《CS》，它一直躲在时光的角落里。那时候，许多被遗忘的记忆又重新在我心底翻涌。  恍惚间，我仿佛又回到了父亲带我打游戏的那个下午。键盘上，按下的是我稚嫩的手指。RUSH B的路上，我的身后又重新浮现起一个高大的影子。

Pros : - Nice looking world. - Very nice music. For me the best part of this game. - Cookie cutter story (but good for a MMO) and good story telling. After ARR that is. ARR can use an editor to get rid of all the pointless filler fluff.  - Interesting job system. - Glamour system. - Gathering. It is better than the classic node system for sure. I am trying really hard here to name some positive things :/  Meh's : - Not much variety to level a second job, which can be quite boring. - World building. Lot of invisible borders. - FATE's. One of the more simple versions of event systems. - Housing. Limited for reasons that don't hold up anymore today. And for some reason they can't even copy full functionality of an inn room to a private room of a house.  - Crafting. Interesting crafting mechanics, but let down with aweful retainer inventory system and most of crafting is quite useless. But I guess it is good enough for people who like to complete things. This is a problem with themepark MMO's in general tbf. - Retainer job system. This would've been a pro if the retainer interface wasn't so clunky.  - Combat. Tab target with heavy reliance on rotations. No class customisation. Slow cooldown. This is another thing that feels very outdated. It is as if they looked at Everquest as example. This is a con for me, but I realise now that some ppl just want buttons to click in a predictable order.   Con's: - All features are gated behind main story. Which is especially jarring between ARR and first expansion. Where it just feels as if your progression is stalled for an unknown time. I've never experienced anything like this in a MMORPG.   - Alt unfriendly. Can't mail to your alt, can't share housing rights, no shared unlocks except for veteran status, which is an account thing.  - Ingame catering to fanservice. To be fair, FF lore is already a weird mix of sci-fi and fantasy and real world history/culture , so I guess maybe those cross overs won't stand out too much?  - Retainer inventory system. Pointless dialogue that you can't skip. Can't craft from retainer inventory. I really want to kill those npcs. Let me do that and I move it up to Meh category.  - FATE's , this time in Con category, for the moment when you become very bored with them because they are all the same.  - Class design. Without the nice looking special effects, you are left with a 'more is better' rotation design and no depth.  - NPC interaction in general. This is ridiculously outdated. I am fine with reading a lot of text. But not if it comes with a sentence at a time with each click.   If you don't care for anime of FF franchise, this MMORPG is quite average. There is nothing innovative about it and combat feels very outdated. It lacks all the QoL improvements that you find in other popular MMORPGs.  I can't recommend it to myself. Some of my friends like it. So, when do we get  a 'meh' button? Without one, I have to give it a thumbs down. Can't wait to see how many call this review not useful. Critics should be burned, right? :p

É um ótimo jogo, se tornou facilmente meu favorito até o momento. O jogo conta com um realismo e veracidade de fatos historicos, as armas, armaduras, rotinas e tudo de forma muito boa, apesar de Henry nunca ter existido na vida real (obviamente). Além de tudo isso o jogo é ótimo como RPG fornecendo o aumento de nivel de habilidades separadamente (O nivel de espada é diferente do de alquimia por exemplo) alem de ter diversas armaduras e um combate desafiador e diversificado. As missões tambem contam com diversas formas de resolução dependendo dos seus niveis em cada atributo para ver o jeito como você aborda o personagem, mas se você escolher errado pode ser uma falha. Existem muitas missões secundarias no jogo que tem uma história profunda e todos os personagens tem uma dublagem. Os graficos são ótimos tambem e a aparencia do personagem pode ser modificada com poucas moedas (apesar de não ter muitas mudanças de aparencia possiveis podendo mudar apenas o cabelo e barba do personagem) alem do jogo contar com mods que podem diversificar ainda mais a sua experiencia, os mods não são oficiais mas podem ser facilmente baixados sem que você precise de conhecimentos avançados de tecnologia e computadores. Quanto aos erros do jogo, são muito poucos, ele tem alguns erros em por exemplo no começo Henry usar as mãos nuas na fabricação da espada e flechas de fogo sendo usadas em campos abertos, mas tem erros mais graves como o sistema de salvamento do jogo que muitas vezes não salva automaticamente e o jogo tambem pode fechar sozinho dependendo do seu computador (ele roda muito bem em computadores mais lentos mas pode ter esse erro) e essa combinação pode ser perigosa ao jogo, então recomendo que você carregue consigo muitas poções de salvamento para que possa salvar uma vez a cada 30 20 ou 10 minutos pelo menos.  Obs: se vc jogar o jogo e gostar tente aproveitar ele no modo hardcore depois comece a tentar variar seu estilo de gameplay, isso pode ajudar muito você a se divertir por mais tempo nele  Obs2: Se quiser compre as DLC's elas valem muito a pena, contam mais conteudo para o jogo e te ajudam muito

Clandestine: ~~~~~~~~~~    It is 1996 and the cold war ended five years ago. Strangely, veterans from both the CIA and FSB are rapidly being found permanently terminated under rather curious circumstances. This prompts both agencies to create a new bureau in the attempt to find out who is behind this trail of eradicated veteran operatives!  Clandestine is a stealth/action/hacking type of game where you play a team of two, shall we say two newbies promoted to the arena of super spies. You will play Katya Kozlova and Martin Symborsky, Katya will be the field operative with a very light armoury (a PKK and her hand to hand combat ability) and will need to rely on stealth. Martin will be in the van hacking computer systems and taking control of camera surveillances to help her through each level.   I really enjoy the way you can quickly change from a 3rd person view (Katya) to the hacking control system (Martin) by pressing one button. Essentially, the hacking system is divided in four on your screen: The first part is the console which will show you dialogue and objectives; the second one is the camera feeds where you can take control of a specific camera and study the area around it (enemy movements) or going through undetected; The third is the network view, the hacking system, this is where you send your Node to bypass firewalls, take over computers and even surcharge electric boxes to create an explosion. Time it when a foe is next to it and you will take him down. The fourth is the tactical view which will give you the layout of the level as well as show you where the cameras and computers are placed.  On the solo mode, you can choose from four levels of difficulty. They have put a bit of humour here where the easy level is Bond (007) and the extra hard level is Leon. Also, make sure you gather Intel’s as you will get additional points at the end of the mission for doing so. There is a Co-op mode if you like to play with one of your friend.  Graphics are average but that should not bother you if you like to play a great stealth game. Voice over could have been better too but the controls are good and easy to learn.  Positives: ~~~~~~~   -	Solid stealth game with hacking concept -	Controls are easy to learn -	Solo and co-op mode -	Achievements & Trading cards  Negatives: ~~~~~~~~    -	Average graphics -	Voice over could have been better  This is a really solid stealth/action game with an excellent hacking phase which made it really fun to play.   8/10  Key provided by developer/publisher for review purposes. McPixel is pretty short but quite funny if you enjoy raunchy nonsense.  Definitely not everyone's sense of humour but I can't imagine anyone being that upset about the price tag. That is, if it were on sale. I believe the regular price on this game is $5 at the moment  and if you want to support the developer that's your prerogative. My advice would be to spend less than that on it though.  Each level is a different scenario that puts the responsibility of preventing an explosive from detonating (or equivalent disaster). A mouse only game, you click on one of the various items in the scenario, McPixel interacts with it, and you hope for the best. The humour usually lies in what happens if McPixel DOESN'T prevent the disaster.  There are several levels to play through and in each one two endings to aim for, either a win or specifically funny outcome. The whole game can be completed in a relatively short sitting, maybe 3 hours of straight play. I wouldn't recommend this though since the quickly moving and sometimes flashing backgrounds can be hard on the eyes. The music can also become grating since it repeats mostly the same one track. A saving grace may be that the first time you hear that track you will probably like it.  In summation it is a fun experience and I would recommend this to a friend who isn't offended by the idea of a man pleasuring a giraffe to completion. Still, the $5 price tag may cause buyers remorse especially if you don't smile at the idea of manual giraffe gratification. Buy it for less.

It has been at least 6 years and this unique, underrated gem is still getting updated with new, meaningful content every couple of months. Strong recommend, every single second of the 42 hours spent was well worth it, and with new features on the way I absolutely need to spend more time on it.  Basically, you buld a 2d pixelated blimp or plane. Or a tank. Or a literal fortress. Or literally whatever you want, really. No naval vessels at the moment, unfortunately. There's tons of components to put in your designs with varying levels of complexity, enough that making a good airship is difficult but not nearly as complicated as other design-your-craft games (such as From the Depths). There's also a ton of decorative objects to give your crafts an actual look and feel to them, instead of just being boxy death machines.   The campaign mode is good for introducing players to the features of the game as a curve, with an easy to understand tech tree, and just got updated with a bunch of amazing new features. Sandbox is where you can test your designs and have fun simply watching things burn, and with workshop support, you basically have infinite replayability regardless what you play the game for.  The only downside is the multiplayer isn't always super populated. There's often a few people playing, but I personally have never seen the game above ~20 people online and playing multiplayer at a time. Maybe the new update changes that, though.

Not even playing games on the ol' BoobTube, just sitting there and looking around at the walls, the games on the shelves, back when owning a game meant it was yours. Back before everything became disposable. Have you seen that commercial where they break the TV and just order a new one, back then you could just hire someone to fix it, you could learn how these things worked. Hell, most CRT-TVs still function, they were built sturdy, to last. Things were so different back then, when people would argue which console was best. The whole Sega VS Nintendo debate people occasionally nostalgia over, I didn't care, I had cool games on my Sega Genesis, and my relatives had cool games on their NES/SNES. I'm not going to pretend that this was the intent, nor will I assume everyone will experience that, so I won't recommend this at all just for that alone. I liked this story a lot. I felt that the usage of basically a single room to tell a complex love story between two extremely well realised adult characters was very economical and gave it a real sense of place and purpose that's missing from a lot of longer visual novels. The palace and what it represents to both Liliane and Marius felt like as much as a character as they did themselves.  Presentation is great. Art and music are consistently beautiful throughout. If I have one small quibble it's that the CG art doesn't quite match how Liliane is described. Anyone who has seen the climactic romance scene can probably guess what I'm talking about.  Stories that focus on Marie Antoinette as a tragic figure who was unfairly vilified are nothing new, but the effort went to distancing Liliane from her historical counterpart really helped sell her story as something fresh and original while still paying homage to the inspiration and challenging the reader about their preconceived notions on women who have been unfairly treated by history.  While I did enjoy the last, and I would assume true, end, my favourite has to be the title drop ending. It was very true to Liliane's character as I read her, and the final CG is incredibly striking.  I would recommend this game to anyone interested in a drama about star-crossed lovers, but also more generally anyone looking for a short digestible story bursting with colourful prose and strong characterisation. You really can't go wrong here.

Now this game is a bit of a weird one. Ill make this short and comprehensive for everyone who wants a quick opinion. Im just going to say, If I could describe this game in one word it would be empty. I have played 112 hours now and I feel I have seen everything there is to see. Its empty, its boring, and its tedious, but man does it do a few things right. Immersion is something that shines here. Theres no game that makes me feel more like I am in a spaceship than this game. If you like euro truck sim, then I could see you liking this game due to its large number of missions involving taking something from point A to point B. It is very relaxing and it makes the combat quite tense how little it comes up but it doesnt cure the fact that this is an empty game that needs more content to hold my attention. The visuals are stunning and the physics are very well done making you feel like you are actually driving something with some weight. There are some small touches I find amazing that I would like to see more of, such as the fact that putting on the autodock feature plays orchestral music for a hint of comedy in this serious adventure through space. This game is amazing when it comes to the immersion it offers but I cannot reccomend it unless you are looking for a very relaxing space trucking adventure with the occasional battle. The variety is here but I still find the world to feel empty and lackluster. Call me when I can leave my damn cockpit.

Space Pilgrim Episode I: Alpha Centauri é uma aventura espacial cativante que mergulha os jogadores em uma emocionante jornada intergaláctica. A história acompanha a protagonista Gail Pilgrim, uma piloto espacial, em sua busca para encontrar um planeta habitável para a humanidade.  O jogo oferece uma narrativa envolvente, com diálogos bem escritos e personagens interessantes. A atmosfera espacial é bem representada, com visuais adequados e uma trilha sonora imersiva. A jogabilidade é baseada em apontar e clicar, permitindo que os jogadores explorem ambientes, resolvam quebra-cabeças e interajam com outros personagens.  No entanto, é importante observar que o jogo é curto em duração, o que pode deixar alguns jogadores desejando por mais conteúdo. Além disso, a jogabilidade pode ser considerada simplista para os jogadores mais acostumados com desafios complexos.  No geral, Space Pilgrim Episode I: Alpha Centauri é uma introdução promissora a uma série de jogos de aventura espacial. Se você gosta de histórias envolventes no espaço e jogabilidade relaxante, este jogo pode ser uma ótima escolha.

《Punch Line》是一款带有喜剧色彩的角色扮演游戏，虽说是角色扮演游戏，但实质上游戏更加接近于视觉小说作品。玩家扮演一名在一次意外事故之中身体被别人占领的“少年”，成为了幽体这种不科学的存在，在一只不靠谱的幽灵猫的引导之下，开始了在所住公寓古来馆的冒险之旅。游戏中一个非常有趣的设定就是，当主角见到女性的胖次时，就会触发超能力，将外太空中一颗名为小学生的陨石拉向地球，让地球灭亡。    [h1] 游戏玩法[/h1]  游戏中的一切玩法都围绕着惊爆点这一名词展开。何为惊爆点，这就涉及到游戏中的一个设定，正常情况下，幽灵或者幽体是触碰不到现实之中的物品，除非幽灵的能量等级足够高，或者有相应的媒介，才能触碰到。至于如何提升能量等级，当幽灵或者幽体惊吓到正常人类，并且惊吓等级到达惊爆点时，会从人类身上获取到能量，这些能量能够提升幽灵或者幽体的能量等级，越大的惊吓，就能获得越多的能量。  玩家最开始就需要在房间内的各个物品中选择一些能够让普通人获得足够惊吓的物品，并干扰它，就能获得能量。但由于能量等级的问题，能够干扰的次数并不算很多，如果用完这些次数，还没有达成目的，游戏中就会出现各种情况，让主角看到胖次，让世界毁灭重来，没错，就算是变成了幽体，看到胖次还是会触发超能力，因此我从头到尾看了不下几十次世界毁灭，好在游戏中的对话与场景都能加速或者跳过，虽然开始因为不知道有这功能看了好多次，后面倒是没看多少。  随着剧情的推进，玩家不仅仅只需要通过惊吓就能解决问题，还需要在不同的房间之间，通过惊吓达成连锁，才能通关。比如说玩家首先需要在A房间惊吓A的主人，让其带上某个物品，然后再在B房间弄出动静，吸引A的主人前往，最后在B里将该物品释放等等。虽然每个房间的物品并不算很多，但想要一个个试过来还是相当花费时间的，特别是如果要达成连锁，还需要用特定的顺序触碰物品，一旦失败，就要看一次世界毁灭，还是相当花费时间的。如果你只想看剧情，可以看看这个[url=https://www.ps4pro.jp/entry/2017/02/03/233000] 图文攻略[/url]，虽然因为是PS4版本的可能有一点出入，不过在大致上还是差不多的。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1756934099     [h1] 游戏剧情[/h1]  其实在很久以前，该游戏的动漫刚刚推出，也就是2015年的时候，我就已经将整部番剧完全看完了，当时可以说是惊为天人。可惜的是，这部番剧在当时并没有掀起什么火花，可能是因为开头比较无力的原因，也可能是因为其他原因，就连我安利我的朋友，也没有什么人能够坚持下去。没想到在这么久之后，还能在steam上看到他的身影。  本来这部作品的最大亮点就在于低开高走，以及结局的超大反转，我以为本作应该也逃不出这个圈圈。但没想到的是，游戏与番剧在结局上，甚至在一些细节处理之上，还是有着非常大的不同的。所以说，即使你看过本作番剧，也不用担心，本作会给你带来别样的感动。  游戏中的剧情主要靠着主角在幽体状态下的时间穿越能力，因为幽灵类生物能够较为简易地操控时间，在时间的长流之中自由跳动，除非出现一些较为特殊的状况。也就是靠着这个能力，地球才能一次一次地避免遭受毁灭。但在本作之中，时间穿越与普通的时间穿越有点不同，普通的作品之中，穿越到过去，改变过去，会导致未来也发生改变，而本作之中，穿越回过去，只会创造出一个改变之后的世界，这听起来有点像最近看的《复仇者联盟4》中的时间穿越理念。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1756934058    [h1] 画面和配音[/h1]  作为一款曾经的福利动漫，在游戏中也同样福利满满，在其他作品中藏着掖着不让你看的胖次，在本作中简直就是跳血大甩卖。各种福利场景层出不穷，但这些福利却暗藏杀机，只要你盯着胖次超过两次，就会引发世界毁灭。  游戏以动漫夹杂着游戏进行，部分剧情会以动漫形式展现在玩家眼前，虽然游戏的建模的确很不错，但很多场景之下，如果继续对话，游戏中的角色都会重复同一个动作，显得有点尴尬。  至于我为什么要写配音，那当然是因为本作中的合法萝莉居然是钉宫配的音，特别还是带有大阪特色的地方口音，简直可爱到爆表。当然，游戏中的其他角色配音也不错，只不过没有钉宫口音那么吸引我注意力就是了。  https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1756933981    [h1]总结[/h1]  这绝对是一款非常优秀的作品，虽然将其分为角色扮演类型有点迷，但特殊的设定，福利满满的画面与配音，低开高走的剧情，绝对是一款值得一玩的好游戏。    [quote] 我的游戏真的有那么好玩吗? The 3rd title released by Loolust. It is still a budget jigsaw puzzle game with some lewd anime art.   Unlike the previous title, 69 Yuki, there is no improvement here when compared to the 'prequel'. It is still the same jigsaw gameplay and same lack of options/variations. Also, the number of stages and amount of pieces per stage remained pretty much identical. I see this as a cost saving method to earn some profits in order to try innovating later, maybe. Since the previous one was solid enough to enjoy I will let it slide this one time. If you enjoyed any of the previous titles or simply like this type of puzzles then you might have some fun with this one as well.  Perhaps the biggest asset of this product is the art. The quality is arguably the best so far. Good amount of detail and well done colouring. There is still some simple idle character animation, just like in the previous game. Overall design stayed the same, simple and functional.  Music is ok. Not much to say about it since it's just a simple, calm melody. Fits well but you won't miss it after.  No bugs encountered.  To summarise, 3rd budget jigsaw title from this dev with basic gameplay and simple design. Art is best so far but other than that nothing changed. Still can be fun but only if you like this type and have reasonable expectations: 4.3/10

В арсенале имеется целая куча пушек разных классов и под разный темп игры.  Не все пушки одинаково эффективны и под конец прослеживаются очевидные фавориты но при желании можно лупить с чего угодно. Наличие всевозможных невероятных аугментаций и тактических примочек добавляет разнообразия в обычный топ-даун шутер. Всё это дело происходит под бодрую музыку которая не перетягивает на себя внимание и замечательно дополняет игровой процесс. В игре есть какой никакой сюжетик с простой подачей и незамысловатыми поворотами который будет подоваться в хоте дилогов с основными нпс в виде неких предысторий или рассказов ближайших планов. Есть правда в игре и минусы. Есть заметная проблема с маркером квестов он изредка будет тупить приводя в неверное место или проподая вовсе. Лечится это дело банальным перезаходом. Так же нужно смотреть на необходимый для задания уровень так как в самом начале на нас сваливают кучу квестов но некоторые вам будут не по силам из-за уровня и снаряжения, а некоторые будут просить придти в недоступную по началу локацию. I've always been a big fan of 2 major titles, Metal Gear Solid and Devil May Cry. This game takes the Devil may cry hack and slash gameplay and puts it in the metal gear universe, sounds like win win? Absolutely!!  Since the last DmC game fell flat on its face I honestly thought the fast paced over the top make you feel like the god of gaming genre was dead, this game lets you know one thing, it ain't dead, it was just resting. The good old hack and slash genre is back and blood thirsty with this title, giving the underrated Raiden near unlimited power should you be willing to master the mechanics, at first I was a little fustrated until I mastered the parry's, then it all fell into place and I'm exectuting combo after combo, this isn't a difficult game to get used to, but it can get off to a rocky start.    Gameplay is extremely smooth, Ninja running through the map reminds me of Assassins creed, effortlessly hopping and ducking past obstacles like they're nothing, this game just wants to look cool, and it works. Graphics are stunning, I can't believe this is a console title the visuals looks far too good, just see for yourself.  What's most important about a game in this genre? I'd say it's the combat, you'll be pleased to know its extremely smooth and simple, light attacks, heavy attacks, and Zandatsu, a time freezing slash the living s**t out of everything in front of you mode that you get plenty of opportunity to use. Best advice I can give, don't forget to parry!! Honestly you will find yourself underestimating what Raiden can and can't block, take an attack from a weapon the length of a house, chances are Raiden CAN block it (hope I haven't spoiled anything there). Boss fights are super over the top and will make you angry, you'll restart time after time because you'll want to turn the bosses into dust. Music is a big factor in this game and it'll only stir your anger even more, its fantastic.  This game emphasizes one thing, lots of blood and guts, cut anything, I mean ANYTHING that gets in your way with no effort, ripping out the vitals to heal your own wounds, sound nasty yet...fun? Well what are you waiting for, its time for JACK, TO LET ER' RIP!!

Short version: I give this game 7/10. Has some annoying features, but overall is an experience i enjoyed.   Pros:      Music: the simple music doesn't drown the listener in noise. Instead it focuses on melodies that allways seem to fit the mood.       Combat: All monsters are on screen, so very few of the battles are surprises, and the save points generally give these away. Meals can be eaten before difficult battles for bonuses that help make the game easier for those who are having a hard time. Combat always occurs where enemy is encountered, so the battlefield is constantly changing. The active combat+momentum system is a refreshing take on an old combat mechanic.       Loot: Get different (and more) drops based on how you defeat enemies. Detailed beastiaries make knowing how to get loot for specific crafting items much easier.       Aesthetic: Uses a cohesive art style that is unique to the game. Character portrates change with equipped items.       Lore: There is a detailed journal that you can read at your lesier to summarize where you have been, and what your current goal is. Also offers additional information on items you find/purchase on top of the flavor text on the equipment screen.   Cons:      Game Set Up: do i honestly need to input my preferences every time i start the game? Also, why is my cursor still on the screen when i start playing?       No Exit to Menu: Why can't i exit to the main menu to load a save? Why do i need to completly close the game first?      Illusion of Choice: Every decision is already made for you. No matter what you decide to do, nothing changes. Unles there is a secret ending i don't know about, your choices don't meen anything.       Flux Randomness: I typically only use abilities when i have momentum, and i still only have 4 flux abilities. 2 on one person, 1 on two others. Very rare indeed.

TLDR:   Don't hate this game for its creative or gameplay decisions. Hate it for its technical failure. In other words: this is a fun game until it stops working. All I get upon starting the game now is eternal loading. Not recommended unless the issue gets fixed.  THE FULL REVIEW (spoiler-free)    Most of you have probably already got your info on this game from Megaten youtubers, so here I will mainly touch on things they didn't, or on points I have a different view on.   THE GOOD  Story & Characters   You play as Ringo and three other party members to prevent the apocalypse in a futuristic and apparently stagnant but comfortable society. The plot has three major twists which I found engaging enough to keep me wanting to play. Ringo has a positive and playful personality, and I would love to befriend her IRL. Opinions on the other three party members vary across the playerbase, so make your own mind up. However, they still come across more alive in general than P3's cast (SEES); you can feel both the camaraderie and animosity in SH2. As for Figue, she is wife material; that is a fact!  Art Style  The game has a captivating art style and fresh character designs (within Megaten at least) and it pulls it off well.  The colours pop out very nicely in the whole game without being garish, whether it's on a bright environment like the hub worlds or sabbath attacks, or  the subtle specks of colour in the light signals and yellow lines in the dark subway tunnels. The menus are stylish but not overly so. I like the helpful skill type and weakness/resistance icons. Too bad the text is so small, and you cannot enlarge it in the config at all.  Music   Most tracks are just fine, but there are a few bangers. They are: Mansei Realm, Safehouse, Battle, Boss, Soul Matrix Boss, and the opening theme Hopeless Call. See also Soul Matrix section.   Combat   The battles are easy in random encounters, but harder during the bosses from the mid-game onwards, and hardest during risky (mauve) enemies. The latter category is used to grind for high sums of XP and money. A good balance in difficulty overall. (I played on Normal all the way.)  The main principle in SH2 is the stack and sabbath system. Strike an enemy's weakness to add one of your demons to the stack. Once all your party members have their turn, all demons from the stack you made do a free, all-out attack on the enemy. The more demons in the stack, the more damage you do. This applies only to you; the enemy does not do stacks on you.   Another important change is that aliments are now a big deal, while are buffs and debuffs less so, so you should take ailment skills, vulnerabilities and resistances seriously when making your demons and constructing your party. Learn to exploit this to your advantage and you'll have such fun!  Shield spells (as well as buffs ad debuffs) work on all allies/enemies (so, you know: properly!) which is a definite plus.  Critical hits, unfortunately, do not result in extra turns, unit later in the game as an optional, unlockable, in-game upgrade to your comp weapons.   Overall the stack and Sabbaths make for a fun combat system. I like the build-up to each sabbath with the demon silhouettes and increasingly thick mist and colours. The sabbath attack animations are thrilling and satisfying to watch. I've only ever skipped them twice out of over 100 times.  Soul Matrix   This is a semi-optional dungeon you must complete if you want to unlock more character abilities (summoner skills). Many players have complained that the Soul Matrix is the same visually and musically throughout, and while I absolutely see their point, it's not all bad. The music and atmosphere are very serene outside of battle, and I love to admire the shimmering effect on the floor or background blocks. I advise you to stop and smell the roses. Admittedly, the blocks and BG could at least have been differently coloured for each character, and maybe the hue could have changed the further you progress. Nevertheless, I'll still gladly take the Soul Matrix over Persona 3's Tartarus any day for the positives I've mentioned.  Demon Personalities   Atlus have always tried to flesh out the demons' personalities through their dialogue in the Megaten games I am aware of, and SH2 builds on this trend. The demons in SH2 have text archetypes and voice archetypes to give you an idea of their personalities. Some of the voice archetypes which stood out to me are: the Valley Girl (Mermaid, Apsaras), the cocky and mischievous male (Gremlin, Andras, Cu Chulain), gay male (Mokoi, Mothman), caring older sister or governess (Silky, Valkyrie) and scumbag male (Pazuzu). They did interesting things with Mothman and Pazuz. Info on them below in their own sections.  Unfortunately, these are for flavour only. The excellent demon loyalty mechanic from SH1 is gone. I'm not joking. Demon loyalty was fun in SH1 and half-arsed in the Raidou games.  Mothman (minor spoilers) A certain mothman stalks you throughout the apartment block dungeon to drain your party's MP before absconding to leave you fighting his increasingly tougher possy (nothing you shouldn't be able to handle by then). Mothman may use the gay voice archetype, but you know that one gets bitches. He is a real player. God bless you, Mothman!  When you finally catch up to him, he has three of his fellows with him. Throughout the dungeon I kept thinking you would take him/them out in a boss battle similar to, but even more satisfying than, the cat in Eternal Punishment's TV studio dungeon, but no. They are destroyed for you in a cutscene. [sigh] Never mind.  Pazuzu Atlus has always been good at writing downright scummy characters when they intend to, and in SH2 this honour goes to Pazuzu. He is the objective in a semi-optional sidequest from Aion. His lines are voiced and let you know that although he is powerful and speaks in a refined manner, he is nothing more than a bully. If you have a shred of decency in you, you'll make it your obligation to take him out. Great job, writers. Another Pazuzu appears in the Ash boss fight and uses the poison mist mechanic which was fun.  THE BAD  Demon negotiation   It is overly-simplified. It works, but it's better in Nocturne. Then again, did any Megaten veterans complain about buying demons in an auction in Devil Survivor?  Text Size   The text is much too small, and there is no way to change it. We went from nice and clear in P4G, to OK in Nocturne, to unreadable unless you put your spine into shrimp mode for the unvoiced dialogue in SH2. Please rectify this ASAP,  Atlus. I'm sure it would be much easier than sending Mr. Tomigawa round to fix my back every time.  The technical problem   All I get upon starting the game now is eternal loading. I can't even get the title screen anymore. And this was all of a sudden after playing the game some 135 hours. The solution someone suggested on the Steam forum did not work for me at all even after verifying all of my local files. I cannot even say to wait for a sale, because this may happen to you at any time. Whether you buy it cheap or dear, what good is a game you cannot keep playing?  CONCLUSION What a shame. Apart form the one bug which makes the game unplayable, the good definitely outweighs the bad as long as you can play the game in the first place.

One of the best games of the decade. Mixture of horror with survival and exploration makes the Forest absolutely unique, incomparable. Not to mention action: fighting. An unforgattable experience of crashlanding on paradise alike island inhabited by canniballistic tribes. AI is incredibly lively, you never know what this particular cannibal will do. He may attack, he may try to scare you, he may run away or he may run away and bring friends, he may try to follow you, etc. So its better to figure out where cannibals live and make your own camp as far from their routes and villages as possible. Otherwise you will be dead.  As for survival you've got scavenging, hunting and looking for plants. You can build a small camp or a big house, fortified and circled with different types of traps. Cannibals will find your base eventually and will try to burn it down, so defencing your base with traps is vital. Night sieges of your base are engaging. Since you may waste days on building your home, while cannibals may destroy it in an hour.  Story is non linear and you're free to roam and look for clues on your own. It starts with the simple fact that your son Timmy is kidnapped by a mysterious red-paint-cannibal, but the more you roam around the more you realize this is not just about cannibals. Something evil and ancient recites here on that island.   All in all story progression is linked directly to your explorational efforts. There's a lot of points of interest. You will find out that island attracted a lot of people at different tymes. For example five hundred years ago some christians tried already to recite here and failed. There's a lot of intriguing backstories in the Forest which make the main story a lot more believable and complex than it looks at first.  Anyway exploration is tough, since the island is quite big and also there's a vast cave system. Cave entrances are hidden all over the place. Caves are labyrinthine, dark and filled with monsters a lot more surrealistic than cannibals. Caves are as scary as Amnesia, Outlast, Slender and all those run-and-hide horror games. Here in the Forest you do have a lot of weapon types, thus you do can defence yourself, but this is not so easy even on Normal difficulty. Nevertheless you're not absolutely vulnurable but realistically motivated to live, defence yourself and look for your son.

Game is good. Always something to do. Sure a bit of time grindy, but its an idle game. Challenges are most fun. Equipment is really awesome. The Renown is worth, may not seem like it at first but it is worth it. The Bat Hunter is worth it, as those little bats can provide free bonuses that just help in all possible ways. Lastly always keep your eyes open for redeemable promo-codes, as there are new ones quite often, and they can give you a good amount of free stuff from Relics to crafting dust to even runes for trials. Overall its amazing game.   Even after taking a break, deleting all progress except for deleting purchased items such as my Renown, I can get right back into it without any issues and things are just as fun as it was when I first played. I would also strongly recommend the fandom wiki for this game, especially for the challenges, as a few are extremely difficult. I personally hate trying to acquire the Hungerer pet, and you will too despite the fandom wiki being an amazing guide. Also if you have questions you can just go to the discussion on steam or to the discord and plenty of people can and will help. This is by far my most favorite idle game.
