I started with Stellaris the night of release, but I didn't get to play.  I was too taken with the race creation options to get very far and invested hours in creating all sorts of races to enjoy.  Some based upon my favorites from science-fiction (including a variety of takes on human civilization) and some that I dreamt up on the spot.  Race creation was very enjoyable with plenty of options to create a number of unique species.   I was pleasantly surprised with the depth of options which could be combined to generate similar races with subtle but important differences.  One swarm-like race has as near to a hive-mind as I could bend the game mechanics to create, the other less centralized in a single mind but faster to breed and spread across the galaxy, perhaps outrunning the ability of the swarm to remain homogenous.  The differences may sound inconsequential, but on a huge map with a massive empire the small differences between the two will add up.  I would go so far as to say that race creation is the greatest and only strength the game currently posseses.  In my early experience with the game I found the survey mechanic to be quite enjoyable.  After having played through what seems to be most or all of the events associated with exploration they've grown quite stale.  This would have been less a problem if the game had shipped with a working series of mid-game empire building events. Even having experienced one of the late game crises several times I find that the situation is still exciting when it hits a weak and fractious galaxy.   The game that I presently have I find to be a very good, if slightly lacking in a few areas.  I would recommend it to anyone with an interest in the genre. The game greatly suffers from its about 4.5 hours amount of content paired with its 60 dollar price tag.  Other than that though, Resident Evil 3 is an outstanding game.  The graphics are gorgeous and overall the game play is simple and fun.  The characters are likable, for me at least, and the cut scenes never interrupt the game play for too long.  There are a few semi-cut scene sections where you just hold forward or click a button, but besides those moments I felt the game play always remained interesting and fun.  One common complaint I tend to see, besides the play time, is the difficulty.  The game never really becomes challenging and while I have yet to play through it on some of the hardest difficulties, The main middle of the road difficulty options had never proved any real challenge, though if the player ever got stuck anywhere they would have plenty of options to get themselves out of a tight spot, especially with the guns you can buy after beating the game or from the DLC.  Coming after the Resident Evil 2 remake, I can definitely see a lot of people being disappointed with this games release.  There are no extra side modes like the past entry had, and since the past entry was already longer than this one, it would have been nice to see some more content in the game.  There is Resident Evil Resistance that comes packaged with the purchase of the game, but I haven't tried it due to awful reviews and no one else I know willing to play it with me.  Overall, If you catch this game on sale for around 20 dollars or less, I highly recommend it. Nach all der Zeit im Universum von No Man's Sky habe ich mich dazu entschlossen ein Review zu verfassen.   Zur Anfangszeit war das Spiel kaum der Rede wert, eine offenbar nicht fertige Spielversion wurde für viel Geld auf den Markt geschmissen ... trotzdem habe ich das Spiel gespielt und gut meine ersten Stunden dort verbracht.   Nach und nach wurde es immer weiter entwickelt und neue Inhalte haben es nie langweilig werden lassen. Waren anfangs noch kaum seltsame Planeten zu finden und die Vielfalt kaum vorhanden, so hat sich mit der Zeit hier viel getan. Als die Frachter hinzu gekommen sind, war dies für mich der Zeitpunkt, das Spiel etwas mehr zu suchten, damit ich mir einen leisten konnte ... schnell habe ich viele Methoden gefunden um schnell Geld zu verdienen ... fernab von jedem Bug oder Exploid.   Als man endlich die Portale eingebaut und zum funktionieren gebracht hat, sowie die eigene Basis wurde das Spiel immer interessanter. Vielerorts und vorallem auf Reddit konnte man sich Planetenadresse holen wo man verbesserte bis absolut Perfekte Multiwerkzeuge besorgen oder verschiedene witzige Basen sehen konnte. Hier habe ich wieder an die 100 Stunden ins Spiel investiert, bis ich alles erreicht hatte was ich mir vor genommen hatte.   Nun kam vor kurzem NEXT raus. Hier haben sich die Entwickler wirklich viel mühe gegeben, dass Spiel noch einmal komplett auf den Kopf zu stellen. Man bekommt den ersten Frachter, den man beschützt geschenkt und eine Fregatte dazu, welche man auf verschiedene Missionen schicken kann. Zudem kann man sich immer neue Fregatten anwerben um die verschiedensten Missionen erfüllen zu können. Top! Die Idee hinter den Missionen und Fregatten dort hin schicken kommt hier jedoch sehr aus World of Warcraft (Garnision und Ordenshalle) bekannt vor ... aber davon ab gesehen ist dies echt gut umgesetzt mit eigenen aspekten, dass man immer die Info bekommt, was gerade bei der Mission los ist.   Leider gibt es mit dem aktuellen Update hier und da wieder neue Bugs, sowie Bugs die bereits vor dem Update bekannt und gefixt wurden. So können viele Spieler zur Zeit keine Glyphen von Gräbern bekommen um die Portale zu verwenden, was allerdings essenziell für das komplette Spielerlebnis ist. Hier sollte dringend und schnell wieder gehandelt werden. Andere Probleme und Bugs sind unter anderem, dass meine Basis, die ich unterirdisch gebaut hatte nicht mehr zu betreten ging, weil der Planet alles wieder mit Erde auf gefüllt hat. Manchmal wird die Oberfläsche von Planeten nicht geladen, andermals fliegt man aus der Karte heraus und landet unterhalb des Planeten. Hallo liebe Zocker Freunde, :)  Mein Review ist unterteilt in: -Vorwort -Handel -Schiffe und Stationen -Kampf -Think -Schlusswort  VORWORT Vorab kann ich die negativen Kritiken nicht nachvollziehen. Bei XRebirth habe ich Sie noch verstanden, allerdings ist XRebirth nachdem es fertig entwickelt wurde ein richtig gutes Spiel geworden. Soweit ich weis ist es bisher bei jedem X Game so das es immer weiter entwickelt wurde. Und wenn wir mal ehrlich sind hat jedes Game hin und wieder einen Bug und ich denke, bei so einem komplexen Game ist es extrem schwierig es Bugfrei zu halten.  Das Game ist bis jetzt das geilste X was ich gespielt habe und ich hab Sie alle gespielt :) Seitdem XBeyond the Frontier in der Computer Bild Spiele war.  1. HANDEL Der Handel ist nochmal einfacher geworden. Sobald man ausreichend auf der Karte aufgedeckt hat, kann man diese benutzen um zu handeln. Man kann die Ware die man Handeln möchte filtern, sodass man auf der Gesamten Karte nur diese Ware sieht. Wenn die Frachter Kapitäne genug Erfahrung haben, können Sie auch als selbständige Händler handeln. Ihr könnt sogar Schürfer Schiffe selbständig abbauen lassen und verkaufen lassen.  Ein Gamer hat geschrieben, dass die Wirtschaft brach liegt nach einer gewissen Zeit. Ich weiss nicht wie man so ein Bullshit schreiben kann. Da immer wieder neue Waffen Schiffe ect. gebraucht werden. Und selbst wenn kann man die Wirtschaft durch eigen Handel wieder ankurbeln.  2. SCHIFFE und STATIONEN Es gibt ein Völker Rang System, d.h. man kann nicht sofort jedes Schiff und Ausrüstung kaufen. Sobald man genug ansehen hat, steht einem jedes Schiff und jede Ausrüstung zur Verfügung. Was auch einfacher ist, ist das man sich die Ausrüstung nicht mehr mühselig zusammen suchen muss. Sobald man sich ein Schiff ausgesucht hat kommt man in einen Konfigurator in dem man alles selbst zusammen stellen kann. Selbst die Stationen kann jeder so zusammen stellen wie Er will. Das einzige was man dafür benötigt, sind die Blaupausen die man von den Fraktionsführer kaufen kann. Wenn Ihr möchtet könnt Ihr diese auch Illigal erlangen, indem Ihr EMP Bomben an Stationen zündet und dannach die Lecks scannt.  3. KAMPF Wunderbar, wir können wieder jedes Schiff steuern. :) Vom leichten Scout zum schweren Jäger zum mächtigen Zerstörer/Träger. Es macht einfach Spaß die Feinde im Dogfight zu zerschießen. Das Coole es ist meiner Meinung gar nicht mehr so einfach, da die Feinde nicht im Fadenkreuz bleiben und selbst Raketen weichen Sie auch aus.  4. THINK Wie man so schön sagt. Es steht einem seine Kreativität keine Grenzen gesetzt. Einige Kritiken schreiben, dass das Universum leer und langweilig ist. Das kann ich nicht bestätigen, es ist ein Sandbox Game indem man viele schöne Orte/Sektoren finden kann. Indem auch reger Handel betrieben wird. Selbst die Fraktionen treiben jetzt aktiv Krieg um die Sektoren, sowas gab's bei X noch nie.  SCHLUSSWORT Ich kann eine klare Kaufempfehlung abgeben, dass Game ist fertig und wird jetzt nur noch erweitert. Ich freue mich auf 3.0 wenn man eigene Sektoren haben kann und mit Regeln belegen kann. :) Für weitere Fragen stehe ich Euch gerne zur Verfügung.

Greatest Contra clone/Spiritual sequel. It takes a lot from both Contra & Super C with a spice of HardCorps and Shattered Soldier. The overall level design follows the Super C template with a little bit of HC influence as you will be facing bosses about 2 or 3 times a stage. the Shattered Soldier influence comes with the chargeable weapon which gives a strategic element to know which weapon to use at what time and when it is better to simply tap'n'leave with a Charge shot rather than fire at will. The patterns for the bosses are mostly inspired by HC, which feel a bit unbalanced at times since you don't have the abilities needed, but it comes out as a NES-Hard difficulty where you either man up and do a perfect run or you simply won't make it. The last boss is incredibly hard. I'd recommend this game in a Heartbeat to any old-school Contra fan, especialñly if you liked Contra/Super C/Hardcorps/Shattered Soldier over any other installment.   [b] TL;DR If you're an oldschool Contra fan, you better get this game immediately (it is currently bundled for 1.99 on bundlestars and is frequently bundled in other bundle sites as well)[/b]  9/10 Would Lock n' Load and Attack Aggressively again.

金玉其外败絮一半其中   这是一篇晚来的测评，在经历整整一年之后没等到DLC后，我终于能对赛博朋克2077，这部吸引了世界各地无数目光的游戏作出准确评价 。 首先作为游戏史上唯一一款发售前能做到如此宏大规模宣传的游戏 2077向我展示了游戏营销能做到何种地步   无论是游戏界大媒体还是小自媒体，还是CDPR在各大视频网站的官方号，合力向我展示了一个魔幻，冷酷且迷人的赛博朋克世界，火线夜之城也好，乱七八糟的机箱设计大赛，汽车载具品鉴也罢 ，对这个世界的补充与说明的一切都理所当然成为对赛博朋克2077本身的渴望。 无数次让人骂街的跳票之后 我终于能管中窥豹2077的真实一处。 在经历了请假等游戏的狂热与激情之后 ，体对于我这么一个PC,PS4购入了双首发的玩家来说，能亲自体验到2077是相当美妙的一件事 ，像历经长年等待而后收获果实的滋味。 而后这颗果实却把你磕掉了大牙。  先掠过最令人不适的游戏体验部分，从游戏深度出发，首先2077的玩法机制没有那么多挖掘的，在发售前繁多的测试，爆料，体验当中一个以打枪为主带有GTA看门狗要素的3DRPG游戏该是什么模样它也就是什么模样，枪战，车辆追逐还有黑客入侵，这些东西发售前就被挖的很深了，但这并不代表游戏本身不有趣，黑客定位然后用枪支穿墙爆头，连带传染躲在角落看敌人死光，系统重启满血秒杀，各类义体手撕敌人或者用传统的FPS方式刚枪杀过去等，2077在游玩过程中提供的体验相当不错，私心可以打个70多分，且并不难上手只要接触过打枪游戏沉浸2077的玩法相当简单 缺点则是游戏数值随着游戏推进越来越膨胀，极大影响游戏体验，最高难度到了后期几枪杀重锤，难度的选择更多是前中期资源不足的情况下有所区分 而游戏的义体系统本该可以做的更好，应该更注重功能的取舍而不是数值的堆积，黑掉摄像头的义眼，掰开大门的猩猩手，早期测试中的分子线入侵应该是游戏的主要功能，而不是单纯加了点数值和换了个近战武器那么简单，我能察觉到CDPR对于义体的重视程度，但后期义体系统已经变成整个游戏数值膨胀的一环。  其次是游戏最精彩的部分，CDPR做了那么多年沙盒游戏对于巫师系列的理解造就了2077优秀的任务和演出， 整个游戏的任务支线辅以剧情演出加上一些彩蛋一步接一步深入荒诞而又残酷的赛博朋克世界，让整个2077有血有肉，我至今记得牛子炸了的老哥，被V亲自钉在十字架上渴望警醒世人却只能变成奶头乐超梦的约书亚，狗屎社会中坚持自己道义的瑞弗，对资本主义秩序下一直战斗至死的反叛者强尼等太多太多印象深刻的NPC。在游玩过程中我看见了游戏内的角色在资本主义下，在公司殖民主义下的麻木，憎恨，反抗等形形色色的态度与情感，这也让我反观如今的现实社会，996，互联网巨头等游戏所展现的事物，庆幸的是，现实生活里没有烂到2077阶级被彻底固化公司与国家政府旋转门不断剥削底层，底层彻底躺平拿着超梦醉生梦死，只有强尼和V少数几个以死殉道想叫醒睡着的人，不幸的是，现实生活正缓慢靠拢2077。 本作这部分的打分每个人有不同理解，我个人会给到85分，如果没有砍掉大量剧情那我可以给90分 唯一的缺点就是游戏制作管理一团狗屎带来的内容大量被砍，剧情消失带来的结果就是杰基突兀的死，本作剧情流程突兀的短 最后是让人恶心的游戏体验，BUG遍地走，穿模多如狗，PC还好，相对而言BUG不算多，一坨屎的优化才是大问题，而PS4版本就是狗屎中的狗屎，能不能打开游戏，进了游戏秒不秒退，就算不秒退整个游戏也还是卡成一坨，不过这里主要谈PC，主机版本略过，总而言之我在PC版2077中遇到的BUG有 经典黑梦（沉浸游戏剧情的话算加分项）主要NPC和歌子消失 暗杀目标死亡不结算任务 开车追人任务被NPC车辆卡穿模  大街上行走被一车子打飞  赶路莫名其妙被殉爆  当然现在的2077好了很多 大部分BUG你现在是不会遇见的（大概 这部分BUG是2077口碑爆烂的最大原因，连砍掉大量游戏内容也只能算第二，除去黑梦这种无心之举，烂到不能再烂的地步  打分我给1分 1分给黑梦  以及本作最大的争议，由于CDPR的弱智高层的不作为和游戏项目组的混乱，本作有大量内容被砍，夜之城地铁，每个房间都可以进入，高度自由且丰富的纵向探索内容等大量卫星 一个都没有做到，当然不排除CDPR出DLC补上，不过就以CDPR目前的样子来看可能性极小，如果没经历过发售前大量设定和资料宣传的洗礼，我可以接受2077这款抛去BUG本体相当不错的游戏，但经历了如此大规模的宣传和多年的苦等，谁不是期待一个真正的游戏界里程碑呢？ 但CDPR欺骗了无数渴望2077的玩家，给出的2077大量阉割了内容，而公司高层在游戏发售后摆烂推卸责任不作为让我这个从巫师2入坑的新玩家心寒，你这样谁还敢买你的游戏？ 如果你没经过CDPR的画饼宣传轰炸，那么2077是一款不错的游戏，除去BUG游戏整体75分是没问题的，除了后期有赶工痕迹，游戏是相当自洽的  如果你和我一样经历了CDPR多年的画饼营销，那这个游戏只是个优秀的残次品，它确实勾勒了一个赛博朋克世界，但并不能经受时间的冲刷，而我想要的，是一个让游戏界惊艳很多很多年的经典  我还是会推荐给所有人，因为赛博朋克2077是个不错的游戏，更因为这场史无前例的营销应该被铭记   —————————————————————————————————————————————————— I'm likely going to revisit this review once I finish the game, however, it has been suggested that I split up the game because of how long it can be if you listen to all the voiced dialogue and go through every route, both of which I (intend to) do. So, here I am, 5 endings out of 30, and 55 hours with only two men romanced, though I wouldn't really call it romancing. Even put mildly, even considering the time period, this specific game (Kyoto Winds) is more of friendship building than romance building, and you have to have an appreciation for the story more than looking to romance some hot guys. I came into the game understanding this, after reading reviews that said the romance is in Edo Blossoms, I can completely confirm this.  Kyoto Winds is, in essence, the very long common route to Edo Blossoms, where sometimes the MC might figure out she has some sort of feelings towards a LI, but she's not entirely sure what those feelings are, if they exist at all, and then the ending practically says: To Be Continued. Does that make the game bad? No. I don't think so. Unless your aim is simply to kiss the dude, then you're going to be sorely out of luck in that regard.  What's good, bad, and in-between about this game?  Good: Several branching stories and paths. I feel like my choices actually matter. Different options lead to different revelations so repeated play throughs (and there will be many since there are 12 LIs) doesn't (yet) feel like a chore. Skip feature for read text, so when you do eventually know everything, you don't have to slog through 10 hours of the same story that you didn't find interesting. Saying that, there isn't much that I didn't find interesting. I reread every bit. Service Record section in the main menu, allowing you to pick up at a specific chapter instead of starting all over. Lovely art. Music I didn't get tired of hearing. Even considering the mystical aspects of this historical fiction, the stories were realistic and people were seriously injured or even died. I tend to enjoy when mortality is not only possible, but likely and the heroes (whether it be MC or LIs) don't have plot armor.  Bad: It really bothered me the amount of the game where there was no BGM. I understand stopping it for dramatic purposes, but sometimes it was simply gone for no reason, and for an extended period of time. And the scenes where they looped the same 2 seconds of background chatter to give the impression of busy areas, super annoying. MC is predominantly helpless. If you want a damsel in distress, this is perfect. Flimsy excuses for the MC's personality, both for flaws and strengths; it simply makes little sense for why she is the way she is and instead of just saying that's the character they input illogical correlations for causation. MC doesn't grow, really. The game takes place over 4 years and she's practically the same person from beginning to end.  In-between: MC is self-aware enough to acknowledge how useless, unintelligent, and inexperienced she is without dwelling on it, so it doesn't turn into a pity-party, nor spur any sort of fervent tasks to be a better person. Translation. It isn't that it is poorly translated, it's that the language is extremely modernized and Americanized, so certain ideas aren't expressed in a clear manner unless you know about Japanese culture and the Japanese vocabulary associated with those ideas that you so happen to pick up on through the verbal dialogue and not the written text. I don't see how it would be possible to get the route you're aiming for without a guide, if you are the type to aim for certain LIs. I tend to play and see where it takes me, but eventually I'll want to go down everyone's path, and I'm not sure I'll be able to without much trial and error due to the amount of choices that are either removed or changed based on previous choices.  TL;DR: It's really not a bad game, and I dare even say it is a GOOD game as long as you don't go in with expectations of steamy, romantic stories, light-hearted fluff, or men solely interested in the MC, since they all have their own agenda and MC is pretty much along for the ride.

ダークソウルとトゥームレイダーを組み合わせた様なゲーム。謎解き要素はない。 ソウルライクをやりつつ、アドベンチャーを進めていくといったイメージ。EPIC games が関わっているらしくフォートナイトに似たデザインになっています。 やり込み要素が充実しており、何度も周回して楽しめるようになっています。経験値が入手不可になる装備なども用意されており、低レベルクリアも可能です。ちゃんと面白いゲームなのでオススメです。 以下では個人的ですが、良かったところと悪かったところをまとめてあります。   ■良かったところ（ネタバレ含む）  ・エンドコンテンツが充実しています。ボスが多数追加されます。難易度を上げて低レベルクリアとなれば、かなり歯ごたえがあるのではないでしょうか。２週目はレベルや装備品・アイテムを引き継ぎます。モンスター達もさらに強力になります。新たな装備品や素材も追加されます。  ・全６種類の武器から２つを選んでビルドを組みます。どんな組み合わせであっても、必ずシナジーするように設計されています。ヒットボックスが良くできており、ジャストガード・パリィ・ドッジなど、アクション性が充実しています。上手くやればノーダメージ攻略も可能だと思います。  ・収集品の豊富さと、探索が迷路の様に複雑です。道に迷うことも度々あります。武器の強化素材や、装備品の設計図などを集めたり、サブクエストによって様々なイベントが用意されています。特定のアイテムを集めると、シークレットエンディングも用意されているようです。   ■悪かったところ  ・話が長いと感じたところです。会話中の質問の多さと、道中見つかる文書の内容が非常に長い。すべてをしっかり読んで進めていくとなれば、何十時間も費やすと思う。逆に言えば読み応えがあるし、物語の背景もよくわかるので、ここは個人差があると思う。一度見つけた文書はアーカイブからいつでも読めるので、面倒に感じた人は流し読みでもいい。  ・サブクエストがよくわからない。メインクエストの目的は画面上に表示されますが、サブクエストは表示されません。ジャーナルに記録されるのは良いのですが、主人公ヒルダのいい加減なメモ書きをヒントに進めていくので、難解です。ヒルダの個性が見える部分でもあるし、答えを発見した時の楽しさもあるので、そういう意味でソウルライクを示唆していると思う。  ・役に立たない能力値がある。APの回復量とスキルダメージです。これに関してはもっとやり込まないとわかりませんが、全く割り振らなくても十分であることです。攻撃力を伸ばせばスキルダメージも伸びていきます。効果を実感するために多くのポイントを割り振らなければならないので、今後のアップデート次第といったところです。   個人的な感想なので、何とも思わないような部分であったり、はたまた今後改善されるかもしれません。 全体を通して遊んでみて面白かったゲームなのでオススメです。今のところあまり人気がないのが不思議に感じる程です。 よかったら参考にしてみてください。

Science-fiction James Bond story with two anime waifus delivered by Winged Cloud. Just another Sakura VN?  It is a short, mostly comedic, macho special agent fanfic-like story. A little bit of romance triangle, a little bit of tentacle monster, ekhm... entanglers, invasion and a bit of ecchi. It is not a serious story and I only enjoyed parts of it with such approach. There are some choices but don't mistake it for real choice; it is as linear as it can be and there is a single ending. I would say it oscillates around average. A brief cameo of Sakura Beach characters is an extra for those who've played those.  The character sprites are nice. As usual, Inma's art does not disappoint butdon't expect much variation. Also, Inma only draws ecchi stuff so if you expect anything explicit look elsewhere. Backgrounds are pretty good but rather sterile; devoid of life I say.   As for the audio side. There seem to be a tradition of no voice acting in Inma's drawn VNs so yeah, characters are silent. Music is only partly fresh. It's standard for budget VNs to reuse assets and this is not exception. [h1]While I do enjoy football,[/h1]  both on and off field, I don't enjoyed being swallowed by one wave of statistics after another. I wanted to try managing a club in a more streamlined fashion, handle the transfers, communication, squad tactics and so on, without feeling like being an overworked number cruncher. I also admit, that I'm not very proficient in translating my ideas into match day tactics.  For these reasons and some, FMT was the ideal choice for me. It allowed me to take over a club of my choosing - try my hand at managing, transfers, match simulation, etc. - without eating tons of my time in order to just get through a single season. It was really enjoyable and fun, just my cup of tea.   In my opinion, both FM and FMT are great games, but the latter is more suitable for people who either don't enjoy delving too deep into the tactics (blasphemer!) or simply don't want to invest huge chunks of time to see some competition and club progress (go play a broswer football manager, you casual!). I'm both of these people, while also being a huge football fan (minus the craving and dedication to be the next virtual del Bosque or Alf Ramsey). Because of this I was able to really enjoy Football Manager Touch, which sated my hunger for some fast paced, entertaining, none-too-serious yet not-too-dumbed-down field action.  [b]CUT TO THE CHASE:[/b] [list] - great streamlined (lite) alternative to regular Football Manager, retains the fun aspects, while also allowing fans and gamers of the more casual persuasion to enjoy it[/list] [list]- performance on a system requirements exceeding rig was great[/list] [list]- didn't notice any bugs at all, had a few crashes to desktop, which were mildly annoying[/list]  [list]- even though the menu music is not bad at all, I kinda blocked it out after starting the game for the umpteenth time[/list]  [list]- you get what you buy: this is football, don't expect ever changing plot dynamics and surreal twists, because this is a sport, with set rules; that's why it might get repetitive depending on your approach to it[/list]  If you found yourself in some of the descriptions in this review, give it a try. [b]I recommend it.[/b]

There's only one real nongameplay or story issue i have with the game thus far, when i boot it up and talk to an npc. the game lags for the first conversation. Other then that and the difficulty spikes. the game is fun, for sure.  Let's start with the basics.  Roguelikes have bad difficulty curves, usually, this one is still not perfect, as there's a few spikes that make sense storywise, but still aren't as fun to deal with inside gameplay.   The gameplay is very basic in theory, so it's easy to learn it. But it's difficult in the same way a sport is difficult. The few fundamentals you have to rely on (dodging, weapon management, health management, positioning, hazard/gimmick adaptability) become fleshed out in the best way.   Let's just talk about one, and then you can imagine the others.  Dodging enemies is a basic thing, but because environments change from room to room, and because you're dismantling the room (cover objects- like tables, hazard objects- like red video game containers), the game becomes less repetition and more decisionmaking. This becomes more complex as you gain abilities that use room props as weapons, cover gets destroyed, enemies with projectiles are introduced, then spawned in groups, bosses generate enemies that are also forcing you to dodge in certain ways.  All of these things, they fluidly interact with the basic dodge roll you are given. The few but unique and satisfying upgrades you can find within runs do not BREAK the mechanic or fundamental. They only give the mechanic more wiggle room, and more player choice gets added to the decisionmaking.  A roll upgrade may give your rolls a status effect, you can hit enemies and set them on fire with it, making you roll INTO the enemies.   The fundamentals of this game all are like this, very basic to understand, very hard to separate, but most importantly, never complex enough to overwhelm the player with rube goldberg number status chains.  this is because the writing is supposed to, and is definitely first for why you should play the game.  The best way to represent the writing in a roguelike is through respawning and interacting with the story each loop. At least. that's what it seems like recently developers are doing.  The approach isn't perfect for a long narrative, or a highly complex game of thrones style plot, but it works for narratives about repeating themes. Like for hades, futility, willpower, meaningless struggle, and how drama and lessons come from failure and success.  In Going Under, the tone and comedy tells itself via repetition, how the insanity of tech startup culture becomes more obvious, the more you understand the personalities of people who exist within that culture.  The worst boss isn't a bad boss because he's making one decision that hurts employees, it's the mindset that drives everyone up a wall. It's so much more funny to see the consistently horrible decisions, BECAUSE he is telling you about his grind, and his idea guys, and why beating up union workers is cool. The comedy comes from the absurdity being consistency.  It's so on the nose, and so brutal, because it uses repetition.   Artistically. I LOVE the vision and the tone.  The art style, the absurdist, nihilist sarcasm, the killer soundtrack, the writing, the game design is all there.  The only issue i have IS the difficulty spikes being so jarring. Spoilers on where. The first half is alright, easy to grasp, kinda tough, but it's a good balance. Then the special dungeon hits, and it feels kinda like there isn't a curve at all, until the boss swiss cheeses you with a dark souls fight.  Then the difficulty spike 2. The revamped dungeons are WAY harder, TOO much harder.  I don't hate it, I don't want an easy mode, I just feel like the power ups feel less impactful. This feels like the game chucked me off a cliff, if i wasn't familiar with this from isaac, gungeon, spelunky. I would have dropped the game. Tbf, it isn't easy in the beginning, and the game does wait for the sucker punch until the second half. But, that's my only REAL gripe with the game. So overall. I love it.

角色行动种类分等级顺序制虽然点子很好，但是容易导致玩家在学习期间忘了做哪一步或者是多做了哪一步，但在学习过后又会导致玩家行为的策略单一，因为行动顺序上总会出现最优解，如果能够让某一动作（尤其是猎人直接射击）这一动作能够吃到消耗点数多少的收益的话，能给玩家带来更多的策略性。而法师并不像玩家普遍所理解的法师一样，使用法术直接攻击，而是与场景里的物体所互动从而进行小范围内的攻击，再加上游戏内场景的地形编排与掩体的设定，使得游戏也更加合理与真实。寻常的角色扮演游戏都是硬碰硬，你一下我一下，有来有回，而这游戏则是利用控制技能与掩体，以及回血手段的贫乏，让玩家更加注重于无伤战斗，尽量做到只有玩家能打出伤害，而敌人都造成不了威胁的场面。角色的每一次掉血都能牵动着玩家的内心，而角色受到的伤害并不会让玩家觉得是因为数值的原因而导致受伤，而是会让玩家觉得是因为自己的抉择导致角色受伤害，这一点让我深有体会。

I cannot go further into detail without spoilers as this really is a story driven experience. However, I can go further about the shortcomings of the game as a sequel.   Balancing feeding and power use is gone. There are opportunities to do both, but they do not actually matter.   The choices are sadly given as much weight as the old bioware Jedi games. Meaning you are either Good to the point of martyrdom and stupidity. Or you are heartlessly evil selfish to the point of mustache twirling. It kinda sucks. Further, even though they were quite clear about there only being the lasombra clan as a choice I still feel is a detraction from the previous game. Follow The Cpt Froggy Club Curator Page for plenty more![/b][/url][/quote]  Ancestors Legacy: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~   The Middle-Ages is probably one of the most fascinating eras in human history. It started in the late 400’s AD at the fall of the Western Roman Empire and lasted all the way up to the 1500’s AD. Europe, at this stage, had plenty of small kingdoms with their own rulers. As the centuries progressed, many of these small kingdoms allied themselves and became forces known as The Anglo-Saxons, Germans and Slavs; all of them with incredible conquest stories. During this period, new invaders from the north arrived on the scene. . . the Vikings . . . set on spicing things up in Europe a tad more. Are you related to one of the groups of people mentioned above? Whether yes or no, jump into the thick of the Medieval Ages, in Ancestors Legacy!  Ancestors Legacy is a real-time strategy game developed by Destructive Creations and published by 1C Company.  This game offers 4 campaigns (Vikings, Anglo-Saxons, Germans and Slavs) which include 5 chapters to complete per campaign in the single player mode, as well as a multiplayer mode where you can either battle against the AI, or opponents online.  Straight off the bat, you’ll be able to choose which of the four nations’ campaigns you want to play, which is a massive bonus, in my opinion. You’ll still have to successfully complete a chapter to unlock the next, which is fine. In terms of difficulty, you can elect to play against easy, normal or hard AI in the campaign mode.  Each chapter in the normal difficulty progresses in length, starting at around 30 minutes for the first chapter, all the way up to over 2 hours for the final chapter.  At the time of writing this review, I have finished the Vikings campaign and played 2 chapters in the other three campaigns.   The first aspect that I really like in the game is the cut-scenes between the missions. They are based on facts, splendidly portrayed with stunning illustrations, and superbly narrated. Personally, I felt that I was in the middle of a documentary before going into battle - just spot on!      The layout is pretty conventional as far as this genre of game is concerned.  The action takes place on the majority of your screen. On the lower right-hand corner of your screen you will find the interface functions of your towns, buildings, upgrades and military units. On the opposite corner, a mini map will be displayed, and between the two corners are your units. The maximum number of units you can create at any given time is 10, and each of these units will have a maximum of 10-foot soldiers, either five knights or chivalry units, and three with weapons of destructions, such as the catapult.   In each of the single player missions, you’ll have to achieve certain tasks, which can vary from capturing villages, destroying outposts, sabotaging specific resources (such as a well) or rescuing some of your countrymen or pirates (Vikings) from captivity. Most of the maps have villages to capture. By taking these villages you’ll gather resources to build new defences both in your main town, as well as in the captured villages. If you gather enough wood, you’ll be able to build traps on roads (mud paths, really), which will serve to slow down incoming enemy forces, and even cause heavy casualties.  In terms of the gameplay, it is pretty much an isometric style with great graphics and fluid animations. The interface is very easy to use; you can either select all units, or just one at a time, and give them orders to go somewhere or to attack an enemy unit. What you really need to be good at is hiding some of your units in the bushes and flanking the enemies from the right and the left, to deliver as much damage as you can to the opposing units. Bear in mind that your own forces may find themselves in this same predicament. There are basically a couple of ways to get your units back to health. The first way is to fight until you destroy your opponent. You may or may not lose soldiers in your squad.  Their health bar might swing from green to red, which means that one or more soldiers have deep wounds. To heal these injuries, all you have to do is to set up camp anywhere on the map (if you’re not involved in a fight).  If you’ve lost a few soldiers, head up to your main town, or the village you captured, and replenish your squad(s).   If you like playing skirmish, or against other players online, it’s extremely easy to set up and you’ll find plenty of servers to play in.  From what I can gather, most of the servers are based in Europe.   Graphically the game looks great and is very easy to get used to. As I mentioned, I really like the cut scenes, and the soundtrack is pretty good, too. All the controls seem to work well, as far as I can see. The only issue I encountered is that I could not re-load a saved game after an update.  Apart from that, it’s smooth.   Positives: ~~~~~~~   +	Great graphics +	Superb cut scenes +	4 Campaigns with 5 chapters each +	Multiplayer mode +	Good soundtrack +	Achievements  Negatives: ~~~~~~~~   -	Experienced issue loading a saved game after an update -	No Trading cards  A great real-time strategy game set in in the Middle Ages. Probably one of the best I have seen this year! Sire, this should be in your game library, period.  8/10  Key provided by developer/publisher for review purposes. Un curioso juego de simulación belica de la guerra aerea en Gran Bretaña duranta la IIGM. Y digo curiosa porque el juego se divide en dos fases muy claras, una primera de gestión de recursos y creación de las defensas (durante 50 dias) que tiene el jugador para proteger Londres del ataque alemán. En esta fase, tendremos que administrar, con unos pocos de recursos economicos, las escuadras, los aeropuertos, los radares, y cosas similares, mientras el rival se dedica a enviarnos oleadas de aviones para espiarnos y bombardear nuestras infractucturas, cosa que deberas de evitar enviando tus propias escuadras de aviones, que anteriormente deberás de haber recrutados, equipadao y entrenados.  La otra fase del juego es cuando, en el aire, tu escuadra se encuentra con la de un rival, y comienza un combate aereo, que no deja de ser un wargame por turnos (aunque es en tiempo real, es posible pausarlo y dar las ordenes a tus aviones).  Cuando acabe cada batalla, volveras al menu anterior, y tus pilotos habrán ganado experiencia, habran sido derribado, y generalmente, llegará un momento en que la escuadra tendrá que volver a su aerodromo a respostar o recuperar pilotos si recibe demasiadas bajas.  A grandes rasgos, este es el juego. Es un wargame ligero con toques de gestión, pero que para que te guste, te tienen que gustar estos juegos, ya que de casual tiene poco.  Me gusta que los Alemanes primero te mandan escuadras ligeras para buscar tus bases, despues otras dos o tres escuadras similires, para de repente, enviarte un escuadrón con bombarderos que como no los detengas te destruiran todo lo que tengas, incluido los aviones que tienes respostando en las bases.  Mi consejo es que mantengas siempre una escuadra en el aire y otra respostando y lista para salir, pero nunca dos en el aire salvo extrema necesidad...

Great discover-the-rules puzzle game. If you liked Baba is You or A Monster's Expedition, you'll like this too. I don't want to say too much more, as it'd spoil the games surprises.  One great thing Can of Wormholes has that many games don't is the hint system. Instead of giving you the answer, it gives you a simplified puzzle that contains a similar idea to the main puzzle. The hint puzzles almost never fully give the answers away either, and this makes the difficulty of the game a lot smoother without ever feeling cheap.  One misstep I should mention is the final world - it felt more like a farewell tour rather than a final challenge, and I would have preferred a final challenge. I was ready for more surprises in this final world, but it fell flat here.  Still, all the other worlds were great, and I definitely recommend Can of Wormholes to puzzle game fans.

This a good game. Holds a lot similar to the good of resident evil and I've also heard that it's story can be compared to silent hill 2, I have not played silent hill 2, I just know that means good. Don't be fooled though, it definitely does it's own things to stand by itself and has other influences it wears on it's sleeve, none of which I found out of place. I found it's narrative structure compelling and I wanted to learn more every step of the way.  Interesting sci-fi worldbuilding and excellent music, leaves a lot to be speculated on in terms of story, it's very good at delivering information in crumbs at just the right times but can still be narratively decisive when it wants to.  The game definitely isn't very hard though, with some slight tedious back tracking you can easily have a surplus of equipment and never be in any real danger. I only died once on my two playthroughs and it was because I didn't understand a boss mechanic. The aiming is mostly lock-on though there is a free aim option, I would say the game isn't made for free aim.  The strongest part of the game are it's puzzles, I brought out the notebook for this game and it was fun figuring everything out.  All that being said my biggest gripe with the game is the inventory system. 6 items only. 2 of which I mostly used for weapons, 1 of which an item which is required to traverse some areas of the game, and around 2 slots for health or ammo items. It became extremely tedious running into too many items and quickly running out of room, forcing me to go back to the item box every couple minutes. At the start I would be doing this as I didn't want to not pick up ammo or health in turn for key items but by the end I just became spam using health items and throwing away ammo.  It's a great product, no, I'd better put it as a great outcome of a lot of science fiction works and survival horror gameplay.

It's got an interesting premise. Instead of another game that allows your creativity to roam free, they ask you to channel it into finding solutions to one problem. A massive amount of debt. You're tasked with tearing apart old space ships, getting as much salvage as possible, doing it as quickly as you can, all without getting yourself killed. It's OSHA's Nightmare, The Game.  The better you get at tearing apart the ships, the more money and upgrade points you bring in. Upgrades go towards your tools and equipment to further make quick work of the job you're doing. this doesn't necessarily make it easier. Just because your cutting tool can cut through the hull of a ship, doesn't mean you still don't have to depressurize the ship or you'll lose all the salvage inside to the void. Just because your grappler can throw 6 tons around like it's nothing, doesn't mean you don't have to be careful throwing that giant slab of titanium into the processor or it'll get beaten up and become scrap for the furnace.  Challenging modes are planned for a later date but that doesn't mean you can't challenge yourself now. I'm trying to find the fasts and most profitable ways of getting things done to meet quotas by listed deadlines for more bonuses. Sometimes you nail it, other times you cause an explosion and lose everything. It's wonderful.  Bumps and crashes as of right now, still very much an early access title, but a great way to lose track of time. Looking forward to how this game progresses.

这一款优秀的种田游戏，游戏策划说这款游戏已经到了改编的极限，实际上我不这么认为。 有时候，难以改变的仅仅只是思维，而不是程序。  我个人认为，假设出现模拟器2，他的类型和模式也不会超出1的框架，这是从创造者的思维决定。  只要改变一下思维，1代还可以更优秀。  思维一：凡人的战争 建议：凡人的战争不应该只是一页纸，更可以是你的徒弟，你的宗门，和其他宗门的徒弟，其他宗门的争斗。更可以是争夺地盘，村庄，资源的另类游戏方式。  思维二：智能演算不足，这个问题跟太吾绘卷的问题是一样的。NPC势力不会扩张，不会相互攻打，如同一潭死水没有流动。没有流动的游戏，是没有生命力的游戏。  思维三：繁琐：很多时候，玩家只需要操控一个NPC就够了，其他的NPC可以自行演化，也就是智能代管，让玩家选择一个项目，让NPC自己去修行，去游历，去冒险，去于其他门派的NPC结缘，结仇。从而遭遇突来的打击和杀戮，这才符合攻击的合理性。（这个功能其实跟外门弟子的功能是类似的，种田、砍柴、挖矿，只是形式变了一下即可，可以让玩家更加专注的培养一个角色。）  思维四：神道：神道修行可以转变为另类的玩法，比如玩家建设宗门直接变成了建设城隍庙，满足信徒香火，完成各种任务，积蓄神力，从土地神之类的一直升到天帝，这很种田，也完全在模拟器的范围之内。（可以加入阴间，鬼神，神战之类的元素。）  暂时就这么多，如果创造者觉得不错，等2出来送个首发。

So I'm just going to add on to the pile of positive reviews.   To put it briefly, Deep Rock Galactic is primarily about two layers: [b]exploration[/b], and [b]FPS combat[/b]. Both of those layers manage to be simultaneously deep and strategic, as well as fun and satisfying. The game boasts an impressive level of variety and options in all aspects, and excellent audio and visual design. It is well-balanced, and nearly every strategic option is viable.  One feature I greatly appreciate is that before starting a game you are given a selection of possible missions to choose from, including details like mission length and complexity (separate from difficulty) allowing you to cater your experience to your preference. This also benefits the progression, as you can choose to avoid the more complicated objectives/mechanics until you are comfortable with the basics. This game is simple to learn while still being engaging at higher difficulties or more complicated mission types.  While intended as a 2-4 player co-op experience, it's surprisingly entertaining to play solo, with the game providing an alternative mechanic for solo players which feels well thought-out, as opposed to simply filling the remaining slots with bots. Additionally, from my experience, the community is healthy and friendly to newcomers, and you can easily find strangers to play with. Essentially, you don't necessarily need friends to play with in order to enjoy this game.  Deep Rock Galactic provides a lot of value for its asking price (and frequently goes on sale) and features no intrusive micro-transactions or loot boxes. The DLC for this game is merely cosmetic with no gameplay effects.  [b]TL;DR[/b] If this game looks interesting to you, chances are you will love it.

垃圾游戏，我是傻逼  —————————————— 制作组竟然愿意问为什么给了差评，还蛮少见的，那我回答一下。  please google： 很高兴你们愿意主动聆听玩家的意见，我说几个我对游戏的不理解。 首先要说明的是，我在通过所有教程关后，只和3位朋友一起玩了合作，并没有进行过单人游戏。 1.我认为在游戏过程中，真实性的模式高过了对于游戏性的考虑，导致了很多时候会非常的无聊，比如我们开了7KM的车就为了去扑灭一个垃圾桶。（这也许能反应消防员的真实工作责任，但是大量的出现在游戏中会增加挫败感）是的，如果他只出现了一次就算了，在我们的游戏过程中，这种情况出现的次数太多了，在我们已经熟悉了配合之后，总是想着去挑战一些高难度的任务，却分配这样的任务给我们，心理落差很大。 2.上一点也引出了另一个问题，任务难度不是一种合理的曲线，而是完全随机的，我们刚刚扑灭了一个四层的办公室，下一次却是好几公里外的一个垃圾桶，这会使我们对接下来的关卡没有任何期待。 3.我不知道出发的地点是固定的还是随机的，因为我们没有重复打过一关两遍，但是出生点并不是以事发地点最近的地方开始是我可以肯定的，因为我们在开车过程中路过过我们别的消防站，这也让我们产生疑问，为什么不是选择最近的消防局前往事发地点，而是要专门换别的，是为了用糟糕的开车手感影响我们吗？（虽然开车的手感一般，但因为这并不是游戏的重点，其实就我个人而言是不在乎的，但是请不要每次都那么远好吗，开车的过程实在是太无聊了） 4.作为一个具有教育意义的游戏，我认为游戏中对于被命名为“回火”的概念是存在问题的，这会误导真实中遇到火灾的人，虽然专业知识我知道的并不多，但是开门后躲在一旁的这种方式绝对是不可取的，也希望制造组可以至少文字或者语音的方式提醒玩家，这是游戏中做了简化的处理。 游戏结束好几天了，就想到了这几条，希望可以得到反馈，并祝制作组游戏大卖

I enjoyed this game and would be back for another run through soon.  The early game is a bit challenging because of the number of slots available on your starter ship, but that kept it exciting and it is very satisfying when you get a nicer ship with more space to work with.   Starting about mid-game,  this becomes more of a relaxed jaunt through space, just enjoying the spacy ambiance.  It is simple and relaxing with gameplay being straightforward.  It is a nice way unwind.  I only ran into only one bug on my first playthrough, and it was with the autosave system.  But the developers are very active on discord and are planning to address this in the next patch.  They even sent me a fixed up save file.  It is good to see more games in the space exploration genre and I wholeheartedly support indie developers in this space, which is my favorite genre of games to play.    There is no space combat in this game, so the focus is purely exploration with a little bit of resource management and survival.    I think there is a solid foundation here that the devs could potentially build upon. More depth and meaning to that exploration game loop (without necessarily tying it to a storyline) would be very welcome for example.  Overall, I would recommend this to someone wanting to spend a few hours in a casual space-themed game.

While I dislike giving any game a negative review, I found this game to be incredibly frustrating, not only in its pointlessness but also in its lack of story development and overall game play. I had to web search the point to this game since the story is so lacking. It's basically like playing a space shooter set on very hard and you have the worst ship possible yet you're expected to just die over and over until you can get enough credits to afford step 1 out of 4 or 5  for an upgrade which you seem to get no benefit from until you complete those steps and what's worse is that when you complete those steps, the improvement is minimal. Incredibly frustrating if you like a normal sense of accomplishment, progression and immersion. The whole re-spawning/cloning idea just seems like it was a way for these develops to provide a bare bones game yet covered this fact by making it a story element - creative yet again, no pay-off for those who like a normal sense of progression that isn't tied to constantly dying.   Another aspect I found frustrating is the supposed crafting system, again, something else I had to web search because the game offers no sense of direction other than the linear stage progression but you don't get a choice there other than choosing the upper or lower path. I've played this game over 12 hours and unlocked about 4 things to craft and not once found the trade station that you supposedly unlock crafting at so basically everything I collected and lost due to constantly dying from encountering enemies too powerful for an early game stage was also pointless and frustrating. This wouldn't be so bad if you could upgrade your ship in-between levels but nope, you have to get killed and restart from the beginning for that to happen. Overall, the game does look great and the combat is intense although extremely unbalanced and frustrating especially if you play it with a controller, the default controls are just garbage and targeting is also extremely frustrating unless you're using lock-on and missiles that home in on their target. Keyboard and mouse? Also frustrating due to the tethered targeting system - even worse than No Man's Sky. Most enemies you encounter in the beginning will lace up your ship before you even get close enough to them to return fire or get a good shot at, and to make matters worse they do more damage to you than you do to them and they have higher shields than you, even the supposed easy enemies, especially if two or three of them get on you. Want to try to dodge and outmaneuver your enemy? Forget about it. Your ship is effectively more of a paper target weighted down with lead than it is a ship with shields. I understand that the starter ship is exactly that but you should at least have a chance to get somewhere without losing half of your ship's integrity or payload. I'm not sure what motivated these devs to create this game but dying over and over again due to unbalanced game play/combat and overly powerful enemies at early game stages is not something I would consider fun or even remotely interesting.  I would only recommend this game to try-hards, those who are gluttons for punishment, or my worst enemy. Otherwise save your money, there are more substantial space shooters out there, I wouldn't even recommend getting it on sale unless it were priced at $5-$10 because that's about all it's worth.

Alors, je commence par le bémol: le jeu n'est pas en français,et là quel regret et quel dommage pour tous ceux qui ne pourront pas y jouer et à qui je déconseillerais de l'acheter si votre niveau d'anglais est vraiment à la rue, car il y a beaucoup de textes qui impliquent des choix et des conséquences dans l'histoire.  Ceci étant dit, le jeu est génial! Graphismes superbes, carte du monde superbe aussi. Sur la carte tactique, les combats sont très tactiques, c'est quasiment de la haute couture avec beaucoup de paramètres à utiliser, des équipements (glyphes) à stuffer sur vos unités après les avoir craftés bien sûr. Vos unités qui progressent en prenant de l'XP, devenant de plus en plus puissantes donc on s'y attache à ces petites bêtes là.  Sur la carte  du monde les possibilités sont infinies aussi, tellement les factions sont nombreuses, chaque faction ayant un éventail d'unités spécifiques, mais que vous pouvez  tout de même recruter si vous avez obtenu les lieux le permettant et par la suite construis les bâtiments dans votre tour qui permettront eux aussi ces recrutements divers et variés. Les factions: les hommes, les orcs, les gobelins, les vampires, les elfes, les morts etc, chacune composée de guerriers divers et variés mais que vous ne découvrirez qu'en avançant sur la carte. La magie et les sorts sont très présents évidemment et sans doute est ce le jeu qui me donne le plus l'impression de vivre ce que je ressens dans les films du seigneur des anneaux, même si ce jeu n'y fait pas référence, je dis cela juste pour essayer de faire comprendre le ressenti que j'ai en jouant à Spell Force Conquest of Eo  Le jeu n'est pas compliqué, mais il est touffu et par voix de conséquences complexe par la multitude de possibilités qui s'offrent à vous, les quêtes qui viennent s'ajouter au fur et à mesure des lieux que vous visitez, mais les tours passants votre perception de ce qui vous entoure s'aiguise ainsi que votre expérience et connaissance du jeu (c'est mon cas au bout de 14h de jeu).  Je vais essayer de conclure, car il y aurait encore tellement à dire, en vous disant que les possibilités, les choix, l'histoire et le monde sont tellement vastes que je ne peux pas, ici, tout vous décrire, j'oublie bien d'autres choses mais ce qui est la preuve que ce jeu est, à mon goût et selon mon humble avis, énorme!  Une démo serait la bienvenue pour ceux qui hésitent encore.

I recommend this game with a caveat.  To begin with, this game is the definitive way to experience board games on a PC. It has just about every tool and item you'd want, such as dice, calculators, rule books, card decks, and timers. And this is made all the more impressive when you factor in the workshop content, which effectively brings many well-known tabletop and board games into the simulator, and this includes stuff like Jenga and Uno and DnD boards. It's an absolute blast to play with friends, and even pretty fun to play with random people on open servers. The controls are a little confusing at first and can be a bit clunky as it relies on a lot of shortcuts if you don't want to rely on the contextual controls to figure out what you're doing.  Now, the caveat: The VR is no bueno. Unless you have an Index, the UI scaling is abysmally small to the point that it's barely legible. I had to boost the render resolution in the per-app settings of Steam to try and remedy it, but it just wasn't improving. The UI is essentially the same as it is on desktop, only it floats about a metre in front of you and many things you'd hope would be mapped to the controllers are still just buttons on the interface. Not only that, the controls are rather disappointing to say the least, which is baffling since you'd think this game is ripe for VR. Things that should be intuitive such as reaching out and picking up a card becomes a chore as the controls are very contextual. It just can't seem to decide if you want to flip a card, pick it up, or pick up the entire deck it's on. And the performance gets even worse in VR in spite of the simplistic graphics. I understand that the VR is not the primary focus of this game, but it's a shame to see it not get the best treatment it could get.  However, if you don't care about VR, then disregard that second half. It's a great simulator with more pros than cons.

Deadlight is an easy sell for me because it's a cinematic platformer, a subgenre that hasn't been all that popular during the last 25 years or so. I think there's not even a community tag for it on Steam.  Besides that I don't think Deadlight is all that great either, the somewhat grounded animations the genre is known for are undermined by the addition of wall jumping, and the story is frankly terrible, one could say it's generic at best. However, the movement and presentation are solid, I especially like how high contrast lighting is used to take advantage of the fixed perspective. It's a commonly used resource among bleak zombie stories, but it looks good and helps with the readability.  So, overall, I make a net positive balance out out of Deadlight. However, If you want to get into the genre then I recommend Oddworld: Abe's Odysee to start out instead.

Game was quite fun, easily 150hrs for a full playthrough. I've got good knowledge of the PF system but I don't min/max as much esp on a 1st playthrough.  While I built a solid character (Monk/Dragon Desciple/Sorcerer) I didn't want to have to micromanage all builds. I will say if you use the Default builds given by the game, you will struggle in end-game allies with less than +40 to-hit will struggle to land blows on the final enemies (given they have 50+ Armor Class) and most builds with a +5 Weapon and +6 Stat belt with some buffs will have +30-35 Attack (meaning they can hit a 55 on a 20 so you're looking at less than 25% hit rate while the enemy routinely whacks you for 80 damage a hit. On Core+ you'll have to really know the game and CC or maximize damage because the default builds will not fly above Normal Difficulty which I highly recommend for your first run.  Some regions, esp one in Chapter 3 feel way overturned and if you don't have what is needed to counter them, well you better pray for nat 20's on your attacks. A fair bit of fun with the system is expressing builds and trying out new things but there are many times where you *need* a powerful Dispeller or someone who targets Reflex Saves with Magic and has high Spell-Penetration. If you don't check specific boxes you will have a bad time because there are assumptions made in Paizo's higher CR enemies (such as having Death Ward on all PCs or having a dispelling caster or a Cleric/Oracle (Daeran's default build will work for a healer very well though).  So if you enjoy CRPGs, like the Pathfinder or Dungeons and Dragons style gameplay/system then this is a great game to pick up. Play on Normal or lower if using the default game builds or you're new to Pathfinder... Core Difficulty is the TTRPG ruleset and it's hard mode which should tell you what the actual hard mode in game would be. It is definitely worth your money though and is well made; the bugs I encountered were mostly minor: - Bugged attacks in Turnbase mode (have both Move/Standard action) but being unable to attack; no the character was not paralyzed/stunned or fascinated. - Glitchy handling of Dominate/Madness effects a few times a character would become 'stuck' as an enemy and I was forced to either reload or kill them to resolve it. - Ragdolls flying out of loot range, is minor and funny. - Feared enemies will run the entire map to get away from you. Sometimes into other combats, so best to run back and let them reset if they start running into unexplored areas.  My only complaints really is that the Crusader Mode is a bit lackluster in goals. It plays like Risk/Military Management game but otherwise it's not very engaging which made Ch3 and Ch5 drag out a fair bit.

Keep in mind most of the other (negative) reviews are from early access.  Anyway, I'd give this game a buy with a caveat. If you, like me, are always searching for starship sims (less Tie Fighter more Star Trek Bridge Commander), you might enjoy this game. If you aren't, however, you probably will not like this, as it is a fairly simple, shallow experience. That experience, however, does scratch that utterly maddening starship sim itch.  This game allows you to play like you're Captain Picard or Admiral Adama, which is something a lot of us really want, but not something that's often made. Most of the games in this genre are decades old, rarely talked about or even remembered, and sometimes not even capable of being played on modern machines -- even with DosBox. This game fills that very large gap. If you are looking to sit on the bridge and take command over starship systems and crew, this is for you.  So what is the game like? It basically amounts to a series of simple mobile-like minigames superimposed over a smallish 3d open world and resource management simulator. You can pick and name your captain, crew, ship loadout (everything from weapons systems to what kind of food replicators you ship is equipped with), and starting resources. The controls are not able to be changed, but they are fine as-is and not anything that you'd worry about changing anyway. For that matter the interface is streamlined and easy to use. The mini-games are actually enjoyable, if simplistic, so the game ends up being pretty fun for the price.   The only things I dislike about the game are its lack of depth (the minigames really do feel like minigames and the away missions are just randomly generated die rolls with possible stat bonuses applied as far as I can tell) and its visual style (some may like it, but I find it a hideous mess that's aesthetically similar to the worst of bargain-bin scifi crap--lots of glowing neon, random hexes getting in the way of everything, plastic-looking textures, hideous ship design, etc). These may be deal breakers for some, but I'm willing to put up with it because A) It's cheap and B) it exists in a genre that's very rarely explored.   tl;dr It's a simpler FTL in first person, except you feel more attached to your crew and ship

Anyone who can read around 2012 may feel nostalgic playing this game as one of the plots is based around preventing the world from ending, much the same way people believe it was gonna happen in the real world (unless it did happen and we're all secretly in purgatory).  Set mostly in the city of Constantinople, Assassin's Creed Revelation for me was a cultural shock. The language, people, presentation, history, architecture and plenty more were so refreshing to enlighten new experiences like no other games I've played. Even by doing nothing, the city feels so alive with people being people, like singing, shopping, talking and trying to flirt or steal from me. It was also intriguing exploring a city in a cave, I never imagined anyone like that would be possible before, but for some reason now I found it fascinating to do more personal research into it. There's a lot of fun to be met while playing outside of the mission, like challenging yourself to pickpocket money out as many people as without using my equipment, soon getting my ass beat up after getting caught. I'm sure it is like this in the other previous Assassin's Creed games, I'm just letting you know you wouldn't be disappointed with what the developers delivered to us in this one as well.  So Revelation continues the story of Ezio who despite being almost past his prime base from his slow movement (that doesn't hinder the gameplay mind you), is still a charmer and more mature evolving into becoming a respectful character.  There were also added new items and abilities added into this game like bombs, hook blades and being able to summon assassins which are very fun to use. Like, imagine how cool it will feel to take down all your foes with the click of a button leaving behind a pool of corpses and pretending as if nothing happened.   The main story,  the romance and the side quests were actually good, and easy to follow, despite being quite predictable at times, like you can't tell you wouldn't be able to guess who is the antagonist between 2 siblings, basing it off their haircut.  At the end of the day (or night), this is a great game for completing Desmond's story as well as passing the torch. Ultimately, this was the first and last Assassin's Creed I've played (so far) that I really enjoyed. I think after finishing the campaign 4 times, (3 times on Xbox 360 and once on PC) I feel I'm more than qualified to recommend this game. Even for £10, I feel it is worth it (as the multiplayer isn't available). It's interesting that a simulation of work could be fun, but Giants pulled it off.  As a long time player of farming simulator 2015, I wasn't expecting much of a change in this iteration, but I am glad to say I was wrong.  Not only have many of the mechanics been improved ot make things more realistic, but the graphics are insanely gorgeous!  Even the DIRT looks awesome- something we take for granted in real life, but is difficult to reproduce in a game/simulation.  My only suggestion for improvement in an update would be water.  Mud puddles should be splashed through, streams that are forded should have the water pushed around the tires, and the water should really be moving better than it is.  I know water is a difficult thing to reproduce, but many graphic designers are doing it pretty well now.  I also want to see MUD.  Oozing, squeezed, pushed, rutted mud.  When the mud dries, I want to see the ruts left behind.    Also, I want to see dirt clods falling off the tractors, especially on roads, not just tire tracks (which is great, don't get me wrong!).  My last suggestion is the 1st person view.  I believe walking shouldn't be more like... gliding.  I need to see my legs and feet.  I need to see my hands and arms.  I want to see my hands on the steering wheels turning the wheel and allowing it to slide back through my hands.  Even with these missing items, I would still highly recommend the game!  I'd rate the simulation/game at a 8.5 out of 10. The additional 1.5 could be made up with splashing mud puddles, mud, water, and the 1st person view.

Like many others have mentioned, this game is very short (around an hour long) and doesn’t have a save feature, so it has to be completed in a single sitting. This isn’t a problem, though, because I didn’t want to put it down anyway. This game is fantastic at creating an uneasy atmosphere and sprinkling in just enough jumpscares to keep you on edge without overdoing it. Although The Convenience Store is brief and doesn’t have much replay value (in my opinion, of course), I think the length suits it well and the price for what you get is fair. It’ll only take you a couple playthroughs to get all the achievements. The only bug I noticed was a very minor graphical one on the night it was raining; I could still faintly see rain falling even after going inside the store. And although not a glitch, I always had to turn off the weird camera filter the game starts with since I could hardly make out anything with it. Finally, to hopefully save someone the trouble of wasting a playthrough to find out, [spoiler] throwing away the last tape gives you the exact same ending as watching it does. So unless you just feel like chucking it anyway, you might as well ignore the bin so you can at least see the video. [/spoiler] So, while a handful of things bugged me, overall I thought The Convenience Store was a great little horror game that is well worth a try. Gets a recommend from me.

At times like this, I wish Steam would allow us to re-review a game so we can keep a record of older reviews and opinions based on old versions of a game.  I first played Subnautica way back in late 2014, when I was fourteen. The game has come a long way since. A [b]long[/b] way. There was just a big empty ocean to explore, some simple resources to collect and a few tools to craft. I even remember when terraforming was still a feature that absolutely destroyed the frame-rate and corrupted saves.  This game is a very different beast now. Well, since its completion in 2018 and 2.0 update in 2022. The devs went from making a survival-crafting game in a saturated market, to a story-driven atmospheric experience that I absolutely loved and regret not having the courage or attention span to enjoy sooner. It's not the most compelling story of all time but the way the story and equipment progression is cleverly fed to you by having depth thresholds, and biomes that are too dangerous to traverse without a vehicle and oxygen upgrades is very clever and really pushes you to test your comfort zone.  The graphics are definitely dated somewhat by their 2014 roots, but the biomes are so colourful and expertly ambianced, with a brilliant soundtrack by a (sadly but rightfully disgraced) composer with an other-worldly quality.  It's definitely not a perfect game, though. I think Subnautica really loses steam in the late-game, as you travel deep into the cave system beneath the open sea. Resources become scarcer down there, required upgrades to your vehicles to reach the final area are presented to you all at once and take a fair bit of time to acquire, and the final tasks of the game entail scouring every corner of the map to collect resources. It's a bit bloated and slows down an otherwise engaging 20-40 hour game.  At the same time, you may never see a fair chunk of the game world, as many resources are found in at least half a dozen biomes, and some of said biomes are more of an aesthetic addition than a vital location to visit. This is a double-edged sword, as it is rewarding to explore the world and see new and interesting landscapes and sea creatures; But also entirely missable if you're afraid of leaving the beaten path or only focus on the 'necessary' objectives of the game. There are a couple places in particular I visited only once and never returned to.  This review is rambly because I wanted to give some updated thoughts but there isn't really anything new to say that hasn't been said better already by others. Glad I revisited this one. Right now, the only things you can really do, is hunt for food and pick up metal and quartz to craft better oxygen tanks and items. So if you are looking to buy this game, it will be a great adventure game about learning more about your surroundings, but right now, it's more of an exploration game. It will have a lot more content when it is finished though. It is a lot of fun to explore, and the graphics are great and the game runs well despite being an early access game. Make no mistake, if you are afraid of water levels and/or ocean levels in video games, this will leave you unsettled. Some of the bigger, more vicious creatures of the sea are being added. Trust me, the only place where you feel safe being out of your sub, is when you are in a reef.  After a while, you can craft a mini submarine which you can explore the depths with. The game has a lot of content right now, but it does not have a save feature.  Overall, it's a great game in its current state, and I recommend picking it up in the Steam sale. The game can only get better from here...

So after 24 hours of gameplay I have decided to give my verdict on relics new venture on the DOW series. For all its flaws ( and there a few) I would give this game a thumbs up and recommend it. Overall the game isnt so bad, the graphics are stunning, the units for all factions are interesting and fun to use which you get to play with across a relatively alright campaign. The multiplayer is challenging and now has an anhilation mode which is very fun to play.   When it comes to the flaws there are a few that i couldnt help but pick up on. The first one which bugged me was Gabreil Angelos, for whatever reason they have decided to change the voice actor and I miss his booming, authotarian space marine chapter master, hammer swining motherfucker I have come to love from the first and second dawn of war games. The game has overalled alot of mechanics and now heavily leans on how well you can micro manage the abilities of each unit to really get the full use of them. it reminds me much of DOTA except you can have dozens of units and one big skirmish each with their own ability that you need to constantly focus on, especially in the PVP. The cover system as you know it is gone, replaced by these rather strange shield domes which become uselss if your attacked by a melle unit.   The campaign spans across 17 levels where you flip between the three factions which i disliked. im a big space marine fan boy and would have preferred to have a seperate campaign for all factions but the campaign itself was a fun experience if not very predictable. I also felt that there are not equal amount of missions for each faction and that they are all not the same length, so you could play a big mission with the Eldar that can take around 45 mins and then a quick space marine mission that lasts 20 then your straight back into the eldar again.   There may seem like a few bad points but the biggest thumbs up for me and this game is that its just plain FUN. I play video games because there challenging and fun and DOW 3 does that pretty well. The Ork scrap mechanic to upgrade units and build vehicles is pretty sweet and watching a whole army of eldar getting chewed up by twin Imperial Knight gattling guns was just seriously fucking cool.   Yes the game has dumbed down, yes it isnt as big as Dark Crusade or Soulstorm in terms of campaing and invading provinces and planets, yes they removed some good features from previous titles and your correct, it isnt the best DOW title. But its bloody fun to play.

ver1.01とver1.02の時点でノーマルED3種全クリしたのでレビューします。 6体目のキャラがクリア後も!マークが付いている方はomakeテキストを読みましょう。 本体をインストールしたフォルダに含まれています。  頒布後1週間以上経っているのでネタバレに考慮せず書きます。  良い点 ①今までの原作にないゲームシステム 黄昏シリーズの格ゲーで無理やり弾幕やパズルゲーをやってきた 萃～憑までのストーリーモードをより洗練させた感じのゲーム性です。 難易度が高いと感じる方が多いのは慣れていないので当然ですね。 攻略のコツとしてはタイミングよく攻撃を振って 目押しで弾消ししながら殴るのが基本になりますが、 そういったゲーム性故にモーションに癖があるキャラは慣れるまで大変かもしれません。 スペルカードによっては安定したパターン化も可能なので そういう攻略のアプローチ感は整数作品に近いです。 格ゲーで色んなキャラをトレモで弄って楽しめるタイプの方は長く楽しめるかと思います。  ②遂に出た新キャラとこれまでスポットが当たらなかった既存キャラ達の活躍 あの饕餮が遂にお披露目です、 掲示板やイラスト投稿サイトで生まれた数々のイマジナリー饕餮に黙祷・・・。 あとは10年や20年近く公式でスポットが当たらなかったキャラ達が活躍します。 心綺楼辺りから匂わせていた村紗の血の池地獄の伏線に触れたり、 まさかのフランドールや依神姉妹が登場したりと東方の畑の人間なら狂喜狂乱する事間違いなしです。 個人的にフランと霊夢の掛け合いは、 かつて紅魔EXを数百回もリトライしてクリアした身としてはグッと来る物がありました。  ③発売されたという事 「何を言っているんだ？」と思う方も多いでしょうがこれは重要な事です。 智礼奇伝や酔蝶華といった最近の書籍作品が地獄関連のネタにようやく触れる事が可能になります。 メタ的な観点になりますが今作が延期されて出ない間は幻想郷の時が止まっていた可能性があったのです。 頒布された事によりリアル永夜返しが決まり、 ようやく各メディアで鬼形獣キャラにもスポットが当たると思います。  良くない点 ①ボリューム不足 EDを見るとわかるのですが、 凄まじい少人数で今作は作られています。 それでも年単位で延期した割に過去の黄昏作品と比較して、 ゲームのボリュームが少ないのは事実ではあります。 タイムアタックや縛り攻略といった古典的なアーケード作品を楽しむ様なプレイングが出来る人はまだしも 一度クリア出来れば良いといったスタンスの方は様子を見るのもありかと思います。 というのも、黄昏作品は頒布後に追加コンテンツを実装する事も多かったからです。  ②システムが不親切 キャラ毎の技やキャンセルルートは実際に使って探らないといけないという 昔のアーケード作品さながらの現状です。 後は弾消しや弾抜けが不可能な弾幕の中には被弾して見ないとわからない 初見殺し的なのも存在します。 こういった要素をストレスかやりこみ要素どちらかに受け取るかはプレイヤー次第ですが、 せめて全キャラにトレーニングモードの様な物があれば完全に賛同出来た気がします。  以上です、 個人的には今作のシステムでスマブラみたいなオンラインPvPが出来たら嬉しいと思っています。 憑依華PC版の公式サーバーが停止している現状なので、 かなり手間がかかるかと思いますがそういった物が出てくれたらなと勝手に期待しています。

I had the game on GamePass and I liked it so much I wanted to show 343 support and bought the game on Steam (cuz tbh, I only paid $1.00 for 3 months of game pass lol).  As a person who has played every Halo game, and routinely played through the entire saga before each new release, with friends or alone on heroic and legendary. I really enjoyed this one for many reasons. It is flawed in a few ways but the good parts make up for it.  Stuff I liked:  - combat can be pretty intense and satisfying  - enemy chatter is awesome, and I think mark meer plays the jackals (commander shephard)  - characters and the relationships between them, including their arcs  - grapple hook (make sure you upgrade it ASAP, cuz you can literally be spider-chief and straight up walls)  - ammo and weapons are everywhere and varied well  - exploring the map to find the upgrades, skulls, easter eggs, audio logs etc  Stuff I'm kinda on the fence with:  - Open world map is pretty empty and it slows the pacing down a bit, however, it also lays the framework for the devs to expand upon with DLC or future releases and so I find it acceptable, so long as it doesn't follow Ubisoft's example.  - The game has some 'bosses' but I think they could do a better job with their mechanics. Still it was a nice inclusion, and if they improve it in DLC or future titles, then I think it's an alright direction for the game.  Stuff I didn't like:  - TAA, holy cow, it's so blurry unless I'm playing on my 4k TV or unless I supersample it to oblivion. As awesome as the game is, a lot of the cinematic moments (not talking about the cutscenes but just gameplay), kind of get soured because of that  - Vehicle controls are a bit silly for some vehicles and they get stuck a lot because the game doesn't have destruction physics. So yeah, your tank will get defeated by a 3 foot tree.  - Would have been nice to see a few more Spartans in the story, or characters from the other games. Some show up in audio logs, but that's about it.   I have plenty minor praises and complaints as well, but generally more to praise than hate, and so I'd say this game is a solid 86/100. If you have some disposable income, it wouldn't be wasted on this game.

Pros: + unique premise + pre-rendered scenes still look good  Cons: - real-time rendered characters do not look good anymore - annoyingly voiced dialogue (English) - serious holes in plot for a story-driven game  Picked up this game on Steam sale on the promise of a good story and reasonable puzzles. I was disappointed. While the game is one of the few to actually present an original premise (so many are derivatives of a “you are a quiet antihero looking for vengeance”) the entirety of the plot is really presented in the first few minutes of the game. Character development takes place through a series of phone calls which are supposed to show the personal growth of the main character through the use of a sub-plot, but really have no connection to the main events of the game, nor do they server to connect you to the hero. It is also unfortunate that the English voice-acting (can’t speak for other language tracks) is overdone, so that you find yourself skipping dialogue lines as quickly as you can read them, rather than listen to the hammy delivery. In spite of this, I could still have lived with the story, were it not for a number of serious troubles with the plot (see spoiler section to read my beefs). 間違いなく良いゲームではあるんですが、それを相殺しさらにマイナス方向へ持って行くレベルのバグが多いです。  [h1]バグ周りについて[/h1]  どんなゲームなのかはトレーラーや各種ムービーを見ればなんとなくわかるので、このレビューでは主に気になるバグ等をまとめていきます。  [b]・ロードの度に畑(自動化施設含む)がバグる[/b]  読み込み時に毎回畑に植えた種が消失します。 その上、土を設置しなおさないと新たに種が植えられないバグも同時に発生します。 自動化施設は中身を取り出し、設置しなおしたりしないと再び稼働しないバグも発生します。 非常に面倒な上、序盤は植えたものの確定ロストは結構痛いです。  [b]・オブジェクトの設置がバグる[/b]  オブジェクト配置時に置けてないのに置けている判定になったり、 判定のみ出現し現物が存在しないことになったり、 重なって配置されてしまったりすることが結構頻発します。  [b]・各種作業台インベントリ内のアイテム消失[/b]  ロードを挟むと作業台内のアイテムが消失することがあります。 自動建築アームのインベントリは特にバグりやすく、間違えてインベントリにアイテムを入れたままアームを撤去すると、確定で内部のアイテムがロストします。  [b]・NPCがバグる[/b]  このゲームはNPCをどんどん仲間にし、それらに指示を出して製造を効率化したり、イベントを進めたりするゲームです。 しかし、エリアによってはNPCの挙動がバグり、【その場で周り続ける】【壁に埋まる】【消える】等のバグが発生します。 その間は指示された行動は一切せず、その状態で話しかけるとそのNPCが増殖するバグも同時発生します。 増殖したキャラはその後ずっと増殖したままかつ、同名別NPCとして指示まで出来てしまいます。  非常に細かい建築が売りのゲームですが、凝った建築や装飾をするとそれが原因でNPCがスタックします。 ちょっとした段差や普通の階段でもスタックするので、結局地べたに簡素かつ平坦な部屋(入口極大)を作ることになり、せっかく細かく調整できる建築も意味を成しません。  NPC周りのバグは本当に多く、現在結局自分ひとりでクラフトや建築等をしています。 このゲームのシステムが全く生かせない状況で地道に進めてはおりますが、現状面倒臭さが面白さ楽しさを上回ってきてしまっています。  [b]・時間が止まる[/b]  ゲーム内時間は比較的早く進んでいき、夜になったら疲労で寝なければいけないシステムです。 しかし、原因は分かりませんが突然時間が止まるようになってしまいました。 研究というシステムがあり、研究中の時間加速というシステムを無理やり使って時間を進めつつゲームを進行していますが、 割とこちらも面倒な状況になってしまっています。  このゲームを始めた当初は物凄く楽しめていましたし、次のエリアが気になったり、ストーリーやキャラクエストでワクワクしていましたが、現状バグが多くなりすぎて楽しむより面倒臭いという感情が上回ってきてしまっている状況です。 今のところは本当にバグだらけなので、しばらく寝かせる方が良いかもしれません。 バグが減るという保証もありませんが…。  一応完全に詰むまでやってみるつもりではありますが、モチベが続くかどうか…。
